We evaluate our approach across diverse environments and benchmarks: routed ensembles improve average performance by 4.3% over baselines for online environments from Meta-World and MO-Gymnasium, and kernel surrogate attribution improves correlation with leave-one-out analysis over existing baselines by 50%. When applied to trajectory selection, kernel-based attribution yields a 27% improvement in reward over baseline attribution methods.

papers.title: Parametrically Enhanced Ergotropy and Charging Power in a Three-Mode Bosonic Quantum Battery
papers.abstract: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that potentially serve as fuel for other quantum devices by receiving and supplying energy. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to enhance ergotropy and charging power of quantum Battery in the system under consideration through squeezed light. Moreover, The system comprises a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary cavity acting as a mediator, and an energy--storage battery cavity. Quantum nonreciprocity and directional energy flow are established via destructive quantum interference between the direct coupling path and the loss--engineered indirect path. A degenerate optical parametric amplifier integrated into the charger cavity acts as an active, phase--sensitive energy source that injects two--photon quantum excitations and anomalous correlations. Using a strictly open--quantum--system framework derived directly from the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the full expectation--value dynamics and stationary states. We show that active parametric driving drastically increases the stored energy and peak charging power while maintaining nonreciprocal energy trapping in the battery. We achieve a multi-order-of-magnitude boost in the battery's stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We also analyze the effects of pure dephasing on the charging power, ergotropy, and extractable work quality.. Although two--photon pumping introduces photon--number fluctuations that slightly lower the fractional ergotropy ratio ${\cal W}_{\rm B}/{\cal E}_{\rm B}$, the absolute extractable work remains substantially elevated compared to unassisted configurations.

papers.title: Decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification for quantum low-density parity-check codes
papers.abstract: Real-time decoding is a fundamental necessity for building fault-tolerant quantum computers. In this work, we introduce decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification (DAWG), an ensemble based approach that combines Tanner graph sparsification with ensembling belief-propagation (BP) decoders. The DAWG decoder runs BP decoders over the full detector error model Tanner graph for certain iterations to then transfer the posteriors to a sparsified graph in which additional rounds of BP are run. Each of the decoders in the ensemble uses a different transfer matrix to map the posterior information to the sparsified graph. We use the serial schedule for the minimum-sum BP decoders and, thus, employ Vibe decoding ideas by randomizing the schedules of each of them. The performance of the DAWG decoder is then numerically studied for bivariate bicycle codes and superdense color code circuits to be compared with other state-of-the-art decoding approaches. Importantly, the DAWG decoder shows a similar performance to Relay belief-propagation and Vibe decoding when combined with an order-$0$ Localized Statistics Decoding (LSD-$0$) post-processor. Crucially, the post-processor is called an order of magnitude less times than for Vibe with the same ensemble size, indicating that the introduced latency tail will be minimal. Furthermore, LSD-$0$ operates on a sparsified decoding graph of a fraction of the size of the full detector error model, which simplifies the resources required by specialized hardware to support it. Overall, the DAWG+LSD-$0$ decoder represents a viable low-cost BP-based decoding algorithm for quantum error correction codes.

papers.title: Preference-Guided Cooperation in Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning (MOMARL) addresses agent coordination and objective trade-offs simultaneously while optimising overall system performance. Existing work tends to treat multi-agent cooperation and multi-objective optimisation as largely independent components of a learning problem, which amounts to an exorbitant complexity except in trivial cases. We study here whether the structure provided by multiple objectives can itself be exploited to facilitate cooperation, rather than being treated as an additional optimisation challenge. We formulate MOMARL at both the team and individual levels and introduce objective-wise counterfactual credit assignment to evaluate each agent's contribution across the team objectives. We propose Meta-Gradient Informed Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MIRL), with static (MIRL-S) and dynamic (MIRL-D) variants. By incorporating meta-gradient information, MIRL enables agents to learn how to prioritise objectives individually while collectively optimising the system-level objective, allowing the multi-objective structure to directly guide cooperation. Experiments on a multi-objective multiple particle environment show that our methods improve Pareto-front quality over baselines, with the dynamic variant achieving the strongest performance.

papers.title: Local Broadband Gigahertz Spectroscopy via SQUID-on-Tip DC Readout
papers.abstract: Superconducting microwave circuits are shaped by their local electromagnetic environment, yet standard microwave measurements do not resolve the local fields and device features that govern their behavior. Here, we combine microwave spectroscopy, nanoscale magnetic sensing, and topographic imaging in a single tapping-mode SQUID-on-tip microscope. The nonlinear Josephson response converts local GHz excitations into Shapiro steps, enabling quantitative measurements of microwave frequency signals and their excitation strength using only DC readout. Applied to a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator, local spectroscopy reproduces the power-dependent resonance and nonlinear bifurcation observed in microwave transmission measurements. Spatially resolved measurements map the microwave response while simultaneously recording topography and static magnetic features, including vortices and Meissner screening currents. Electromagnetic simulations reveal how coupling through the superconducting probe leads limits spatial resolution and guides localized detector designs. Together, these capabilities establish a platform for correlating microwave circuit dynamics with the local structural and magnetic environment of superconducting devices.

papers.title: Fuji: The Shape, Composition, and Spread of Demand Bursts on Robinhood Chain
papers.abstract: Demand on blockchain-based marketplaces arrives in bursts and at a high rate. On these platforms the data are completely visible, which makes it feasible to compare the bursty demand against the usual load. The congestion manifests as an increased demand for gas, the primary resource a blockchain sells. Existing studies consider how to price the gas. The demand itself, and what it is made of during bursts, has not been measured. We measure it on Robinhood Chain, a layer-2 blockchain that quickly became a venue for trading tokenized equities and memecoins. We collected the data from every block of its first three active months and more than 50 million Uniswap swaps that occurred during bursty periods. We find that a burst trades about as many pools as a quiet period, mostly different ones, and trades them harder, on top of elevated demand that accumulated for hours. With the bursts aligned on their peaks, the median peak is 2.5 times the usual load. Both the rise and the fall of the demand are described by the sum of two exponential functions with different timescales, a slow one of hours and a fast one of minutes. Against a matched quiet period, a burst has 1.05 times the pools, 1.40 times the trades, and 1.21 times the senders. We use two models to explain the arrival of bursts: externally triggered cascades and self-excitation. The former fits the data relatively better. Inside a burst, the entry of each trader into a pool is followed for about 24 seconds by more entries than the existing traders predict. Whether this is because of imitation or because of a shared signal is left open.

papers.title: From skew Combinatorial Nullstellensatz to sharp Ax-Katz congruences and zero counts
papers.abstract: We give a unified account of zero counting in finite-field polynomial rings with commuting variables twisted by a common automorphism. A decomposition into fixed-field slices connects skew evaluation with ordinary polynomial evaluation. First, we derive a slice coefficient formula from the skew Combinatorial Nullstellensatz and use it to deduce skew Chevalley-Warning, including the sufficient condition $n>h\sum_i d_i$. Next, classical Ax-Katz gives the corrected integer congruence $Q^{\max\{0,\lceil(n-h\sum_i d_i)/D\rceil\}}\mid N+(M-1)δ$. We construct homogeneous examples proving optimality for every positive degree table and every number of variables. We also establish a sharp lower bound with a prescribed zero, an input-sensitive coefficient-filtration refinement, and transfers of known bounds for nonlinear zero sets. Detailed calculations explain the origin correction, incomplete norm blocks, and the distinction between characteristic-$p$ summation and higher integer divisibility. Existing geometric, interpolation, and counting theorems are explicitly attributed.

papers.title: LUCID: Local Understanding of Covariate Importance with Conditional Density Estimation
papers.abstract: Computing local-level variable importance (VI) is critical for understanding machine learning models. Local permutation-based VI metrics offer a simple yet powerful approach, measuring how much a model's output changes when perturbing its inputs. However, existing perturbation strategies often ignore feature dependence or account for it only through restricted approximations. Perturbing a feature without fully respecting this dependence can generate unrealistic counterfactuals, thereby evaluating the model in regions unsupported by the observed data distribution. We address this gap by introducing a new model-agnostic local VI metric and estimator, Local Understanding of Covariate Importance with conditional Density estimation (LUCID). LUCID perturbs features of interest using plausible values drawn from the full conditional distribution given the remaining observed features. We establish theoretical connections between LUCID and existing VI measures, and provide an estimator with convergence guarantees and uncertainty quantification. Finally, we demonstrate LUCID's stable performance and practical utility across simulated and real-world examples.

papers.title: Graph Neural Network for Wide-Area 6DoF Ambisonic Rendering
papers.abstract: Wide-area 6DoF rendering from sparse Ambisonic recordings is commonly addressed by interpolating parametric spatial descriptors rather than the waveforms themselves. This preserves the fidelity of a nearby measured signal and avoids phase artifacts caused by mixing distant arrays. However, existing DirAC-based approaches rely on geometric interpolation weights that do not depend on the acoustic scene observed by the microphones. We propose a lightweight Graph Neural Network (GNN) that refines only this interpolation stage. The known Ambisonic arrays and the query position are represented as a graph whose nodes contain local DirAC features and whose edges encode relative distance and directional relations. The network predicts positive query-conditioned weights over the measured arrays, while the target energy, diffuseness, and direction of arrival are reconstructed by an analytical DirAC layer. Experiments on unseen rooms, unseen speech signals, and unseen array configurations show that the proposed weighting improves energy reconstruction and radiation-pattern similarity with respect to baseline interpolation.

papers.title: Yang-Mills-Higgs Limits of Reflexive Higgs Sheaves
papers.abstract: For stable Higgs bundles, Hermitian-Einstein metrics can be obtained as limits of the Yang-Mills-Higgs (Y-M-H) flow. We study the algebraic structure of subsequential limits of this flow for reflexive Higgs sheaves over compact Kähler manifolds, without assuming stability. We prove that the limiting reflexive Higgs sheaf is isomorphic to the double dual of the graded sheaf associated with the Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration of the initial sheaf.

papers.title: SEMA-Auto: Sighted and Efficient Multi-Turn Attack with Autonomy
papers.abstract: Existing jailbreak attackers fall into two classes: static planners fix their single- or multi-turn adversarial plans in advance, remaining simple but losing sight of the victim's replies, wasting turns and limiting transferability; interactive generators read each victim reply to generate the next-turn attack but require in-loop evaluators for success signals or hints, incurring substantial costs and inflated performance. Bridging this gap, we propose SEMA-Auto, a sighted and efficient multi-turn attacker with autonomy, interacting with the victim model and terminating the session by itself upon success. To stabilize its behaviors and boost its capabilities, SEMA-Auto is trained in two stages. Synthetic bootstrap tuning installs the notion of attack targets and conforming decisions by fine-tuning the base model with bootstrapped trajectories. Decision-supervised reinforcement learning then optimizes two objectives jointly yet separately, reinforcing the attack with higher jailbreak reward while supervising the decision at each turn against an absolute target. Our method achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) attack success rates (ASR) across multiple datasets, victims, and judges, outperforming all static and interactive baselines, within almost the fewest turns, demonstrating both effectiveness and efficiency. For example, SEMA-Auto performs a $76.0\%$ ASR@1 within an average of $3.0$ turns against DeepSeek-V4-Flash on AdvBench, while the best static baseline is $54.8\%$ with fixed $7$ turns and the best interactive baseline is $43.8\%$ in $3.7$ turns. Against safety-hardened frontier models, GPT-oss-120B, GPT-5.4, Claude-Haiku-4.5, and GPT-6-Astra, our counter-trained attacker achieves an average $59.6\%$ ASR@1 on HarmBench, $13.8\%$ over prior SOTA. Our code is available at: https://github.com/microsoft/SEMA

papers.title: The Weyl Problem for Planar CBB$(-1)$ Surfaces in Hyperbolic $3$-Space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Weyl problem for noncompact convex surfaces in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$. We prove that any planar CBB$(-1)$ surface with countably many ends can be isometrically embedded as the boundary of a closed convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{H}^3$ such that each connected component of the ideal boundary of $X$ is either a round disk or a single point. By known rigidity results, such an embedding is unique up to isometries of $\mathbb{H}^3$. Moreover, we show that the assumption of countably many ends can be dropped if Koebe's circle domain conjecture holds.

papers.title: Minimum Contagious Sets in Trees with Degree-Proportional Thresholds
papers.abstract: We investigate how large the minimum size of a contagious set can be among trees of a fixed order. Given a graph $G$ and $ρ\in[0,1]$, an inactive vertex $u$ becomes active when at least $\lceil{ρd_G(u)\rceil}$ of its neighbors are active. An initial set of active vertices is contagious if the process eventually activates every vertex. We obtain exact values for the minimum size of a contagious set in perfect $d$-ary trees. We then determine the exact maximum of this minimum size over all trees of order $n$. We establish this result by bounding the number of pairwise disjoint resistant sets, each of which must intersect every contagious set, and constructing trees that attain the resulting bounds. Finally, by bounding the change in the minimum size of a contagious set under a leaf exchange, we show that, for $0<ρ\leq1$ and $n\geq2$, every integer between $1$ and this maximum occurs as the minimum size of a contagious set in a tree of order $n$.

papers.title: Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (DRE): A Radiometric Measure of Electric Light Source Efficiency
papers.abstract: Photopic luminous efficacy (lm/W) weights optical power strictly against human eye sensitivity V (lambda), creating a systemic metrological penalty for electric light sources engineered with broad spectral output in the ultraviolet (280-380 nm) or infrared (780-4000 nm) bands. Similarly, metrics evaluating chromaticity, color quality, or melanopic pathways assess photoreceptor responses strictly within the visual band, offering no measure of broad-spectrum physical radiant power conversion. To resolve this limitation, we introduce Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (eta_DRE), a radiometric framework that evaluates how efficiently an electric light source converts electrical power into an optical spectrum matching natural terrestrial daylight across domain Omega = [280 nm, 4000 nm]. The framework factorizes performance into primary physical quantities: domain-restricted Wall-Plug Efficiency (eta_wall [W_optical/W_elec]), measuring unweighted electrical-to-optical conversion, and Daylight Spectral Fidelity (eta_spec [unitless, 0-1]), quantifying geometric shape match to the ASTM G173 AM1.5G solar reference via total variation distance (1 - TVD). Multiplying total optical power by spectral fidelity yields the absolute Daylight-Referenced Output Power (P_dr [W]), establishing a direct physical flux quantity for lighting specification. Dividing by electrical drive power gives the summary metric Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (eta_DRE = eta_wall * eta_spec [W/W_elec]), measuring net reference-conforming radiant output per electrical Watt consumed. The mathematical architecture is reference-agnostic, domain-extensible, and maintains provable lower-bound monotonicity for eta_wall and eta_DRE under spectral truncation. Open-source reference software is provided to facilitate deployment and standardized rating of broad-spectrum light sources.

papers.title: Correspondence Is Not Transfer: A Pairing-Controlled Study of Clinical Audio-Metadata Alignment
papers.abstract: Clinical audio models are often trained by aligning recordings with participant metadata or text derived from it. This metadata is rarely a clean disease signal, since a single profile also contains symptoms, age, sex, missing responses, and recruitment information. We examine what alignment adds to frozen audio features by varying only the audio-meta data pairing. We keep the audio backbones fixed and train only a projector under correct pairing and three shuffled conditions that progressively preserve the disease label and recorded sex. We then evaluate each projector on profile retrieval, attribute probing, and disease classification on covariate-matched test sets. On UKCOVID, correct pairing clearly improves retrieval and makes sex easier to decode, confirming that the pairing manipulation works. Most of the sex-probe gap disappears when the control also preserves recorded sex, while a small retrieval gap remains. Matched disease AUROC differences are small, and every interval includes zero, so modest benefits or harms are not ruled out. The same pattern appears when we rerun the frozen pipeline on CODA TB, Cambridge COVID-19 Sounds, and Coswara, where retrieval and sex-probe contrasts are consistently positive but disease contrasts are not. We find no consistent evidence that better profile correspondence translates into better disease prediction and suggest reporting these outcomes separately.

papers.title: Charge-Dependent Coordination and Redox Energetics of Actinide Fluoride Complexes in Molten Salts
papers.abstract: Redox control in molten fluoride salt reactors determines actinide solubility and corrosion of structural alloys, but the role of local fluoride coordination in this control remains poorly understood. We use density functional theory with explicit LiF microsolvation to study the coordination chemistry, intrinsic redox energetics, and fluoride-exchange kinetics of Th(IV), U(IV), and U(III) fluoride complexes. The coordination response to solvation primarily follows the formal charge of the complex rather than the actinide at its center: we find that cationic and neutral complexes gain fluoride ligands, most anionic complexes keep their coordination number, and $4-$ complexes lose fluoride. Coordination number then strongly controls the intrinsic U(IV)/U(III) reduction energy. From CN 4 to CN 7, this energy rises by up to $11$ eV and changes sign; a continuum-solvation estimate opposes this trend and therefore establishes the intrinsic value as an upper bound. Fluoride exchange barriers are low, so redox partners of different charge do not keep the same coordination numbers in solvated clusters. Finally, above a threshold between CN 5 and CN 6, single-reference DFT converges to a ligand-reduced U(III) state inconsistent with formal $5f^3$ occupation, however the physical nature of this is still unresolved. Therefore, local coordination is a primary variable in the prediction of redox behavior in molten actinide-fluoride salts.

papers.title: Model Selection for Off-Policy Evaluation via Pairwise Bellman Validation
papers.abstract: Model selection and hyperparameter tuning pose a central challenge in off-policy evaluation (OPE) because errors of fitted Q-functions and occupancy-ratio estimates cannot be directly evaluated from held-out transitions. Bellman-residual and minimax validation methods often require auxiliary regressions or optimization over separate critic classes, adding computational and tuning costs. We introduce pairwise Bellman validation (PBV), a tuning-free minimax procedure for selecting among finite classes of fitted Q-functions and occupancy-ratio estimators using held-out transitions. PBV constructs critics from pairwise candidate differences, requiring only finitely many empirical moment calculations without auxiliary validation models or separate critic optimization. We establish finite-sample oracle inequalities relative to the best available candidate, even under candidate-class misspecification. Our key insight is that Q-function errors and log ratios between candidate and true occupancy ratios provide oracle critics whose Bellman and adjoint Bellman moments control estimation error. Pairwise candidate differences approximate these unknown critics, while penalties account for comparator approximation error. For Q-function selection, we first develop unweighted PBV, which evaluates pairwise Bellman moments under the offline distribution and admits oracle guarantees under a pairwise coercivity condition relating the offline distribution to the target-policy dynamics. We then develop target-aligned PBV (TA-PBV), which uses marginalized importance weighting to provide error control without pairwise coercivity. For occupancy-ratio selection, we develop adjoint PBV (A-PBV), which evaluates adjoint Bellman moments against log-ratio critics. On Hopper and Deep OPE, unweighted PBV performs competitively, while target-occupancy weighting can improve performance in settings with controlled overlap.

papers.title: Heavy Heisenberg Algebras, Zero Modes and Modularity
papers.abstract: It is known due to a result of Miyamoto that zero mode correlators of weight $1$ vectors of vertex operator algebras are quasi-modular forms, and that their generating series are Jacobi forms. In this article we generalize this to higher weight vectors. We consider weight 2 vectors that generate what we call heavy Heisenberg algebras. We prove that their zero mode correlators are a specific type of quasi-modular forms. As a consequence, they too can be summed up into a generating series with Jacobi-like modular transformation properties. As an application of our results, we sketch an argument that gives the asymptotic behavior of the dimensions of states of our VOAs.

papers.title: E0.5: From Reconstructive to Future-Predictive 3D Foundations for Robotic World-Action Modeling
papers.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) offer a promising framework for embodied intelligence, yet mainstream approaches remain centered on video foundation models or vision-language models. Even when geometric features extracted by 3D models such as VGGT are incorporated, they are typically passed into a video model or VLM that serves as the primary backbone, leaving 3D geometry as an auxiliary input or prediction target rather than the native foundation for world modeling. We present E0.5, a geometry-native world-action model built directly on 3D foundation models. E0.5 introduces two key innovations. First, it adopts a 3D foundation model as the primary backbone, making 3D geometry the native representation for both world modeling and action prediction. Second, it explicitly predicts future 3D states together with actions, enabling the model to capture geometric world dynamics beyond action-only modeling or future video prediction. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 first demonstrate the effectiveness of E0.5 without embodied-data pretraining, achieving success rates of 89.90\% and 50.09\% under clean and randomized settings, respectively. Building on these results, we further pretrain E0.5 on more than 160k robot trajectories from AgiBotWorld-Beta, jointly learning robot actions and future geometry within the pretrained 3D foundation. This embodied pretraining improves mean real-world manipulation success rates by approximately 15 and 7 percentage points on AgileX Piper and Zerith H1, respectively. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of geometry-native foundations to acquire robot interaction knowledge and transfer it to physical manipulation. E0.5 embodies this geometry-native approach as a member of the VWA family of world-action models.

papers.title: Large Excursions of Reflected Lévy Processes: Local Asymptotics
papers.abstract: This paper establishes uniform local large-deviation asymptotics for excursions of a Lévy process $X$ with negative drift $-β$ and $α$-locally regularly varying Lévy measure $ν$, reflected at its running infimum. Under the excursion measure $\underline n$, we first prove that the lifetime $ζ$ and height $\overlineε$ satisfy \begin{equation*} \underline{n}\big(ζ\in(t,t+δ] \big) \sim \underline{n}(\overlineε\in\big (βt,βt+βδ]\big) \sim\underline{n}(ζ)\cdotν\big((βt,βt+βδ]\big), \quad \mbox{as } t\to\infty, \end{equation*} uniformly in $δ\in[δ_0,\infty]$ for every $δ_0>0$. In contrast to the asymptotic equivalence of the corresponding tail events, fixed-width lifetime and height windows have asymptotically negligible relative overlap. Nevertheless, for any positive function $θ$ satisfying $|X_t+βt|/θ_t\to0$ in probability, \begin{equation*} \underline n\big( |\overlineε-βt| \leq θ_t \,\big|\, ζ\in (t,t+δ] \big) \sim \underline n\big( |ζ-t| \leq θ_t \,\big|\, \overlineε\in (βt,βt+βδ] \big) \to 1 . \end{equation*} For conditioning windows of sublinear width bounded away from zero, both conditional excursion laws converge under spatial rescaling to a single-jump process with deterministic jump size and random arrival time determined by the integrated excursion survival function. An additional time rescaling yields the same deterministic linear descent killed at zero. Finally, we identify the joint limiting distribution of the unscaled pre-terminal position and terminal overshoot, including continuous and discontinuous termination.

papers.title: ACTIVE: A Dynamic Pareto-Frontier-Based Unified Index for Dual-Vector Query
papers.abstract: Existing approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) methods generally assume that each entity has a single vector. In many real-world applications, however, an entity is associated with more than one vector, and queries may jointly consider two attributes. With different queries assigning different weights to each attribute, Pareto-frontier-based indices provide an effective solution for dual-vector retrieval by connecting to approximate nearest neighbors under all possible query preferences. However, existing Pareto-frontier-based approaches suffer from substantial inefficiencies in both index construction and dynamic updates, limiting their practical applicability. To address these issues, we propose ACTIVE, a dynamic Pareto-frontier-based DVQ index that supports efficient construction and updates while maintaining high retrieval performance under varying query preferences. It employs angle-constrained active-range computation and connectivity-loss-driven adaptive repair strategies to accelerate node insertion and deletion, respectively. Extensive experiments show that, at comparable (or slightly below) search accuracy, ACTIVE improves insertion throughput by $1.20$--$1.43\times$ over DEG, and deletion throughput by $1.64$--$2.06\times$ over neighbor-reconnection-based repair and by $22.64$--$39.51\times$ over reinsertion-based repair.

papers.title: A Stochastic Proximal-Gradient Method for Regularized Generally Constrained Continuous Optimization
papers.abstract: A stochastic proximal-gradient method is proposed and analyzed for solving regularized optimization problems subject to nonlinear equality constraints and nonnegativity bounds. The objective function's values and gradients are available only through inexact stochastic oracles. The method decomposes each trial step into one component that reduces linearized infeasibility and a second component that seeks optimality while preserving that reduction. Trial steps are accepted or rejected through a relaxed sufficient decrease condition subject to stochastic merit function evaluations. Without assuming unbiasedness of stochastic gradient estimates, it is proved under reasonable assumptions that the method reaches an $ε$-KKT point within $O(ε^{-2})$ iterations with high probability. This guarantee further implies almost-sure termination in finitely many iterations and an $O(ε^{-2})$ bound on the expected iteration complexity.

papers.title: CLOSURE: Cross-Channel Closure for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Multivariate time series produced by industrial installations and server clusters are under continuous monitoring, and anomaly detection is the first line of defense before a local fault escalates into a system-wide failure. In the absence of labels, the dominant paradigm trains a reconstruction model on normal data and scores the residual to reach a verdict. Recent work has steadily enriched the expressiveness of the recovery map through Transformers, diffusion models, and cross-scale associations. A residual, however, only certifies that an observation can be recovered; it does not certify that the variables still explain one another as they do under normal operation. A coordinated yet unfamiliar operating transition inflates the residual without breaking any relationship, whereas a sensor drifting away from its peers may leave the residual silent. Methods that fold inter-variable dependencies into the reconstruction objective inherit this ambiguity, because their relational evidence is ultimately supervised by the same recovery loss. We therefore propose CLOSURE, which evaluates recoverability and cross-channel consistency as two normal-data prediction tasks learned in separation. The recoverability task is solved by a diffusion reconstructor conditioned on a discrete memory of normal temporal bases. The consistency task is solved by a relation-closure operator that predicts every channel exclusively from the others, where the target's own trajectory is withheld and sparse signed gates decide which peers are actually used. The two scores are reconciled only through calibration on normal data. Extensive experiments show that CLOSURE consistently outperforms recent reconstruction-, frequency-, and topology-based detectors on public benchmark streams, confirming the value of examining consistency alongside recoverability.

papers.title: On explicit formulas for Grassmannian polylogarithms and Gelfand-MacPherson forms
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Goncharov by showing that his Grassmannian $n$-logarithm can be recovered by integrating the Borel invariant form on the symmetric space $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(\mathbf{C})/\mathrm{SU}(n)$ over a naturally defined ideal simplex. As corollaries, we recover the finiteness of primitive canonical integrals of Brown and the evaluation for wheel graphs of Brown and Schnetz. We also compute explicitly the Gelfand-MacPherson forms for powers of the first Pontryagin class and give a general integral formula for the Gelfand-MacPherson forms associated to each component of the Pontryagin character.

papers.title: A Sphericity Filter for Space-Filling Designs in Nondeterministic Experiments
papers.abstract: Space-filling designs support flexible modeling in noisy multi-response experiments, but an individual design can give poor precision for low-order effects. We use a low-order working model to identify effects whose estimation precision we seek to protect, while allowing a more complex final response model. The filter selects one complete design from a candidate pool by minimizing a geometric loss divided by sphericity, without exchanging or altering its points. Sphericity measures the balance of the working-model confidence ellipsoid's principal-axis variances, independently of its volume. In a working-model basis orthonormal over the prediction region, sphericity is the shape factor of the I-criterion, which measures average prediction variance. In cube studies with quadratic least-squares and Gaussian-process fits, this target filter gives modest average prediction gains over the geometrically best candidate at small geometric cost. Gains in working-model precision are largest near saturation: in a four-factor example, worst-decile prediction standard error falls by about a quarter relative to the geometrically best candidate. In constrained mixtures, raw coefficient-based filtering and A-optimality can emphasize extrapolated Scheffe coefficients and yield poor regional prediction precision. Target filtering improves regional working-model precision in most settings studied, mirroring the advantage of I- over A-optimality for highly constrained mixture designs.

papers.title: Classical traversability of a carbon BTZ wormhole
papers.abstract: We investigate the classical traversability of an analogue spatial wormhole geometry realized on a two-dimensional curved carbon membrane. The background is obtained by implementing a reflection-symmetric doubling technique on the exterior spatial sector of a non-rotating Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli black hole, effectively replacing the event horizon with a smooth traversable throat. Within this framework, massless Dirac quasiparticles propagate as spinorial light rays whose kinematics are governed exclusively by the metric curvature, forcing them to track the null geodesics of the ultrastatic spacetime. By evaluating the exact geodesic equations, we demonstrate that classical traversability is dictated by a sharp binary threshold in the conserved angular momentum, where the minimum throat radius acts as a centrifugal potential barrier that separates traversing paths from reflecting ones. We show that near-critical trajectories experience a logarithmic divergence in their angular evolution, causing the quasiparticles to execute multiple spatial windings around the throat before escaping. These classical ray-tracing configurations establish the necessary geometric backbones for future mesoscopic investigations.

papers.title: The size of an overtwisted disk
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of size for an overtwisted disk, defined in terms of the Shelukhin-Hofer energy required to stabilise Legendrians in its vicinity. We compute this size for the standard $3$-dimensional overtwisted disk, which we use to prove that certain explicit product hyperdisks in higher-dimensional contact manifolds are overtwisted (and their overtwisted size can be computed explicitly as well). We then use the overtwisted size to establish a number of quantitative results on contact flexibility. Concretely, we (1) obtain quantitative $h$--principles for Legendrians in the complement of an overtwisted disk, (2) construct overtwisted-at-infinity contact manifolds whose Legendrian Shelukhin-Hofer metric vanishes, (3) estimate overtwisted size under contact products and under products with Liouville manifolds, and (4) derive action bounds for contractible Reeb orbits in closed overtwisted contact manifolds.

papers.title: VidEdit3D: Flexible 3D Gaussian Editing with Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in text-guided 3D editing, particularly with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), have shown promise but still lag behind the flexibility of 2D editing tools. Existing methods face a critical trade-off between preserving multi-view consistency and allowing structural modifications. Image-based editors can also struggle to apply the intended edit to objects viewed from unusual angles. To address these limitations, we introduce VidEdit3D, a framework that reformulates 3D scene editing as a trajectory-based video editing task. By drawing a parallel between camera movement in static 3D scenes and temporal dynamics in video, we leverage the robust spatiotemporal priors of pre-trained Video Diffusion Models (VDMs) to encourage semantic and structural coherence across views. Specifically, we propose Trajectory-Guided Rendering (TGR) to select informative keyframes and construct smooth video clips aligned with VDM input requirements. To propagate edits from an anchor view to these clips, we develop Flow-Aligned Video Editing (FAVE), a training-free framework incorporating an Editing Consistency Guidance (ECG) mechanism. ECG contrasts source and edited image conditions at a shared latent state, using scheduled source-image amplification to strengthen adherence to the edited reference while maintaining original scene context. Finally, we introduce Region-Selective 3DGS Refinement (RS-GS) to strictly confine geometric and appearance updates to target primitives, reducing background attribute leakage. Experiments demonstrate stronger instruction alignment and better multi-view consistency than the baselines.

papers.title: EEGaze: Multimodal Attention Prediction in Visual Search via EEG-Based Saliency Refinement
papers.abstract: Visual search is ubiquitous in daily life, from locating keys in a messy apartment to finding a tool in a cluttered workshop or an application icon on a desktop screen. While visual attention is to a large extent driven by image content, research in psychology indicates that user cognitive states have a significant influence on attention allocation. A promising way to access information about cognitive states is via Electroencephalography (EEG) recordings. Despite this potential, previous works in computational attention modeling have largely disregarded EEG, and related studies in psychology operate with abstract, simplistic stimuli, or even artificially guided search procedures. We bridge this gap with two contributions. First, we present EEGaze 140, the largest publicly available multimodal dataset of free visual search with realistic stimuli. The dataset contains synchronized EEG and eye tracking recordings from 36 participants across 140 naturalistic scenes, covering two scenarios: searching for desktop icons and finding tools in cluttered workshop scenes. Second, we introduce EEGazeNet, the first method for human attention prediction in visual search that integrates EEG signals. Our approach consists of a EEG guided refinement stage that adapts the output of a state of the art saliency prediction method to the user current cognitive state. In comprehensive evaluations on EEGaze 140, we show that EEGazeNet consistently outperforms all baselines and ablation conditions.

papers.title: Competing coherence geometries in positive maps: positivity hierarchies, atomicity, and optimal entanglement witnesses
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of positive maps on qudits whose Choi operators combine two competing coherence patterns: independent exchange couplings and a collective set of diagonal couplings. For every mixed member of the family, we derive exact conditions for positivity, complete positivity, and all intermediate levels of k-positivity, and we determine the complete phase structure of decomposability and atomicity. The higher-positivity thresholds depend on the channel multiplicities, whereas the exact decomposability boundary is universal in scale-free coordinates. Its proof combines an explicit positive-plus-copositive decomposition with a matching family of positive-partial-transpose (PPT) states. The latter form PPT edge states whose detection region is an ellipse, or a disk after collective rescaling. An embedded-qutrit certificate shows that indecomposability and atomicity coincide throughout the mixed family. In contrast, the purely collective endpoint is decomposable over its entire positive interval. Finally, at maximal coherence, an explicit positive subtraction produces an atomic optimal entanglement witness with the spanning property and a strictly larger PPT- detection set. The study thus provides an exactly solvable setting in which k-positivity, decomposability, atomicity, PPT-edge-state geometry, and witness optimality can be compared in arbitrary local dimension.

papers.title: Entropic hypocoercivity via the Polchinski flow: an application to the lattice sine-Gordon model
papers.abstract: We develop a multiscale criterion for exponential decay of relative entropy in the canonical stochastic quantization of lattice field theories, the underdamped Langevin dynamics of the field and its momentum. For smooth bounded perturbations of Gaussian fields, the criterion requires the uniform operator-norm bound on the smoothed interaction Hessian along the Polchinski flow of Bauerschmidt and Bodineau to have a small $L^2$ norm in the scale variable. The decay constants depend only on this $L^2$ norm and the friction. The proof measures the transfer of momentum dissipation to position on the same scales that decompose entropy. A phase-space extension of the Polchinski flow gives Gaussian coarse-graining that commutes with free kinetic evolution. Integrating position--momentum cross terms over these scales yields a corrector bounded by entropy. A force defect accounts for changes in the averaged interaction force away from equilibrium; its evolution in scale controls the errors in the kinetic estimate. For the massive two-dimensional lattice sine--Gordon model with $0<β<4π$ and small dimensionless local coupling, the criterion gives entropy decay for all finite-entropy initial laws, uniformly in the lattice spacing and the volume. For friction proportional to the mass $m$, the rate has optimal order $m$.

papers.title: Endpoint gradient bounds for centered convex maximal operators and probability kernels
papers.abstract: We establish the endpoint gradient estimate for centered homothetic maximal averages in every dimension $d\ge2$ over each fixed convex body with $C^{1,θ}$ boundary, $0<θ\le1$. In particular, the centered ball maximal operator satisfies the $W^{1,1}$ gradient bound in every dimension. Neither strict convexity nor a lower bound on the support gap is required. The geometric argument combines concentration in gradient values with nonhomogeneous calibrated rows and a summable radial correction. It extends the scalar refinement, direction-history construction and global assembly of the planar centered-disk proof of OpenAI. A separate transfer theorem gives sharp singular-derivative identities for bounded compact probability kernels once local BV output is known, and gradient continuity under an additional spatial-tail condition. Quantitative contact and translation estimates yield further profile and kernel examples. The estimates retain the fixed body's regularity data; the endpoint for arbitrary $C^1$ and nonsmooth convex bodies remains open here.

papers.title: Beyond Physical Illness: Can Clinical Narratives Reveal Emerging Mental Health Risks in Chronically Ill Patients?
papers.abstract: Mental-health risks such as depression, dementia, and suicidal ideation can emerge during hospitalization among chronically ill patients and may worsen without timely recognition and intervention. However, most existing mental health studies focus on patients with established psychiatric conditions rather than patients hospitalized primarily for physical illness. In this work, we investigate whether latent mental-health risk in chronically ill patients can be inferred from longitudinal clinical narratives. We construct a weakly supervised cohort around 4,000 patients from MIMIC-III using mental-health evidence extracted from discharge summaries. A hierarchical state-space framework derives mental-health representations from day-wise clinical narratives and models their temporal evolution for risk estimation throughout hospitalization. Preliminary results demonstrate improved binary risk prediction using the proposed representations and show distinct model derived risk trajectories between risk and no-risk cohorts, providing a foundation for studying emerging mental-health risks in chronically ill patients.

papers.title: The Evolution and 'Chineseness' of Urban Screens in China: From Propaganda Posters to Smart City Interfaces
papers.abstract: Urban screens have become a global feature of the media city, yet their developmental paths are not universal. This paper argues that the evolution of urban screens in China constitutes a distinct paradigm of media urbanism, termed Chineseness, understood here not as cultural essence but as a relational, historically situated configuration of three linked elements: deep-rooted lineages of public communication; state-steered technological leapfrogging driven by industrial policy and mega-events; and a regulatory paradox that enables spectacular scale while tightening operational control. Drawing on a five-stage genealogy (1990-present), a chronology of representative screens, and five paradigmatic cases, the study shows how this configuration produces temporal-spatial compression, the coexistence of multiple technological generations, and privileges collective witnessing over device-centric interactivity. The paper contributes a documented genealogy of Chinese urban screens, develops temporal-spatial compression and collective witnessing as analytical tools for non-Western media ecologies, and positions Chineseness as a globally relevant alternative to market-led models of media architecture.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of solutions for a random PDE-ODE model describing glioma invasion and radiotherapy
papers.abstract: We study a stochastic model for the growth and invasion of glioma cells in the anisotropic brain tissue, also incorporating effects of radiotherapeutic interventions and associated uncertainties. The PDE-ODE model couples glioma and healthy tissue dynamics in a nonlinear manner and explicitly includes treatment-related stochasticity through random depletion terms. The macroscopic system has been obtained by an upscaling procedure from a microscopic description in [1]. We prove the existence and uniqueness of local strong solutions to the corresponding stochastic system. The analysis addresses challenges arising from the nonlinear coupling, anisotropic diffusion, taxis mechanisms, and stochastic treatment effects, providing a first rigorous step toward the mathematical understanding of stochastic continuum models for glioma invasion and therapy response.

papers.title: samQEq: universal charge equilibration for molecules and conductors
papers.abstract: Charge equilibration assigns atomic charges by equalizing an atomic chemical potential built from electronegativity, hardness and the Coulomb interaction. Under one global constraint it lets charge flow without limit between molecules, which fluctuating-charge models prevent with one neutrality constraint per molecule. A metal needs the opposite: a global constraint and a hardness near zero, and there the charge operator becomes indefinite unless it includes each charge's own self-energy. Here, we present samQEq (solids-and-molecules QEq), a unified charge-equilibration package for LAMMPS that combines the two constructions in one energy functional and one matrix-free solve. An orthogonal projector imposes one neutrality constraint per molecule, and the finite-width self-energy of a Gaussian charge on designated conductor types, narrower than the conductor's own Gaussian, keeps the conductor's part of the operator positive definite at any hardness. On a gold slab carrying a water film, the operator stays definite down to the conductor limit of the model, the metal screens a point charge by a constant amount at every height beyond 4 Å, and the film's charges stay bounded under dynamics. Reciprocal-space electrostatics is evaluated inside the matrix-vector product, and three distinct shielding kernels are run-time settings. We verify the implementation by reproducing a published fluctuating-charge water model without refitting, and the native ReaxFF charge-equilibration step to approximately $10^{-9}\,e$. On a single four-V100 node the largest tested systems run at approximately twice the throughput of a 128-core CPU node. samQEq thus provides one charge-equilibration layer for molecules, conductors and the interfaces between them.

papers.title: Compositional Operational Rank, Smooth Realizability, and Dimensional Reduction
papers.abstract: Higher-dimensional theories distinguish the dimensionality of a microscopic description from the number of directions accessible to a physical observer. Relating these notions requires not only dimensional reduction, but also a consistent preservation of operational independence across different levels of description. We establish sufficient conditions under which a compositional operational rank is preserved first as the dimension of a smooth integral leaf and then as an observable Fisher-information rank. The key requirement is closure-faithfulness: the smooth realization must preserve the dependency relations of the operational closure, rather than merely its total rank. Together with real representability, constant rank, involutivity, and observer/scale compatibility, this yields a local integral leaf whose dimension equals the operational rank. A further primary-identification condition is required at the measurement level. If an independently specified observer image coincides locally with the primary integral distribution and the admissible protocols provide local resolution, finite labeled-mixture closure, and locally constant outcome support, then the same rank can be realized by a finite composite Fisher-information protocol. The construction holds for arbitrary finite rank. At r = 4 it provides a conditional operational criterion for dimensional reduction in higher-dimensional theories: a viable reduction must preserve the relevant operational dependency structure, not merely produce four effective coordinates. Quantum-hardware negative controls further show that the same restricted Fisher rank can conceal different larger ranks under a broader pre-specified measurement protocol. The framework therefore constrains the operational outcome of dimensional reduction without imposing a universal four-dimensional bound on microscopic state spaces.

papers.title: Do Similarity Measures Measure Similarity? How User Activity Creates Phantom Correlation in Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Item-item similarity is one of the oldest and most foundational signals in recommender systems: two items are assumed to be similar when the same users consume them. Despite the sparsity and scale of interaction data, the implicit assumption across the field is that item co-occurrence reflects genuine shared preference, capturing what users like together. In this paper, we demonstrate that a substantial fraction of observed item-item similarity is an artifact of variance in user activity rather than shared taste. Even if every user consumed items completely independently, differing only in their total consumption volume, standard similarity measures still detect strong associations between items. We term this phenomenon phantom correlation: spurious item association that emerges strictly from heterogeneous user activity in the complete absence of preference structure. Starting from minimal formal assumptions, we show that independent consumption under varying activity is described by a Rasch model, and we derive how the resulting association depends on item popularity for each similarity measure. By comparing our theoretical baseline against real-world benchmark datasets, we reveal the extent to which popular similarity measures reflect phantom correlation, which bears on how item co-occurrence is interpreted and used in collaborative filtering.

papers.title: Improving Signals, Declining Encoder: A Known-Answer Test of Label-Free Monitoring in Self-Supervised Learning
papers.abstract: Self-supervised training is monitored without labels, through the loss and statistics of the learned features. We report a case where we know the encoders lost part of what they had learned, so we can check whether these signals noticed. We trained LeJEPA encoders on synthetic images with known generating factors. In nine of ten seeds, the readability of those factors fell abruptly and stayed down, nearly always along the same direction in factor space. Meanwhile the loss kept falling, and most of the eleven label-free signals we tracked kept improving and rated the declining runs better than runs that did not decline. Standard change-point detection rarely flagged the decline near its onset, and selecting checkpoints by these signals mostly chose ones after it.

papers.title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
papers.abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) of microservice failures has attracted many LLM agents whose investigation is hand-crafted, through standard operating procedures, fixed stages and role agents. Each is evaluated on its own data against few baselines, so it is unknown whether this design beats letting a capable model investigate on its own. We compare three simple harnesses that prescribe none of the model's calls (one call over an evidence package, a SQL agent and the Codex coding agent) with five published LLM RCA agents and with statistical and causal methods on RCAtlas, 90 validated cases from eight public datasets, across six models and three reasoning efforts. The simple harnesses are the most accurate (PR@1 65-77% on three mid-tier models), ahead of the published agents (16-53%) and the non-LLM methods (6-39%), on every model on which both families were run. The published agents fix from a tenth to all of their model calls in the program, and a case study shows how these prescriptions skip the decisive evidence. A stronger model mainly improves reliability, a multi-turn harness mainly improves aptitude, and more reasoning effort changes accuracy by a few points at most while multiplying the time by up to seven. Among runs more accurate than the best non-LLM method, every Pareto-optimal run in cost or time uses a simple harness.

papers.title: Growth Phase Map of α and \b{eta} Tantalum as a Function of Growth Temperature and Oxygen Partial Pressure
papers.abstract: Tantalum thin films are used in low-loss superconducting quantum circuits, yet the growth conditions governing selection of $α$-Ta(110), $α$-Ta(111), and metastable $β$-Ta on c-plane sapphire remain uncertain. We deposited 100 nm Ta films by dc magnetron sputtering on Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) at 300-900 $^\circ$C while varying the O$_2$ partial pressure from a $5.5\times10^{-11}$ Torr ultrahigh-vacuum baseline to $2.23\times10^{-4}$ Torr. Absorption-corrected X-ray diffraction texture coefficients were used to construct a ternary phase-orientation growth map in terms of temperature and the oxygen-to-Ta impingement flux ratio ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}\leq4.8\times10^{-6}$ to 19). Without added oxygen, $α$-Ta(110) dominated at every temperature. At an O$_2$ pressure of only $2.5\times10^{-9}$ Torr ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}=2.2\times10^{-4}$), $α$-Ta(111) accounted for 98-99% of the normalized texture weight from 300 to 700 $^\circ$C, decreasing to 65% at 900 $^\circ$C. Substantial $β$-Ta formed only at the highest oxygen dose, dominating at 300 $^\circ$C and disappearing at 900 $^\circ$C. The apparent $β$(001)/$α$(110) selection energy of $1.07\pm0.16$ eV is comparable to the activation energy for oxygen diffusion in Ta, consistent with oxygen transport influencing phase selection. Oxygen also produced orientation-dependent changes in crystallite size and microstrain. These findings establish oxygen-controlled processing windows for phase- and orientation-selective growth of Ta films for superconducting devices.

papers.title: Self-intersection local times of Volterra Gaussian bridges with large end-to-end distance
papers.abstract: Self-intersection local times serve as the Hamiltonian in the Gibbs measure of continuous polymer models, for which the end-to-end distance is a key quantity. We study multiple self-intersection local times of Volterra Gaussian bridges, \emph{i.e.}, Volterra Gaussian processes conditioned on their final location $a$, as $\|a\|\to\infty$. For $d$-dimensional $(2,ζ)$-locally nondeterministic processes with $ζ\in(0,2/d)$, we prove that these local times exist in every $L^p$. Under two further conditions on the kernel, the $p$-th moment of the $m$-multiple self-intersection local time of the bridge is of exact order $\|a\|^{-γ}$ for every integer $p\geqslant1$, with $γ=p(m-1)(2-ζd)/(2-ζ)$. In the plane, for kernels $k(t-s)$ with $k(0)\neq0$ and under strong local nondeterminism, we restrict the double self-intersection local time to $\{t_2-t_1\geqslant\|a\|^{-α}\}$, $α>0$, and establish a phase transition: its expectation decays like $\exp(-c\|a\|^{2-α})$, converges to an explicit positive limit, or grows logarithmically, for $α<2$, $α=2$ and $α>2$ respectively.

papers.title: The Undecidability of FO3 and the Calculus of Relations with Just One Binary Relation
papers.abstract: The validity problem for first-order logic is a well-known undecidable problem. The undecidability also holds even for $\mathsf{FO}3$ and (equational formulas of) the calculus of relations. In this paper we tighten these undecidability results to the following: (1) $\mathsf{FO}3$ with just one binary relation is undecidable even without equality; and (2) the calculus of relations with just one character and with only composition, union, and complement is undecidable. Additionally we prove that the finite validity problem is also undecidable for the above two classes.

papers.title: Traveling Waves for Mixed Nonlocal-Local Systems of Conservation Laws on $\mathbb{S}^1$
papers.abstract: Non trivial traveling waves in genuinely nonlinear conservation laws hardly appear and, in some cases, scalar nonlocal conservation laws inherit this feature. Here, we show that mixed nonlocal-local systems of conservation laws display a far richer scenario. A variety of traveling waves may exist, different components may travel with different speeds and traveling waves can appear as time-asymptotic limits. Technically, these results need a significant extension of Dafermos' "trend to steady state" theory, exploiting properties of Hamiltonian systems solved by generalized characteristics.

papers.title: On the Nash equilibrium for a model of traffic flow
papers.abstract: The paper consider a conservation law model of traffic flow on a highway, where each driver chooses an optimal departure time $τ^d$, based on a departure cost $\varphi(τ^d)$ and an arrival cost $ψ(τ^a)$. Nash equilibria are studied, where no driver can reduce his own cost by changing his departure time. The first results provide continuity estimates on the arrival time, depending on the distribution of departures. In terms of the ${\bf L}^1$ distance, we show that the corresponding map is Hölder continuous with exponent $1/2$ in Lagrangian variables (labelling individual drivers), and Lipschitz continuous in Eulerian space variables. Concerning the regularity of the a Nash equilibrium, our results show that, when the total number of drivers is sufficiently large, a queue alway forms at the entrance of the highway and the corresponding traffic density contains a shock. Moreover, for any number of drivers (possibly small), we prove that for generic $\mathcal C^2$ cost functions $\varphi, ψ$ the Nash equilibrium solution still contains a shock. In the last section of the paper, assuming that the initial departure rate is not a Nash equilibrium, we consider an evolution equation for the departure rate, where each driver keeps changing his daily departure time in order to reduce his own cost. It is proved that this nonlocal integro-differential evolution equation admits a unique solution, globally in time. This provides some theoretical support to earlier numerical simulations, which indicated the dynamic instability of the Nash equilibrium and the possible existence of a chaotic attractor.

papers.title: A Unified Arena for LLM Agents across Diverse Eurogame
papers.abstract: Interactive environments offer a practical way to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents, and competitive games extend this evaluation to decisions shaped by competing goals and other agents' choices. Yet existing evaluations confined to individual games or execution frameworks leave unclear which competitive advantages persist across settings. We introduce DECE (Diverse Eurogame Competitive Environments), a unified arena spanning ten Eurogames with shared interfaces and evaluation protocols. These games combine lasting strategic commitments, competition over shared resources, and multiple routes to victory. Our primary study evaluates 12 model-harness configurations, spanning nine models and four execution harnesses, in 480 three-player matches across ten games. The main and supplementary studies comprise 1,032 completed matches in total. These comparisons reveal broad cross-game ranking agreement alongside game-specific strengths. Matched studies show that the same model can perform differently across execution harnesses, adding another source of variation to these profiles. These performance advantages do not consistently translate into better token or cost efficiency, making resource use an additional consideration when comparing configurations. Together, the findings support evaluating complete agent configurations by both their competitive performance across games and the resources needed to achieve it.

papers.title: A solution to Haagerup's problem: Normality of weights is commutatively determined
papers.abstract: We prove that a weight on a C$^*$-algebra is lower semi-continuous if it is lower semi-continuous on commutative C$^*$-subalgebras. This can be used to prove a von Neumann algebraic counterpart that a weight on a von Neumann algebra is normal if it is normal on commutative von Neumann subalgebras. This provides an affirmative solution to Haagerup's second problem (Problem 1.11) on normal weights posed in 1975.

papers.title: OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Specialist policies alone do not ensure task-level reliability, while powerful multimodal agents rely on costly reasoning and external experience that compact models struggle to reproduce. We introduce OmniBrain-0, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). It distills powerful teachers' interaction experience into manipulation and navigation experts, then consolidates their decision capabilities into OmniBrain-0. Unification therefore occurs within the learned decision model rather than only at the tool interface. We further introduce Rubric-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), a data flywheel in which a Meta-Agent turns execution evidence into refined rubrics, step-level reminders, and verified trajectories for domain-expert updates before their reconsolidation into OmniBrain-0 through MOPD. We evaluate OmniBrain-0 on LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa365, RoboTwin 2.0, and R2R-CE Val-Unseen, as well as multiple real-world manipulation tasks. OmniBrain-0 combines strong cross-domain task performance with substantially lower inference and execution overhead than its closed-source teacher, demonstrating efficient transfer and consolidation of embodied capabilities into a compact unified agent.

papers.title: Focusing Efficiency for Large Intelligent Surfaces
papers.abstract: This paper studies wireless power transmission (WPT) with large intelligent surfaces (LISs) in a single-user scenario, with emphasis on power-transfer efficiency. The optimal current distribution on the LIS is derived under a total-power constraint for an arbitrary receiving antenna, providing a theoretical characterization of the maximum achievable focusing efficiency. The analysis shows that the efficiency is strongly affected by the receiving radiation pattern, antenna orientation, and transmission distance. Clear performance differences are observed among practical antenna types for specific orientations, whereas directional averaging makes their average focusing efficiencies much closer. The theoretical findings are further validated by full-wave FEKO simulations, showing good agreement with the predictions of the proposed formulation. These results provide insight into the impact of receiver characteristics and propagation geometry on LIS-enabled WPT and offer a theoretical basis for efficient single-user power-transfer design.

papers.title: Immersive Commons: Designing Ephemeral Spatial Dialogue for Co-Located Mixed Reality Environments
papers.abstract: Head-mounted mixed reality (MR) often prioritises individual immersion, potentially drawing attention away from others sharing the room. This paper asks how MR can support co-located spatial dialogue through embodied interaction and activity visible to non-headset observers. We introduce Immersive Commons, a design framework, and Atmos Messages, a prototype combining gesture-based, ephemeral spatial messages with voice transcription, preset text, and a public floor-plan overview. Following a Research through Design approach, fifteen participants created 236 messages across two sessions, including 48 voice-authored messages. Questionnaire responses highlighted playfulness and social awareness, while observations suggested opportunities for exchange grounded in the architectural setting. Interaction clustered near the public display, although this was also where participants put on their headsets. These findings suggest the potential of ephemeral spatial messaging to support co-located exchange, with playfulness, shared visibility, and architectural context informing the design of more social and situated MR experiences.

papers.title: Tidal contributions to neutron star orbital precession around Sgr $A^*$
papers.abstract: We investigate tidal contributions to the orbital precession of neutron stars around the supermassive black hole Sgr A*, using stellar configurations described by the Tolman - Oppenheimer - Volkoff equations. We examine the dependence of tidal precession on stellar compactness, pericentre distance, and the quadrupolar tidal Love number $k_2$, and compare its magnitude with general relativistic orbital precession. The calculated tidal angular shift decreases strongly with increasing pericentre distance and, for the stellar configurations considered, with increasing compactness. Larger Love numbers enhance the tidal contribution. This behaviour reflects the strong dependence of tidal precession on the stellar-radius-to-pericentre-distance ratio, $(R/r_p)^5$. Despite the enhancement during closer encounters, the predicted tidal shifts remain extremely small, reaching approximately $3.5 \times 10^{-18},μas$ within the displayed parameter range. The ratio of tidal to general relativistic precession spans approximately $10^{-33}$ - $10^{-28}$, indicating that relativistic precession overwhelmingly dominates. Our results suggest that direct detection of the neutron-star tidal contribution through orbital precession around Sgr A* would be exceptionally challenging under the assumptions of the adopted model.

papers.title: P-stable degree sequence regions for bipartite and directed graphs
papers.abstract: The switch Markov chain is a natural method for sampling graph realizations with a prescribed degree sequence, and $P$-stability is a general sufficient condition for its rapid mixing. Since $P$-stability is often difficult to verify directly, we develop an approach based on the simpler and more readily verifiable property of \emph{full graphicality}. We consider bidegree sequence regions obtained by fixing the two class sizes, the common degree sum, and lower and upper bounds for the degrees in each class. Such a region is fully graphic if every bidegree sequence satisfying these constraints has a bipartite realization. Our main result shows that every fully graphic region of this form is $P$-stable. More precisely, for class sizes $n$ and $m$, the perturbation ratio is at most $(nm)^5$. It follows from a known theory that the switch Markov chain is rapidly mixing on every such region. We also show that full graphicality can be tested on a canonical extremal bidegree sequence and use this characterization to derive several new explicit sufficient conditions. By encoding loopless directed graphs as bipartite graphs, we develop a parallel theory for directed degree sequences. This gives analogous extremal characterizations, sufficient conditions for full graphicality, and $P$-stability and rapid-mixing results for directed degree-sequence regions. The encoding process allows most corresponding statements for the two cases to be formulated and proved in one run.

papers.title: Quantum Field Theory on the Tangent Bundle
papers.abstract: We develop a quantum-field-theoretical framework on the tangent bundle in which gravitational and internal gauge structures are associated with different sectors of an affine tangent-fiber geometry. The translational sector supplies the coframe and its relation to teleparallel gravity. A reduced vertical spectral problem is based on the centrally extended Euclidean group \(E^{c}(2)\), motivated by projective representations of the stabilizer of a nonzero null vector. Twofold multiplicities of equivalent vertical representations in selected left-chiral sectors admit weak \(SU(2)\) actions, while an assumed threefold quark multiplicity admits a locally gauged color \(SU(3)_c\) symmetry. A proposed global quotient correlates the color center with vertical rotations on a threefold rotation cover. Together with the selected chiral spectrum and anomaly conditions, this construction reproduces the observed fractional quark charge assignments. We formulate matter and gauge-field quantization, BRST symmetry, and anomaly constraints. Under the stated projection assumptions, the color sector has the standard local QCD structure, including its one-loop beta function and asymptotic freedom. Additional gauge bosons and dark-matter states are proposed as hypothetical sectors. We also formulate a structural action for possible couplings between teleparallel torsion and additional Lorentz-sector potentials. The framework relates selected structures of particle physics and gravity within a common geometric setting; their further dynamical and phenomenological development remains open.

papers.title: The counts of parity-odd vs even late-growing permutations in the group $\mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ differ by $(-1)^p$
papers.abstract: A permutation $σ\in\mathbb{S}_n$ of objects $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is called \emph{late-growing} if its partial sums never exceed the respective partial sums of the `average' permutation (with the arithmetic mean $n^{-1}\cdot\sum_{i=1}^n i = (n+1)/2$ of $1,\ldots,n$ on average at each entry $σ(i)$): $\sum_{i=1}^k σ(i) \leqslant k\cdot (n+1)/2$ for all positive $k\leqslant n$. We prove that for $n=2p-1$ odd, the set $Φ_p\subseteq \mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ of late-growing permutations is partitioned into parity-even vs odd elements, $Φ_p = Φ_p^{+} \sqcup Φ_p^{-}$, in an almost symmetric way: $| Φ_p^{+} | - | Φ_p^{-} | = (-1)^{p+1}$. The proof is constructive: by viewing the permutations $σ\inΦ_p$ as constrained walks on the integral lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, we describe two filters that pair all but one element in $Φ_p^{+}$ versus $Φ_p^{-}$; the remaining walk $σ^*$ with monotonically growing step amplitudes determines the dominant parity subset.

papers.title: Do Coding Agents Still Need a Debugger? Frontier-Model-Based Fault Localization at the Accuracy Ceiling
papers.abstract: Background: To localize a fault, a coding agent can reason from source code alone or use debugger assistance by running the program and stepping through it in an interactive debugger. While earlier agents struggled with static execution tracing and debugger operation, frontier LLMs have improved at both. Objective: We evaluate how accurately coding agents localize faults without tools across original and transformed programs, how much debugger assistance improves accuracy and at what cost, and how agents use it when optional. Methods: We seed 610 single-line faults into 144 LeetCodeDataset solutions and rewrite each faulty program with five recipes of behavior-preserving transformations. Agents based on Sol 6.1, Luna 6, and Qwen 3.8 localize each fault with no, optional, or encouraged debugger assistance. Results: Without tools, the agents localized 98.2 to 99.9% of faults in original and 96.7 to 99.9% in transformed programs, losing accuracy mainly where recipes restructured loops and conditions. Encouraged assistance removed 63% and 61% of Luna 6's and Qwen 3.8's remaining transformed errors (+2.1 and +1.3 percentage points) at 14.7 to 27.0 times the token use, while Sol 6.1 stayed at 99.9%. With optional assistance, Luna 6 and Qwen 3.8 still gained +1.5 and +1.3 points, though the agents used the interactive debugger in only 0.2 to 6.2% of runs. Conclusions: On short, precisely specified programs, current coding agents localize nearly all faults from source code alone, and debugger assistance removes most errors that remain. Given the choice, agents executed the program far more often than they stepped through it, yet kept most of the benefit.

papers.title: The generic structure of the singular set in the Stefan problem
papers.abstract: We show that, in every space dimension $n\ge2$, the singular set $Σ$ of a generic (in the Baire-category sense) solution of the Stefan problem is countably parabolically $(n-2)$-rectifiable. In particular, $\dim_{\mathrm{par}}(Σ)\le n-2$. This is achieved by proving the following sharp result: in every space dimension, points of the maximal stratum of a generic solution are discrete in space-time.

papers.title: Using the Blackwell-Cover Guessing Strategy to Separate Unobserved Bernoulli Trials - II
papers.abstract: In a prior paper, we investigated what could be said about the number in the pair that was not observed when we employed the BlackwellCover Guessing Strategy. In this paper, we generalize prior results to arbitrary distributions. We use a variant of the BlackwellCover strategy ro take pairs of coins chosen from a mixture of two different distributions G and H such that one of the coins is flipped, and as a result of that flip the unobserved (unflipped) coin is placed in one of two sets A and B. We show that, regardless of which distributions are used for G and H, there are situations in which this can be done so that the mean of the heads probabilities of the unobserved coins in A is less than the mean of the heads probabilities of the unobserved coins in B. What makes this result surprising, in addition to its generality, is a comparison with a corresponding result for marbles. If one knows that one will always be weighing one of two marbles with different specific weights, such as 10g and 20g, knowing the weight of the marble being weighed automatically determines the weight of the other. However, even if one knows that one will be flipping one of two coins with specific heads probabilities such as 1/3 and 2/3, the outcome of the flip of one of the coins will not immediately enable one to conclude anything about the heads probability of the unflipped coin, which is where the BlackwellCover Guessing Strategy comes into play.

papers.title: Persistence Pays: Square-root condition-number dependence for Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin Monte Carlo with a non-reversibly updated accept/reject uniform
papers.abstract: We prove accelerated mixing for a Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin sampler: the OBABO splitting with friction $2\sqrt m$, adjusted with Neal's non-reversibly updated uniform, which is redrawn after every epoch of $E$ steps. For targets $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $mI\preceq\nabla^2U\preceq LI$ and an $L_H$-Lipschitz Hessian, started from a Gaussian at an approximate minimizer, the chain reaches total variation accuracy $\varepsilon$ after $\tilde O\big(\sqrt{κd}+\sqrt{L_H}(d/m)^{3/4}\big)$ gradient evaluations, where $κ=L/m$ and $\tilde O$ hides logarithmic factors. The $\sqrtκ$ term is necessary, already on Gaussian targets. The proof discretizes Lu's entropic hypocoercivity by means of an entropy inequality for free transport, so that the relative entropy of the unadjusted chain decays at a rate of order $\sqrt m$ up to a discretization bias. With the non-reversibly updated uniform, the leading energy errors of velocity Verlet telescope along a path. A coupling argument combines the two. On Bayesian logistic regression posteriors for two standard data sets, which satisfy these assumptions, the gradient cost of the chain with the non-reversibly updated uniform grows roughly like the square root of the condition number at the posterior mode, and that of standard adjusted OBABO roughly like its $3/4$ power.

papers.title: Atomic Security Concerns: Towards a Foundational Language for Security Knowledge Representation
papers.abstract: Cybersecurity governance, risk management, compliance, and security architecture rely on numerous concepts, including security properties, domains, controls, risks, implementation measures, capabilities, and compliance requirements. Although these concepts are widely used, they are often represented through heterogeneous abstractions and vocabularies, making relationships among them difficult to express consistently and leaving much of the associated reasoning dependent on expert knowledge.
