This paper introduces the concepts of Security Concerns and Atomic Security Concerns (ASCs) and explores the hypothesis that cybersecurity knowledge may be represented through a finite set of foundational concerns. Inspired by the role of atoms in chemistry, the proposed approach views cybersecurity concepts as compositions of more fundamental concerns rather than as independent abstractions. Hence, Atomic Security Concerns could be viewed as a common abstraction layer for the representation of cybersecurity concepts, independently of their domain, nature, or level of granularity. Building upon this perspective, the paper explores how Atomic Security Concerns may provide the vocabulary of a cybersecurity language and how cybersecurity concepts may be represented as concern sets supporting explicit relationships among concepts. The contribution of this work is intentionally conceptual: it introduces a framework and research hypothesis for investigating the foundations of a common language for cybersecurity knowledge representation, reasoning, and future formalization.

papers.title: Weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for Stirling--Whitney--Riordan and Laguerre polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a sufficient condition for weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for the Stirling--Whitney--Riordan polynomials. The proof uses polynomial transformations that preserve zeros in a real interval and in the unit disk. As an application, we prove that the extended Turán expressions for the Bell polynomials are weakly Hurwitz stable. We also prove the corresponding result for the reflected Laguerre polynomials using polynomial approximations. These results settle two conjectures of Chasse, Grabarek, and Visontai.

papers.title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
papers.abstract: We construct a controllable imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems using spatially modulated local rotations without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes. This feature unambiguously isolates the redistribution of spectral weights as the sole driver of the anomalous relaxation. Using the compact-boson description, we reveal that these twists act as precise mode selectors: higher-harmonic twists exclusively populate high-energy standing waves, structurally bypassing slow-decaying infrared modes to accelerate convergence. We derive exact analytical crossing times for these reversals and demonstrate that intentionally reintroducing the slow-mode population systematically delays the ITME. This exact mechanism is validated beyond the fixed-point theory via calculations on interacting XXZ chains and ladders. Furthermore, a twelve-qubit simulation of variational quantum imaginary-time evolution reproduces the reversals and their controlled delay, providing a concrete route to realize this protocol in realistic quantum circuits. Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.

papers.title: A theory of noisy linear recurrent neural network learning dynamics
papers.abstract: Biological neural networks are noisy: their dynamics involve difficult-to-predict fluctuations which are likely due not just to chaos, but also to a variety of low-level biophysical processes. Despite the omnipresence of intrinsic noise, its theoretical consequences are incompletely understood, especially in the context of learning. For example, does noise meaningfully shape representation learning, or is it better viewed as a nuisance factor whose presence or absence changes little about what solution is found and when? Here, we argue that intrinsic noise can significantly modulate representation learning in recurrent neural networks (RNNs), since it can strongly break solution-space degeneracies and in some cases control whether a non-degenerate solution exists at all. We show that this is true for an analytically tractable model of noisy RNN learning with a linear activation function and white noise inputs. We find that, in the so-called rich regime (where weights are initialized with small values), noise strongly modulates the directions in which the read-in, readout, and recurrent weights align. Moreover, we find that noise produces a kind of phase transition: for sufficiently high noise, a non-degenerate solution is not even optimal if parameter scales are limited (e.g., via regularization). These results extend recent analytic work on RNN representation learning and show that noise can act as a fundamental determinant of representations.

papers.title: Wrinkling dynamics of thin crystalline sheets and its dependency on topological defects
papers.abstract: We investigate the wrinkling dynamics of thin crystalline sheets under uniaxial compression using a Surface Phase-Field-Crystal-Helfrich (SPFCH) model, which captures the coupling between crystalline order, out-of-plane deformations, and topological defects. In particular, the model allows us to track and characterize two distinct classes of defects, namely those forming in the underlying hexagonal crystal lattice, such as dislocations and grain boundaries, and defects in the wrinkling patterns, known as wrinklons. By resolving the evolution and interactions of these defects, we investigate how the interplay between in-plane and out-of-plane relaxation mechanisms influences wrinkling onset and the coarsening regime. Our results indicate that crystalline defects do not affect coarsening scaling, but they quantitatively affect the onset of wrinkling and the emerging wrinkling wavelength, promote more irregular wrinkle patterns with a higher density of wrinklons, and modify long-timescale morphological evolution.

papers.title: Selective Tie Learning: Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Preference optimization can learn spurious correlations, and augmenting the preference data with ties (equally preferred responses) can reduce spurious reliance. However, ties differ in their corrective effect, making their selection for augmentation important. For log-linear policies, we derive each tie's influence on spurious reliance and show that taking the largest predicted reductions is first-order optimal among subsets of equal size. Computing these influences requires knowledge of the spurious features and the curvature of the training objective, which is often unavailable or expensive to estimate. To this end, we explore using the magnitude of a tie's implicit reward margin and characterize the conditions under which it is a useful proxy for predicted influence. To test the theory and its qualitative transfer to neural models, we estimate influence with a counterfactual proxy for spurious reliance and use a generalized Gauss--Newton approximation to curvature for language models. Across log-linear policies, neural models, and large language models, our selection rules consistently achieve comparable reductions in spurious reliance with fewer ties than uniform selection.

papers.title: Maximal curves with trivial automorphism group
papers.abstract: We construct algebraic curves with trivial geometric automorphism group by taking cyclic scalar quotients of curves of the form \[ y^r-y=xR(x),\qquad r=p^e. \] We give a condition on the genus under which the quotient has no nontrivial automorphism. The proof uses the ramification of a degree-$r$ morphism to the projective line, Castelnuovo--Severi, and explicit automorphisms of the covering curve. The quotient also has gonality $r$, with a unique morphism of degree $r$ to the projective line up to an automorphism of the latter. Applying the construction to maximal additive curves gives explicit maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group in every positive characteristic, including families defined over the prime field and of unbounded genus. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first examples of maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group. Every maximal curve in these families is covered by the Hermitian curve. For every odd prime $p$ and every $n\ge2$, we prove that the curve $\X_{p,n}$, maximal over $\F_{p^{4n+2}}$, is not a Galois subcover of the corresponding Hermitian curve, even over the algebraic closure. Thus every odd characteristic yields an infinite family of curves covered but not Galois covered by the Hermitian curve. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first such infinite families.

papers.title: The neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter
papers.abstract: We characterize the behavior of the neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter scattering on xenon. The inelastic scattering kinematics reshape the recoil spectrum of the signal and produce a qualitatively different neutrino fog landscape. In some regions of the inelastic parameter space the fog is completely absent for future xenon experiments at any scale, while in other regions the fog is dispelled only to reappear at larger exposures. We find that multiple background sources with uncertain normalizations can make the onset of the fog jump discontinuously with the dark matter mass and mass splitting, while the discovery limit varies smoothly. We also describe a mechanism by which reduced uncertainties on neutrino rates may have the unintuitive effect of raising neutrino floors derived from the fog opacity.

papers.title: Information-theoretic entropy imaging of quantum matter
papers.abstract: Phase transitions can generate intricate spatial organization invisible to spatially averaged probes, yet quantitative measures of this organization remain limited. Here we develop "entropy imaging," an information-theoretic technique that harnesses lossless compression to quantify spatial complexity, predictability, and order in quantum materials. Using this approach, emergent spatial textures can be imaged and converted into an experimentally-accessible observable: the computable information density (CID), a compression-based measure of information complexity that approaches the Shannon entropy rate in the large-system limit. Applied to millikelvin microwave impedance microscopy of graphene, the method reveals a pronounced maximum in the CID near quantum Hall transitions, a quantitative measure of the information-rich spatial organization of the critical landscape. A disordered Hofstadter model reproduces this behavior and shows that the CID can identify the quantum critical point from a sequence of images, without ensemble averaging over disorder realizations. The same framework tracks fractional quantum Hall transitions and resolves isolated fractional puddles that coexist with a disordered background. By contrast, the trivial band-edge crossover in a MoSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayer exhibits qualitatively different behavior, suggesting that the pronounced CID enhancement observed at the quantum Hall critical point is not simply a generic feature of a conductive-insulating crossover. We further show that the geometric information encoded in CID is not reducible to a correlation length, and it can even distinguish spatial textures with identical multifractal statistics. Together, these results establish lossless compression as a framework for quantifying emergent spatial organization in quantum materials, with portability across imaging modalities and physical systems.

papers.title: Tapering to Enhance the Performance of Nanowire-Based Fluorescent Biosensors
papers.abstract: High-refractive-index nanowires are of interest for signal enhancement in fluorescence-based biosensing. Here, through electromagnetic modelling, we demonstrate substantial fluorescence signal enhancement by incorporating a tapered section into a cylindrical nanowire and investigate two complementary tapering configurations to address practical implementation challenges. Under near-normal excitation, the excitation enhancement increases approximately linearly with taper length, reaching more than three times that of the corresponding non-tapered nanowire at a taper length of 8000 nm. In a non-imaging signal detection scheme using a low numerical aperture (NA), the proposed tapered nanowire achieves more than three orders of magnitude enhancement in fluorescence signal compared with a planar biosensor. Thus, the tapered nanowire should enable efficient fluorescence detection using compact, low-NA optical configuration. In imaging mode, similarly as for non-tapered nanowires, imaging sharpness beyond conventional microscopy limitations is obtained when imaging from the non-tapered nanowire end, while strongly increased excitation enhancement is simultaneously obtained when exciting from the opposite, tapered end.

papers.title: Annealed sampling of diffusion models in lattice field theory
papers.abstract: Machine learning methods have recently gained increasing interest as possible means of solving critical slowing down in lattice field theory, with particular emphasis on sampling methods using field transformations such as normalizing flows, annealing/out-of-equilibrium methods, and diffusion models. Annealing methods provide appealing polynomial scaling and exactness guarantees, while diffusion models use a simple and efficient score-matching training procedure. This work explores a method combining these benefits, first training an energy-based diffusion model using score matching, then sampling using either stochastic normalizing flows (SNFs) or flow-transformed replica exchange (T-REX). The choice of sampling method can be made after training the diffusion model; the theoretical properties of SNFs and T-REX and their relative trade-offs are discussed. Numerical results are presented for scalar field theory and the O(3) non-linear sigma model, using a class of local-footprint energy models with efficient gradient and divergence calculations. Sampling from the trained models follows predicted exactness and scaling properties, and significantly improves over sampling methods without a learned component.

papers.title: Quantifying Claim Smoothing by LLM Research Agents
papers.abstract: Deep research, or any use of large language models (LLMs) to read a large document collection and produce insights, requires synthesizing information from different sources. In this work, we find that LLMs produce long-form research reports that read as confident syntheses but which fail to accurately reflect the underlying documents. We call this failure smoothing. In collapsing diverse and potentially conflicting sources into a single narrative, the model discards the evidential "jaggedness" of its corpus and asserts conclusions more decisive than the citations can support. We introduce a claim level scoring pipeline, SmoothScore, to quantify this effect. Our pipeline extracts key conclusive claims from model generated reports, then finds evidence relevant to each claim and clusters that evidence along high level aspects. Finally, each claim is scored with respect to the evidence to quantify the degree of smoothing done by the agent. Across 7 systems and 4 datasets, we find that agents consistently produce stronger claims than warranted.

papers.title: Computational complexity of the $H$-coloring problem in cubic graphs
papers.abstract: If $G$ and $H$ are two cubic graphs, then an $H$-coloring of $G$ is a mapping $f: E(G)\rightarrow E(H)$, such that for every $v\in V(G)$ there is a vertex $x\in V(H)$, such that $f(\partial_G(v))=\partial_H(x)$. If $G$ admits an $H$-coloring then it is common to write $H\prec G$. In this paper, for a fixed connected cubic graph $H$, we consider a decision problem, which we call $H$-coloring. In this problem, on the input one is given a connected cubic graph $G$. The goal is to decide whether $H\prec G$. A conjecture by Hakobyan and the author states that $H$-coloring is polynomial time solvable, if $H$ does not admit a $P_{12}$-coloring. Here $P_{12}$ is the unique cubic graph obtained from the Petersen graph by expanding one of its vertices into a triangle. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture under $P\neq NP$, by showing that $S_6$-coloring is NP-complete. Here $S_6$ is the unique cubic graph on six vertices having exactly one bridge. Our second result is an algorithm that solves $H$-coloring problem in time $O^*(c^n)$, where $H$ is a simple connected cubic graph, $n$ is the number of vertices of the input cubic graph $G$ and $c=\sqrt{8}\approx 2.8284$.

papers.title: Number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell
papers.abstract: We prove Shi's conjecture that the number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell of the affine Weyl group attached to a simply connected simple complex group $G$ is exactly $|W_0|/2$, where $W_0$ is the corresponding finite Weyl group. The same formula holds for the corresponding extended affine Weyl group. The key step is to show that the reductive centralizer in $G$ of a minimal nilpotent element has identity component with simply connected derived subgroup and admits no nontrivial algebraic central extensions by $\mathbb G_m$. This gives an isomorphism of based rings between the asymptotic ring of the extended cell and a matrix ring over the representation ring of the centralizer, with matrix size equal to the Euler characteristic of the Springer fiber, namely $|W_0|/2$.

papers.title: On the Anderson Dual of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give complete classifications of the finite groups $G$ for which the constant Eilenberg--Mac Lane spectra $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ are Anderson self-dual up to a virtual representation shift, and we determine all such shifts. For both of these spectra, we determine the representation periodicity lattice for every finite group. As applications, we obtain $RO(G)$-graded universal coefficient theorems relating equivariant homology and cohomology, together with formulas for the Anderson duals of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$-modules. In the $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ self-dual cases, we identify the graded $\mathbb F_2$-linear dual of the coefficient ring $π_\star^G H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ with a representation shift of the ring as a module over itself. This gives perfect multiplication pairings and graded self-injectivity.

papers.title: Priors and parameterizations for Bayesian regression with categorical variables and interactions
papers.abstract: Regression analysis commonly features categorical variables and their interactions to model heterogeneous, group-specific effects. Such interactions are notorious for weak signals and cumbersome parameterizations, and thus urgently require shrinkage. However, the overwhelming default for linear models--using dummy coding, removing a reference group, and applying shrinkage--leads to unwelcome biases, asymmetries, and parameter incongruities across models. We resolve these limitations with a new parameterization-prior combination that couples abundance-based constraints for identifiability with customized shrinkage priors for categorical effects and interactions (BayesABCs). BayesABCs offers a surprising and unique invariance property: the joint posterior of all main effects is (nearly) unchanged by the addition of categorical interactions. We show how this, in conjunction with our shrinkage priors, effectively removes the principal drawbacks of including categorical interactions, thereby making heterogeneous effect estimation broadly feasible. We enforce the identifiability constraints via conditioning and provide a model representation that facilitates efficient posterior computing and direct analysis. Across simulations with a variety of categorical effects and interactions, BayesABCs consistently produces more accurate estimates and predictions, sharper inferences, and unmatched robustness to extraneous interactions relative to competing parameterizations and priors. We apply BayesABCs to study disparities in the error rates of automatic speech recognition systems.

papers.title: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
papers.abstract: We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^λ_F(ρ)\}_{λ>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246]. We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties. The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states. Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed. As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. The non-uniqueness of such a state is also shown.

papers.title: How to get an attractive model
papers.abstract: We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations. We draw attention to this operator because of its clear geometric interpretation and evidence that it possesses a rank-two attractor, conjecturally giving a new example of a Calabi-Yau threefold with modularity properties analogous to those of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$.

papers.title: Modeling the CNOT gate in Germanium double quantum dots
papers.abstract: We model a controlled-NOT (CNOT) gate mediated by exchange interactions in a realistic Ge/GeSi hole spin-qubit device. We use for that purpose a computationally efficient framework based on a compact dressed basis of many-body singlet and triplet states, which enables fast time-dependent simulations that would be prohibitive within a conventional configuration-interaction approach. We discuss the dominant sources of infidelity in ideal (noise-free) devices. On the one hand, the nonadiabaticity of the tunnel barrier ramps, enhanced by the transverse component of the exchange interaction, imposes limits on the speed of the CNOT gate. On the other hand, the AC Stark shift of the conditional resonance and the off-resonant driving of the complementary transition can significantly degrade the gate fidelity and call for a careful optimization of the driving conditions. Finally, we investigate the impact of quasi-static charge noise on the fidelity of the CNOT gate. We find that the capture of charges near the qubits can strongly disrupt the conditional operation, while the nanometer-scale motion of charges results in a loss of fidelity that sensitively depends on the position and strength of the corresponding dipole. Our results quantify the requirements on barrier control, microwave driving, and charge-noise stability for high-fidelity two-qubit operations in Ge/GeSi hole-spin qubits.

papers.title: An Ab Initio Quantum-Chemistry-Based Three-Temperature Approach for Non-Equilibrium Hypersonic Flows: Application to Homogeneous 0-D Chemical Systems
papers.abstract: This work presents an ab initio quantum-chemistry-based one-bin, three-temperature (1-bin 3T) model for non-equilibrium thermochemistry of homogeneous chemical systems in their electronic ground state, derived using the multi-group maximum-entropy principle. The proposed framework captures both vibrational and rotational non-equilibrium effects, thereby enabling an accurate representation of thermochemical behavior in high-temperature gases. To account for departures from equilibrium dissociation, a non-equilibrium correction factor derived from ro-vibrational State-to-State (StS) analysis is incorporated into the population distribution. Because this correction is constructed from the quasi-steady-state (QSS) distribution, the resulting model is valid only for systems and conditions under which the QSS assumption holds. The proposed 1-bin 3T model is validated across a broad range of zero-dimensional test cases through comparisons with high-fidelity StS simulations and Direct Molecular Simulations (DMS). The results demonstrate excellent agreement between the reduced-order model and high-fidelity approaches for both dissociating and recombining environments. Overall, the 1-bin 3T model shows strong potential as an efficient and accurate framework for modeling non-equilibrium thermochemical behavior, while keeping computational costs orders of magnitude lower than the high fidelity ro-vibrational StS simulations.

papers.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
papers.abstract: Sparse outcome rewards make it difficult for long-horizon language-model agents to assign credit to earlier actions. Learned critics provide value estimates for intermediate states, but these estimates can be inaccurate, while estimating intermediate values with repetitive continuation samples from points within a trajectory incurs substantial costs. To mitigate these issues, we introduce FOCUS, an RL method that uses selective branching to help the critic network learn its value estimator. The rollout controller facilitates active learning for the critic by sampling continuations from states that are expected to most reduce the critic's estimation error. These refined value estimates then score the segment between consecutive states with a TD($λ$) advantage, while the sampled evidence supplies training targets for the critic. FOCUS supports long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning through a modular context-management interface that decouples context management from rollout allocation. Our experiments show that using compaction-induced segment boundaries for value estimation and credit assignment, FOCUS outperforms GRPO and VinePPO with matched per-step generation budgets on legal reasoning, deep search, and code localization benchmarks, improving held-out accuracy at Qwen3.5-9B scale by 7.2 points over the strongest baseline on BrowseComp-Plus (55.4 vs. 48.2) and by 4.1 points on DeonticBench (56.5 vs. 52.4).

papers.title: Game theory of academic effort and hiring in the age of AI
papers.abstract: Many academic disciplines (in particular, mathematics and the theoretical sciences) face difficult questions about how to adapt their practices to the rise of highly capable artificial intelligence (AI). Before AI, a well-written research paper with a strong theoretical result acted as a reliable signal that its authors understood their field in depth. Now that AI is widely accessible, such signals have become cheaper to produce. As a result, they no longer reliably sort academics by their level of understanding. This has direct consequences for academic hiring. The age of AI raises a question for each side of the academic job market. Should an early-career researcher invest in a deep understanding of their field, or instead use AI to build a longer resume with many papers? Should a recruiter favor applicants with fewer papers who pass an interview aimed at probing understanding, or insist on both publication volume and a pass? In this paper, we develop a game-theoretic model of this two-sided dilemma. We classify all pure-strategy equilibria that can arise in this game and use learning simulations to identify the behaviors that populations of applicants and recruiters may learn to adopt. Our analysis provides a framework for reasoning about how academic hiring can adapt to AI and for evaluating practices that preserve the value of deep understanding.

papers.title: Third harmonic generation in the transition metal trichalcogenides
papers.abstract: The transition metal trichalcogenides (TMTs) are an interesting class of layered 2D materials that have strong anisotropic electrical and optical properties. We report on the polarization-dependent nonlinear optical response of exfoliated crystals at the third harmonic using non-resonant excitation with a 1560 nm femtosecond laser. All members of the TMT crystal family explored (ZrS3, HfS3, TiS3, and NbS3) display large anisotropy in their polarized third harmonic generation signal, with anisotropy ratios as large as chi_11/chi_22 ~ 6.5. From the expected nonlinear dependence of these monoclinic and triclinic crystals we extract the relative nonlinear susceptibility coefficients. We find that the anisotropy ratio is largest for ZrS3 and decreases across the family, a trend we associate with the proximity of the third harmonic energy to the strongly b-polarized absorption edge of each material. NbS3, the only triclinic crystal, displays a pronounced anisotropy in thick flakes that is strongly reduced in the thinnest flakes, which we attribute to a partial relaxation of the Peierls-type Nb-Nb dimerization that underlies the triclinic distortion. The large anisotropic nonlinear response in this crystal family sets it apart from other 2D materials and makes it particularly attractive for further investigation.

papers.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) can generate multiple tokens in parallel, but often require many decoding rounds to complete a response. Efficient generation depends not only on which tokens are easy to predict, but also on how committing to them helps predict the remaining positions. A highly predictable token may provide little useful context, while revealing a less predictable token can help several other positions become predictable sooner. We propose dSpark, a new schedule distillation-based framework for learning when to commit tokens for faster diffusion language generation. To achieve this, we construct unmasking schedules that prioritize tokens whose reveal makes other positions easier to predict, reducing uncertainty earlier in decoding. We then distill these schedules into the model to enable faster parallel sampling, with a KL-divergence regularizer to help preserve generation quality. We extensively evaluate our approach across mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks. On GSM8K, our method achieves remarkable 10.12$\times$ and 5.12$\times$ speedups over the various baselines on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-7B-Instruct, respectively, while maintaining superior task performance. Our code is available at https://github.com/VILA-Lab/dSpark.

papers.title: Anchored Stein Variational Gradient Descent Algorithm for Non-smooth Sampling
papers.abstract: We introduce a Stein variational framework for sampling from a target density $p\propto e^{-U}$ when the target potential $U$ is possibly non-smooth. The key idea is to introduce a smoother reference potential $U_0$ and the anchor weight $a=e^{U-U_0}$. The resulting anchored Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD) algorithm is able to target $p\propto e^{-U}$ without computing the gradient of $U$ and include standard SVGD as a special case. In particular, we allow the target potential $U$ to be locally Lipschitz while the reference potential $U_0$ is continuously differentiable, along with other suitable assumptions. Under this low regularity regime, we establish a Kullback-Leibler first variation formula for anchored perturbations, identify the corresponding steepest descent direction in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space and prove a nonasymptotic convergence bound for the anchored SVGD algorithm in terms of an anchored kernelized Stein discrepancy. Finally, we also provide guidance on constructing a suitable reference potential $U_0$ based on $U$.

papers.title: The Impact of Flyby Interactions on the Rotation of Open Clusters
papers.abstract: The Gaia astrometric mission has provided the first evidence for the bulk rotation of open clusters. While this rotation may arise from residual spin inherited from a cluster's parent molecular cloud, it is unclear whether this explanation always suffices, as angular momentum is carried away by escaping stars on the timescale of two-body relaxation. In particular, the recent observance of significant rotation ($v_{\rm rot} = 0.81 \pm 0.06$ km s$^{-1}$) in the dynamically old ($\approx 4$ Gyr) open cluster M67 motivates a study of another potential source of spin for Solar neighborhood clusters: tidal torquing from gravitational encounters with passing giant molecular clouds (GMCs). We derive an analytic estimate for the change in angular momentum of a cluster due to an impulsive interaction with a passing GMC, and verify this expectation by performing $N$-body simulations over a range of encounter parameters using REBOUND. For highly energetic encounters, significant angular momentum can be transferred, but the stars that receive the most angular momentum are ejected, leaving the cluster remnant with negligible net rotation. Even when considering a random walk of many GMC-cluster encounters, the integrated effects of these interactions cannot explain observations of dynamically old rotating open clusters. However, we find that within $\sim 5$ Myr post-encounter, some disrupted clusters could be confused as rotating clusters while their stars are still dispersing. Using the local density of GMCs, we estimate that up to $\approx 1\%$ of open clusters in the Milky Way may carry this faux-rotation signal.

papers.title: Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models such as VGGT regress cameras and geometry in a single forward pass, but they report no uncertainty for the camera poses they predict: an incorrect relative pose looks no different from a correct one. We ask whether the frozen model nonetheless knows when its pose is wrong. On HardMatch, a benchmark of 1,000 deliberately difficult image pairs on which VGGT fails on 35% of pairs, a linear probe on VGGT's frozen features predicts pose failure on held-out categories with ROC-AUC 93.5%, compared with 79.7% for VGGT's own point-map confidence and 77.7% for a classifier trained on all of VGGT's outputs. The probe catches failures VGGT is confident about, lets a downstream system abstain on the pairs it distrusts, and transfers without retraining to rotation failures on PhotoTourism and ScanNet-1500, beyond what co-visibility explains. This knowledge is absent from the per-image encoder: it is computed partway through the layers that fuse the two views, and the same holds for a second model, $π^3$. In essence, we find that VGGT knows more about its own failures than it reports.

papers.title: Causal DAG-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Physical Activity Maintenance: Using Prior Data to Inform Future Deployment
papers.abstract: Digital health interventions can provide scalable, personalized support for physical activity (PA), yet sustaining PA over the long-term remains difficult. Because affective experiences with PA are important for activity sustainment, we developed an online reinforcement learning (RL) system for the forthcoming ADAPT factorial trial that personalizes twice-daily activity suggestions aimed at improving affective associations with PA. This setting poses several challenges: participant-specific data are scarce relative to the candidate state space, important states and rewards are partially observed, interventions are frequent while the primary outcome is measured weekly, and activity suggestions can both improve PA-related experiences and increase intervention burden. We address these challenges using an expert-specified causal directed acyclic graph as an integrated RL design tool, guiding state construction, estimation of partially observed states, delayed credit assignment, and representation of beneficial and adverse intervention pathways. We further construct a longitudinal simulator calibrated from a prior micro-randomized trial to compare candidate RL designs under realistic state evolution, missingness, and participant heterogeneity before deployment. Together, this work illustrates how causal domain knowledge and prior trial data can make long-horizon, participant-specific RL more practical for digital health interventions targeting sustained behavior change.

papers.title: Characterising canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We study Brantner-Taelman's canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties and characterise their (quasi)canonical lifts in terms of rational $p$-adic Hodge theoretic data. We also show that these canonical lifts need not be of CM type and that the associated local Galois representations need not split as sums of twists of unramified representations, in contrast to classical results for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces.

papers.title: Exploratory creative pre-ranking: Hierarchical empirical-Bayes Thompson sampling for real-time creative optimization
papers.abstract: Dynamic creative optimization decides which creative of an ad to render for each request. Recent work places that choice before ad ranking, but relies on deterministic point predictors with no calibrated uncertainty. AI-generated content has made creatives nearly free, while feedback per creative remains sparse and selection faces a tight latency budget. We introduce a creative pre-ranker that scores every recalled creative and shortlists each campaign's pool before the per-user ranker runs. Creatives sit in a hierarchy of audience segment, advertised item, campaign and creative, so a cold creative falls back on what its parent levels have earned, and how much it borrows from its parents is set in closed form from historical logs, with one parameter per level and nothing tuned. To stay within the latency budget, the pre-ranker predicts for an audience segment rather than an individual user, from per-attribute counters. It selects by a single Thompson draw per creative, balancing exploration and exploitation so that a new creative still has a chance to be learned. Replaying Roblox Sponsored-ads traffic over campaigns with competing creatives, the shortlist lifts predicted play-through rate by 8.14% against 2.80% for an equally sized random shortlist, forwards more than 40% fewer creatives than the full pool, and adds only 0.2% to serving time. After an A/B test on live traffic, the method now serves in production at Roblox.

papers.title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations
papers.abstract: We establish operator universality at the spectral edge of general Wigner matrices by showing that their suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations, constructed from deterministic initial vectors, converge to the stochastic Airy operator with Dirichlet boundary condition. The result requires control of the entire tridiagonal structure on the scale relevant to the limiting differential operator. The Lanczos coefficients for non-Gaussian Wigner matrices are strongly dependent. We analyze their fluctuations by combining multi-resolvent local laws with quantitative control of Krylov subspaces and a comparison of the resulting Jacobi coefficients with those of the Gaussian ensembles. This approach identifies the limiting Brownian potential directly from the original matrix entries, without invoking Dyson Brownian motion in the step of Green function comparison. The resolvent limit yields joint convergence of edge eigenvalues, embedded eigenfunctions, and spectral measures. For Gaussian, Laguerre and circular $β$-ensembles we construct sharp couplings to the stochastic Airy, Bessel and Sine operators, preserving the finite-matrix laws. For fixed $β> 0$, their squared Hilbert-Schmidt inverse errors have almost-sure orders $n^{-1/3}, n^{-1}$ and $n^{-1}$, respectively, with $a > 0$ in the hard-edge upper bound. We also identify the positive leading order coefficient for the circular ensemble, whose second derivative jumps at $β= 2$.

papers.title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures
papers.abstract: We announce a structure theory for measures on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic distance. Our results include a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability by Jones square functions, and sharp results for $L^p$ beta numbers. The results hold in every parabolic dimension and extend the theories of Edelen--Naber--Valtorta, Azzam--Tolsa and David--Semmes to space-time. The stated theorems and corollaries, together with their proofs, are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: A Robust, Explainable, and Efficient Deep Metric for Speech and General Audio Quality
papers.abstract: We present a robust Speech and Audio Quality Metric (SAQM) that merges features of traditional quality metrics with a CNN trained on a large amount of data using contrastive learning methods. To overcome the problem of limited amounts of human-labeled training data, we propose two pretraining strategies relying on pseudo-labels. One uses an established objective metric PEAQ-2f (based on ITU-R BS.1387) as surrogate loss, the other is based on contrasting a wide range of coding modes by a rule-of-thumb ordering based on expected perceived quality. As a key novelty, our approach lets us generate saliency maps by propagating gradients to identify which feature has the greatest impact on the final metric outcome and enables our system to provide insights regarding the type and extent of distortions present in the tested audio signal. The resulting (SAQM) operates at low computational complexity, performs comparably to (SOTA) metrics on speech while still performing well on general audio content.

papers.title: Data-Driven Stochastic Control of Delayed Air-Conditioning Systems
papers.abstract: We consider a stochastic optimal control problem arising in the operation of industrial air-conditioning systems with delayed activation effects. The delayed transition between inactive and operational regimes induces a non-Markovian structure in the controlled dynamics. We derive a regression-based discrete dynamic programming algorithm on nested state-control grids. We give a probabilistic proof of convergence of the idealized time-discrete dynamic programming problem to the continuous-time value function. Numerical experiments based on calibrated multidimensional forecast-tracking Ornstein--Uhlenbeck models illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

papers.title: Properly embedded Legendrian surfaces in the tangent sphere bundle of hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: We show that every open Riemann surface may be conformally properly embedded in the tangent sphere bundle of hyperbolic $3$-space as a Legendrian surface. We achieve this by constructing proper holomorphic Legendrian embeddings in $\mathrm{SL}_2 (\mathbb{C})$ whose projections to the quotient $\mathrm{SL}_2 (\mathbb{C})/ \mathrm{U}_1$ remain embeddings. As another consequence, every open Riemann surface admits a proper holomorphic Legendrian embedding in the projectivised special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_2 (\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: World Model for Energy Efficiency Maximization in Dynamic Metasurface Antennas
papers.abstract: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) have emerged as a promising technology for realizing large-scale antenna arrays in next-generation wireless networks owing to their ability to enable dense and energy-efficient antenna architectures. However, jointly optimizing digital beamforming and DMA element weights under time-varying channel conditions remains challenging due to their coupled effects on the received signal and interference powers. We formulate this problem to maximize time-averaged energy efficiency (EE) under time-varying channel conditions, subject to transmit power constraints, Lorentzian phase limitations, and minimum rate requirements. To enable long-term planning and improve sample efficiency compared with model-free reinforcement learning, we develop a world model framework that learns latent system dynamics from interactions with the environment and jointly optimizes digital beamforming and DMA element weights through imagined trajectories. Furthermore, we incorporate feasibility-preserving action mappings and safety cost signals to ensure constraint satisfaction during policy learning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves the time-averaged EE by approximately 20% compared with the deep Q-network baseline, while achieving higher sample efficiency and more reliable constraint satisfaction.

papers.title: The fate of $s_{\pm}$ superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent measurement of high-temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate system La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ in the bulk as well as thin film samples, we seek to understand the role of the interlayer coupling in this system in dictating the pairing symmetry. Many proposals posit the existence of an $s_\pm$ superconducting phase in close competition with the mroe conventional cuprate-like $d$-wave state in both weak- and strong-coupling theories. However, at least in the latter, the effects of Coulomb repulsion and the double occupancy constraint have been largely neglected. In this manuscript, we propose a mean-field fractionalization treatment that captures the full $SU(2)$ particle-hole symmetry of the t-J model at half-filling, and show how a systematic treatment of this new symmetry leads to an added Coulomb pseudopotential constraint - one that is absent in the usual $U(1)$ treatment. We then apply this new fractionalization scheme to a simplified bilayer t-J model of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, showing how the Coulomb pseudopotential suppresses the existence of $s_\pm$ symmetry in favor of $d$-wave pairing.

papers.title: Security Region Compression via Hybrid Vertex Pruning for Enhanced Computational Efficiency
papers.abstract: The security region (SR) specifies a joint feasible region in the operational space involving various installations within the power system. It enables dynamic allocation of capacity among these energy units, thereby unlocking additional grid potential for power delivery and mitigating congestion. By constructing a convex hull from a set of vertices to form a polytope, the SR can be effectively represented with an acceptable accuracy loss. However, the SR computation inevitably generates many low-quality vertices, which contribute little to the overall hypervolume and can be discarded. By introducing SR compression, the SR data size can be reduced, which in turn facilitates the memory-efficient computation of SR and time-efficient solution of SR-related optimization problems. Accordingly, this paper proposes a vertex pruning approach that mixes local and backward search policies to achieve effective SR compression. In particular, the backward search strategy allows previously pruned vertices to be recycled when they are re-identified as critical. Subsequently, we incorporate this approach to enhance computational efficiency in the aforementioned applications. Numerical validations are conducted on two realistic medium-voltage Dutch grid cases. The results demonstrate at most 1.65% hypervolume loss with over 96.0\% SR data size reduction after applying the proposed compression approach. Empowered by this compression, the 8-dimensional (8D) SR becomes computationally tractable. Moreover, in relevant grid-aware computation challenges, the solving time can be reduced by at least 52.9% with at most an 1.36% optimality loss. All above validate both the efficacy and values of the proposed SR compression approach.

papers.title: Multimodal Concert Video Editing: System Design and Exploratory Evaluation
papers.abstract: Editing multi-camera concerts requires coordinated decisions about musical relevance, visual quality and cut timing. We present a modular framework that combines instrument activity from multitrack audio, visible instruments and image sharpness with beat-based timing and probabilistic camera selection. An interpretable scoring model links these components to the choice of views over complete shot intervals. Component tests and an exploratory expert study on a four-camera concert yield mixed assessments across the editing variants. The findings motivate extending local audiovisual relevance with contextual and sequence-level criteria. The architecture provides a basis for testing these extensions and studying how component behaviour affects the quality of complete edits.

papers.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization for Agentic Robotics
papers.abstract: Frontier models such as GPT-6 Astra now directly control robots and can generalize better than vision-language-action models (VLAs). We argue that this ability could arise from two distinct, composable skills: semantic reasoning, to understand what a task asks for in a scene, and motion control, to move the robot to do it. We show that small open VLMs are already capable of the first and mainly lack the second. We introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches this missing motion skill, entirely in simulation on simple primitive tasks and from the model's own successes, with no frontier teacher or distillation and no real-world robot data. ZAP reaches 96.7% success on real-world tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra in our harness while running 3x faster and 17x cheaper, and 74.0% on a bimanual adaptation of RoboLab-120, on par with GPT-6 Astra's 72.2%. ZAP also generalizes to new objects, goals, and strategies, and in simulation to a robot embodiment on which it never trained.

papers.title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
papers.abstract: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, mostly on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which also implement global symmetries and their anomalies consistently, but allow the high-energy behavior to better match real QCD.

papers.title: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of $C_n^r$ for even $n$: rigid sequences, products, and growth beyond Harborth's bound
papers.abstract: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of $C_n^r$ and $η(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant. For even $n$, Harborth's construction gives $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+1$, with equality when $n$ is a power of two. Wang and Zeng recently showed that this bound is strict for every $r\ge4$ and every even $n$ that is not a power of two, with an excess of $2^{r-3}(m-1)$, where $m$ is the odd part of $n$; this disproves Properties C and D. We show that the excess grows faster than $2^r$. For every even $n=2^am$ with odd $m\ge3$ and every $r\ge4$, \[ s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+(m-1)\,2^{r-3}\lfloor r/4\rfloor+1 , \] so that $s(C_n^r)-2^r(n-1)\ge c_n\,r\,2^r$.

papers.title: Morse index characterization of the Veronese projective plane
papers.abstract: Following Simons' seminal work in 1968, every closed, connected, embedded minimal surface in the four-sphere that is not totally geodesic has Morse index at least five. In this paper, we prove that equality holds if and only if the surface is congruent to the Veronese projective plane. Relying on recent advances by Bernstein and Ketover, this characterization settles Kusner's 1996 conjecture on the minimizers of the Willmore functional in dimension four for surfaces whose normal bundle has nonzero Euler number. This is always the case, in particular, for embeddings of nonorientable surfaces whose orientation double cover has even genus.

papers.title: A uniform improvement to conformal risk control via a generalization of e-closure
papers.abstract: We extend the recently introduced e-closure principle for multiple testing to general state and action spaces and to arbitrary, including continuously indexed, families of risks. A collection of e-values indexed by states and risks certifies a menu of actions, and every data-dependent selection from this menu controls each expected loss at its prescribed level. Conversely, every valid procedure is certified by its own normalized losses, which often leave part of the risk budget unused. We introduce a method called recertification, which spends this unused budget. Using known distributional structure, it enlarges the certifying e-values while preserving validity and selects a less conservative action from the enlarged menu. One particularly compelling application is to the popular framework of conformal risk control (CRC) with a known loss family. Here, recertification redistributes unused risk budget among the held-out points of each hypothetical augmented sample. The resulting controller is valid under every finite exchangeable law and less (usually strictly) conservative than CRC. For convex losses on an interval of actions, repeated recertification converges geometrically to an admissible controller. As a second example involving false discovery rate control with e-values, recertifying randomized e-BH yields a closed-form procedure that rejects a superset of randomized e-BH for every realization of the randomization and maximizes the expected number of rejections under the same constraints. Recertifying with the larger e-collection of closed e-BH gives a second closed-form procedure that rejects a superset of the first. Experiments on CIFAR-100 hierarchical classification and simulations demonstrate improved budget utilization and gains in informativeness and power over the corresponding baselines.

papers.title: Hidden Singularity and Fractal Dimensions for Extended Harper Operators
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every irrational frequency, the spectra of the extended Harper family throughout the zero-measure regime have finite $1/2$-dimensional Hausdorff measure and lower box dimension at most $1/2$. Both numbers improve to $1/3$ on the isotropic critical boundary. The proof is based on a family of unitary transformations, that specializes to the chiral transform of [BJK] for the case of the critical almost Mathieu. This family allows to make every operator in this regime spectrally equivalent to a singular Jacobi operator. Using these singular representatives, we apply the method of [BJK] to construct covers by $O(q_n)$ intervals of total length $O(q_n^{-1})$, improving to $O(q_n^{-2})$ on the isotropic boundary, where $q_n$ is the denominator of a canonical approximant to $α$. The covers give upper box bounds and, with packing estimates, examples where the box-counting dimension fails to exist.

papers.title: Parameter-Decoupled Superresolution with Airy-Disk-Informed Learning: Application to NGC 4486B
papers.abstract: Estimating the separation of two unresolved or nearly unresolved sources from recorded intensity images is difficult when source brightness, mutual coherence, and phase are unknown and the point-spread function (PSF) departs from a Gaussian. We formulate Hermite--Gaussian (HG) projections of one- and two-dimensional Airy amplitudes and prove that ratios of mode probabilities with equal longitudinal parity exactly cancel the brightness, coherence, and phase nuisance parameters under a symmetric two-source model. For a one-dimensional Airy slice we achieve an explicit multi-ratio separation inversion. For the physical two-dimensional circular-pupil PSF we obtain exact finite-pupil overlap integrals and locally invertible separation responses. Motivated by these analytical invariants, we examine Airy-informed convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on synthetic Airy images with known separations. At 150,000 training images, the approximate mean absolute errors are 0.018 in plotted separation units, 10 times better comparing to 0.18 for non-Airy Gaussian PSF approximation. Applied to an archival Hubble Space Telescope image of the double nucleus of NGC 4486B, the Airy-informed CNN gives estimates of approximately 9.6--12.0 pc for training sets of 100,000--150,000 images, broadly consistent with the historical approximately 12 pc value. We distinguish exact optical-mode nuisance cancellation from empirical robustness of an image-only learned estimator and identify the limits imposed by PSF mismatch and extended galaxy structure.

papers.title: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
papers.abstract: Browser agents do not just need more practice. They need to practice the right things. We introduce MiniWeb, a realistic miniature of the web comprising 65 interconnected websites across 15 domains, where agents navigate, search, and transact as people do. Its 369 human-annotated tasks cover everyday workflows and label 37 reusable interaction primitives grouped into 7 skill families, allowing us to diagnose which skills fail rather than only whether a task succeeds. Benchmarking ten open-weight agents, we find that drag & gesture is consistently the weakest family, with no agent solving more than 24% of its instances. To address this gap, we introduce MiniWebGen, a framework that autonomously generates verified, skill-centric training data from MiniWeb. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-4B on just 3.1K verified trajectories improves single-primitive success by 24.9pp across 13 unseen websites, with gains across every skill family. However, these trajectories teach short-horizon interactions, which do not directly translate to full-task success. We build on this result with MiniWebAgent, which pairs the trained executor with a planner that decomposes full tasks into the skill-level steps it learned to perform. This approach improves task success by 19.4pp points on unseen MiniWeb sites and transfers to external benchmarks, with gains of 9.3pp on WebArena-Lite, 16.1pp on Online-Mind2Web, and 20.0pp on WebVoyager, without training on their trajectories. We provide a simple recipe for compact browser agents: practice reusable skills directly, then compose them to solve unfamiliar tasks.

papers.title: Learning and Reasoning with Geometry: How Generation Helps Spatial Understanding
papers.abstract: Image and video generators can produce spatially consistent visual content, but how to use this capability to improve spatial understanding remains underexplored. We study this problem from two perspectives: geometric supervision during training and explicit geometric evidence during inference. To this end, we introduce a unified geometric understanding and generation model (GeoUG) that integrates depth and multi-view generation with spatial understanding. First, we design a multi-scale depth codec that enables metric-depth generation using a pretrained visual autoencoder, and show that joint training yields task-dependent gains in spatial understanding. Second, we introduce 3DCueBench to control geometric difficulty while balancing selected 2D cues, and find that generated depth provides larger reasoning gains on questions requiring fine-grained geometric discrimination. Building on this finding, we develop adaptive interleaved reasoning, in which GeoUG first drafts an answer and then decides whether to generate geometric evidence to confirm or revise it. We train this decision through reinforcement learning, balancing accuracy gains over retaining the draft against generation cost. GeoUG achieves circular accuracies of 97.9%, 90.8%, and 94.2% on CV-Bench-3D, 3DCueBench, and DA-2K with fewer generation calls than always generating.

papers.title: Sparse Carleman Embeddings for Nonlinear Discrete Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Discrete nonlinear dynamical systems arise in population models, iterative optimization, and numerical simulations, where computing many iterations can be costly in high dimensions. We study Carleman embedding for forced quadratic discrete systems and its application to quantum state preparation. Under explicit stability and initial-state assumptions, we prove that the truncation error decreases geometrically with the embedding degree, uniformly over all iterations. A central obstacle in discrete time is that the lifted update can become dense even when the original coefficient maps are sparse. We overcome this obstacle by constructing an exact auxiliary linear-system representation that applies the coefficient maps one tensor factor at a time, with row and column sparsities bounded independently of the truncation degree. After rescaling, the associated history system has a condition number that grows linearly with the iteration count, uniformly in the truncation degree. These results yield a quantum algorithm for preparing an approximation to the normalized $n$th iterate with constant success probability. Under coherent input-access assumptions, and for fixed sparsity, stability parameters, and a known positive lower bound on the final-state norm, the oracle query complexity is linear in $n$ and polylogarithmic in the inverse accuracy. Numerical experiments in one and three dimensions illustrate the convergence of the truncated embedding.

papers.title: Spectroscopic Survey of Small Solar System Bodies with Ariel
papers.abstract: The small Solar System bodies (SSSBs) preserve records of the formation and evolution of the Solar System. In particular, the near-infrared wavelength region around 3 $μ$m provides crucial insights into the origin and transport of hydrated materials and organics, although it is difficult to observe from the ground because of strong telluric absorption. We assess the observability of SSSBs as complementary science to the ESA Ariel space mission, operating in the visible to mid-infrared wavelength range (0.5--7.8 $μ$m). Using the NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris system, we evaluate the visibility of known SSSBs from 2032 to 2035. Our analysis shows that Ariel can spectroscopically characterize up to 402 unique SSSBs under a conservative limiting visual magnitude of $V=13.6$. If observations can be extended to somewhat fainter targets ($V=16$), the number of observable SSSBs could increase to 2144. Assuming operational scenarios in which one SSSB is observed every 3, 7, or 30 days over a four-year mission, the total numbers of observable targets would be 357, 209, and 49, respectively. We further model the spectral energy distributions of candidate targets to evaluate their observational performance. We demonstrate that Ariel can resolve critical absorption features, such as those at 2.7 $μ$m and 3.4 $μ$m, with a higher spectral resolution than the previous infrared survey with AKARI. Observations of SSSBs with Ariel can provide insights into the distribution and evolution of life-forming materials in the Solar System and constitute a scientifically compelling component of Ariel's complementary science program.

papers.title: Understanding Jev-Style System One Models: Does Structure Reduce Selection Bias?
papers.abstract: Selection bias in large language models (LLMs) can persist despite instructions to ignore presentation order or prompts that elicit reasoning. Recent efforts to reproduce Jev-style System One behavior have produced a growing family of models that predict probabilities directly over supplied candidates. Yet systematic comparisons of selection bias across Jev versions, Jev reproductions, and generative LLMs remain limited in multi-option tasks. This leaves a central question: does Jev-style decision structure reduce selection bias? We address this question with a simple test that shuffles options while keeping question and candidate content fixed. Across two Jev versions, twelve Jev reproductions, and six generative LLMs, we trace individual answers through eight presentations and compare them with fixed-order repetition. On our primary collection of 1,700 questions from two benchmarks, Jev's accuracy varies by less than two percentage points, yet its cumulative failure set expands by 27.3-28.5% relative to the original order, with first failures continuing into the final presentation. Reordering loses substantially more initial successes than fixed-order repetition, a gap that also appears in highly repeatable Jev reproductions. Nor does Jev show a general advantage over the LLM baselines in preserving correct choices. Aggregation offers limited protection: voting yields modest gains for Jev, while even unanimous answers are frequently wrong. These results expose a gap between repeatable decisions and decisions that remain correct across equivalent presentations, showing why stable accuracy alone cannot establish resistance to selection bias.

papers.title: Seeing Through Distractions: Context-Stable Attribution via the Least Core
papers.abstract: Shapley-value-based explanations are widely used for feature attribution in machine learning. However, in computer vision, a feature may reduce the target-class score when added to the complete genuine image, even when the predicted label remains unchanged. We formalize such features as contextual distractors and investigate their attributions under semivalues and the least core. Under a weak average marginal monotonicity assumption, we derive quantitative semivalue--least-core gap bounds and sufficient conditions based on the probability of sampling smaller contexts. We further show that shifting semivalue weights toward larger contexts decreases the signed gap. Finally, controlled image-classification experiments and evaluations on Salient ImageNet provide strong empirical support for our theoretical findings.

papers.title: Interference-induced dynamical crossovers in quantum walks on disordered square lattices
papers.abstract: We study discrete-time quantum walks with Fourier, Grover, and Hadamard coin operators on disordered square lattices, alongside classical random walks. Edges in the lattice are absent with a probability, $p$. In this case, both classical and quantum walks exhibit an essentially identical degradation of transport. We then study a general version of this model, in which the existing edges are retained. However, the absent edges are no longer absent, but now become partially transmitting, with a transmission coefficient $f$. We find that the response is now quite sensitive to the walk protocol and coin symmetry. The classical walk exhibits asymptotic stability of the anomalous diffusion exponent, $β(t)$. In comparison, quantum walks exhibit a monotonically decaying $β(t)$ beyond the initial transient regime, leading to the absence of quantum diffusion in two dimensions. We map the transport regimes in the $(f,p)$ plane and identify the contour for $β=1$, which separates the subdiffusive and superdiffusive regimes. We also examine the effective diffusion coefficient, the inverse participation ratio, and the first two moments of edge transmission. We restrict ourselves to analyzing bulk propagation prior to finite-size boundary reflections. The results indicate that quantum transport depends significantly on coin-specific interference and cannot be fully described by transmission statistics alone.

papers.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: A vulnerability costs more to fix the later it is discovered. As coding agents generate code faster than developers can review it, software needs a first line of defense screening each new function in real time. LLM agents have recently become capable of finding real-world vulnerabilities by working as a security expert would: they run analysis tools, explore the surrounding code, test hypotheses and weigh the evidence before forming their own judgement. This reasoning, however, spans many model calls, so that each verdict takes minutes of compute, far too long for real-time screening. Faster detectors, which fine-tune deep learning models or prompt an LLM for a direct verdict, are less accurate: they judge a function without the context an agent gathers, and an LLM's generated verdict is unreliable even when given some of it. We present REVA (REal-time Vulnerability Analysis), an AI vulnerability detector that brings the security context and code understanding components behind agentic detectors into a single forward pass of an LLM. For each new function, REVA gives the LLM a pre-computed threat model of its module, lightweight static analysis findings and call-graph information. REVA leverages a trained probe to read the LLM's internal representations of the new function in this context. On PrimeVul's held-out test set, REVA on GLM-5.3-Flash reaches 60.0% accuracy in about one second per function. This matches VulTriage (59.2%), the state-of-the-art agentic detector, run on the same LLM, while being over 250 times faster and less than a tenth as costly. On the same prompt, the probe is 14% to 17% more accurate than the LLM's own direct verdict. Across three open LLMs, REVA is at least as accurate as VulTriage, and about 10% more accurate on two of them. An LLM's internal representations thus encode much of what agentic detectors obtain through reasoning.

papers.title: Improved lattice-packing bounds in small dimensions
papers.abstract: We strengthen the upper bound on the density of a lattice packing in small dimensions. A lattice cannot have too many short vectors; we modify the Cohn--Elkies linear program accordingly by allowing the auxiliary function to be positive on a short interval beyond the minimum distance. For $11 \leq n \leq 16$, our bound is tighter than the three-point bound of Cohn, de Laat and Salmon. For $n \in [17, 23] \cup [25, 40] \cup [43, 57] \cup [62, 75]\cup [83, 91]$, our bound lies below the published numerical values of the Cohn--Elkies bound.

papers.title: AI in Econometric Theory: An Example
papers.abstract: This note contains a story and a paper. The paper is about the admissibility of two-stage least squares with weak instruments, a topic we have worked on together since 2019. The story is about how we (or, rather, our LLMs) wrote the paper, and some thoughts on what this may mean for our field.

papers.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
papers.abstract: Frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can control robots without robot-specific training, but how their capabilities compare and interact with post-trained vision-language-action (VLA) and world action model (WAM) policies across manipulation demands remains to be thoroughly evaluated. In this report, we evaluate GPT-6-Astra on EBench as the core of an agent that controls a robot through an agent harness under the same visual and proprioceptive observation protocol as post-trained policies. We study two agent configurations: direct control, in which the agent generates waypoint commands directly, and harness with policy, in which it can also invoke a post-trained VLA or WAM policy for action execution. Under direct control, the agent achieves competitive overall performance relative to post-trained policies. It leads on short-horizon tasks and exhibits the least performance variation across generalization dimensions, whereas it underperforms post-trained policies on long-horizon tasks, tabletop manipulation, and high-precision contact-rich tasks. In the harness with policy, invoking a post-trained VLA or WAM combines the complementary strengths of both components, raising overall task success to the level of the strongest compared post-trained policies while substantially reducing token cost. However, performance remains below the per-task upper bound of the standalone components due to suboptimal policy invocation, fixed-instruction execution without subgoals, and grasp disruption when the agent resumes control. Overall, our study characterizes the capability boundary of a frontier MLLM agent and suggests directions for improving future agent harness design. Project page: https://internrobotics.github.io/EBench-Astra-Tech-Report/

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation With Heterogeneous Client Quantization
papers.abstract: In federated learning (FL), secure aggregation enables a server to compute the sum of local model updates of $N$ clients, without revealing any information on the individual model updates to the server, beyond their sum. Different clients may be subject to heterogeneous bandwidth constraints, and consequently may choose different numbers of quantization levels to represent the information they send. Most secure aggregation works require the clients to project the values of their update parameters to a common finite group (or field), which does not directly accommodate heterogeneous precision constraints on their transmitted masked updates. Existing approaches of secure aggregation with heterogeneous quantization levels reveal partial aggregates of model-updates, and can reveal segments of individual model updates, under certain dropout and client-server collusion patterns. To prevent this privacy breach, we propose an information-theoretic secure aggregation scheme that tolerates client drop-outs, and up to $T$ semi-honest clients that collude with each other and with the server, under heterogeneous quantization at clients. Our protocol utilizes the $(T+1, N)$ threshold black-box secret sharing construction, where secret shares of the client updates, despite belonging to distinct algebraic groups owing to different quantization, are generated from identical linear integer systems.

papers.title: Attainable forms of intermediate dimensions of complementary sets
papers.abstract: Given a positive, non-increasing sequence $a$ with sum $1$, we consider the family $\mathcal{C}_a$ of closed subsets of $[0,1]$ whose complementary open intervals have lengths given by the terms of $a$. We study which functions $θ\mapsto\overline{\dim}_{\,θ}E$ arise as the upper intermediate dimensions of sets $E\in\mathcal{C}_a$. Under a natural condition on the decay of $a$, we show that these are exactly the functions in the class introduced by Banaji and Rutar that take the value $\overline{\dim}_{\rm B}C_a$ at $θ=1$ and are bounded above by the upper intermediate dimensions of the decreasing Cantor set $C_a$. We also show that the lower bound given by the countable set $D_a$ is rigid: if it is attained at one value of $θ$, then it is attained at all larger values.

papers.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
papers.abstract: Human oversight is a pillar of AI safety. It is often exercised by a human in the loop (HITL) who approves critical actions taken by an AI agent. AI agents' increasing ability to bypass guardrails, though, raises the question of how to enforce HITL robustly. We introduce the concept of inalienable human-in-the-loop (I-HITL). An I-HITL protocol ensures that an agent can initiate an action only with explicit human approval, even when the human interacts with a system (e.g., a local agentic harness) compromised by the agent. A strong I-HITL protocol additionally ensures such approval even when an adversarial human attempts to delegate approvals to an agent. To motivate I-HITL, we report on experiments with a popular agentic wallet platform in which raising an agent's spending cap requires HITL approval via emailed one-time passcodes (OTPs). Given access to the user's email and a task blocked by the cap, we find that ten different frontier models will often autonomously raise the cap, harvesting OTPs to bypass a HITL guardrail and surfacing other vulnerabilities. We formally define I-HITL using the concept of communication topologies and prove necessary and sufficient conditions for its realization. We show that an I-HITL protocol requires a trusted entity - a trusted computing device (or equivalent) - and characterize which such devices can and cannot realize an I-HITL protocol. We present a prototype I-HITL system called Countersign that can plug into and strengthen existing HITL systems using off-the-shelf consumer mobile devices.

papers.title: Characteristic gluing to extremal Kerr horizons and the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum
papers.abstract: We prove a non-perturbative, non-axisymmetric characteristic gluing theorem for the Einstein vacuum equations: every Boyer-Lindquist sphere in the domain of outer communication of a Kerr black hole, in particular every symmetry sphere of a Schwarzschild exterior, can be glued along a single outgoing null hypersurface to a horizon sphere of an extremal Kerr black hole of sufficiently large mass. The gluing is exact at both ends and matches the full sphere data, including the transversal curvature. This proves a conjecture of Kehle and Unger in the extremal case. We first raise the angular momentum to the extremal value by rotating shear pulses of non-axisymmetric gravitational radiation, and then damp the incoming data exponentially along a long non-expanding neck. At the degenerate target horizon we invert the linearised problem at all angular frequencies, using a factorisation of a fourth-order angular operator into an angular Teukolsky-Starobinsky product. As an application, we construct one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data whose maximal development contains an exactly Schwarzschild apparent horizon and, at a later advanced time, an exactly extremal Kerr event horizon. This is the first rigorous counterexample to the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum, and proves a second conjecture of Kehle and Unger.

papers.title: Nonabelian Higgs fields from minimal submanifolds
papers.abstract: We construct $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills-Higgs fields on a broad class of noncompact Riemannian manifolds, concentrating in the large-mass limit along prescribed nondegenerate minimal submanifolds of codimension three. The solutions have uniformly bounded rescaled energy. On closed manifolds with $b_1(M)=0$, adding a suitably scaled Higgs potential gives an analogous concentration result. Our construction completes one direction of the correspondence proposed by Parise, Pigati and Stern, realising prescribed minimal submanifolds of codimension three as concentration sets of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Higgs fields.

papers.title: Network nonlocality with tripartite entangled sources
papers.abstract: Quantum networks are built from independent sources, and their nonlocality has mostly been studied with sources that emit bipartite entangled states.
