The ALP miracle parameter space overlaps with a currently allowed region of the QCD axion band, a large fraction of which is expected to be probed by the proposed IAXO experiment.

papers.title: An intermediate-mass stripped star with a dark companion in the Small Magellanic Cloud
papers.abstract: We present discovery of SMASH J004005$-$733351, an intermediate-mass stripped helium star in the Small Magellanic Cloud with a dark companion. The system was identified in a new optical color-selected survey for stripped stars and confirmed through spectroscopic follow-up. We measure an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb}=19.95\pm 0.002$ hours and a radial-velocity semi-amplitude of $K=91.7 ^{+3.2}_{-3.1}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$. Simultaneous modeling of the optical spectrum and ultraviolet-to-optical spectral energy distribution yields a stripped star evolutionary mass $M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84 \pm 0.54\,M_\odot$, temperature $T_{\rm eff} = 68.3 \pm 6.4$ kK, surface gravity $\log g= 4.76 \pm 0.12$, luminosity $\log(L/L_\odot)= 4.28 \pm 0.13$, radius $R= 0.99 \pm 0.09\,R_\odot$, and an unusually high surface hydrogen abundance of $X_{\rm H, s}=0.63 \pm 0.04$. The companion is undetected spectroscopically, and the orbital solution and stripped-star evolutionary mass imply a minimum companion mass of $M_2 \gtrsim 1.2\,M_\odot$. The absence of photometric variability from irradiation rules out a main-sequence companion. The companion is most likely a neutron star (NS), although a massive white dwarf or low-mass stripped star cannot be fully excluded. Binary evolution models predict that the stripped star will refill its Roche lobe after core helium exhaustion, likely producing a stripped or ultra-stripped supernova and ultimately a double NS binary if the system survives. SMASH J004005$-$733351 is among the first known stripped stars with a compact object companion. The system provides a new empirical benchmark for the late stages of binary interaction that lead to (ultra-)stripped supernovae and double NS binaries.

papers.title: ECH0EZ: Estimating the Hubble constant with ZTF SN Ia DR2
papers.abstract: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are instrumental for a precise measurement of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) from the local distance ladder, yet the data used hitherto for this purpose are inhomogeneous and subject to severe selection effects. We present the first, preliminary, cosmological analysis of 772 SNe Ia from the Zwicky Transient Facility's second data release: an untargeted single-telescope sample whose volume-limited subset (z<0.06) is largely free of Malmquist bias. We correct the public data for known instrumental and calibration biases and the redshifts for peculiar motions. Using the 42 SH0ES calibrators (their host distances computed from Cepheids and geometric anchors) and a Bayesian hierarchical model of SN Ia standardisation, dust extinction, redshift and calibration uncertainties, we infer $H_0 = (71.6 \pm 1.5)$ km/s/Mpc after marginalising over deceleration with a flat prior (or $(72.3 \pm 1.1)$ km/s/Mpc if a prior on matter density from Pantheon+ is imposed), with the uncertainty dominated by the number of calibrators. We demonstrate robustness to the choice of light-curve and Milky Way dust models and to extensions of the model to include peculiar-velocity correlations, a host-mass step, and two stretch populations. These results are in agreement with previous distance-ladder measurements and $2.7σ$ ($4.1σ$) away from the value obtained from Planck data, suggesting that the resolution of the Hubble tension lies outside of SNe Ia---or the distance ladder entirely.

papers.title: The Harmonic Structure of Multiparticle Scattering: Amplitude Projection and Non-Renormalization
papers.abstract: We develop a projection formalism for four-dimensional massless scattering amplitudes based on the construction of harmonics on multi-particle phase space. This provides a generalization of the partial-wave decomposition valid for any number of particles. Applying this formalism to calculations of on-shell cuts, we show that any cut calculation can be rewritten as a sum of products of projected coefficients and derive a condition for this sum to vanish. Using the on-shell renormalization group equation in combination with our projection formalism, we derive new non-renormalization theorems for effective field theories valid at general loop orders.

papers.title: Proximity-Induced Giant Majorana Spin Response in a UTe$_2$-Metal Film Heterostructure
papers.abstract: We establish an experimentally accessible route to identifying Majorana surface states through their intrinsic Ising spin response, using UTe$_2$ as a concrete platform. The key is to extend the Majorana correlations into an adjacent metallic film via the superconducting proximity effect, thereby making the otherwise surface-localized response accessible to NMR measurements. Remarkably, disorder further sharpens the Majorana signature: impurity scattering suppresses the conventional $p$-wave proximity correlations while preserving the Majorana contribution, yielding a giant Ising-anisotropic enhancement of the NMR relaxation rate. This approach also offers a powerful means to distinguish among candidate pairing symmetries.

papers.title: Mesons, Confinement, and Complexity: A Krylov Space Perspective on the Long-Range Ising Chain
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between confinement and Krylov complexity in the long-range transverse-field Ising chain, where power-law interactions $\sim 1/r^α$ generate an effective confining potential between domain walls without an explicit symmetry-breaking field. Using the time-averaged Krylov state complexity after a quench as a diagnostic, we find that the complexity is strongly suppressed and only weakly system size-dependent at small $α$ and small transverse field $h_x$, where confinement is strongest, and crosses over to rapid growth at larger $α$, where it increases with system size. Within the confined regime, the oscillation frequencies of the complexity agree with the meson masses of an effective two-kink model, with the dominant frequency growing linearly with the lightest meson mass and the time-averaged complexity decreasing approximately as its inverse square. We further study operator Krylov complexity at finite temperature using the Wightman inner product. At low temperature, it exhibits bounded oscillations that directly encode the meson spectrum, whereas this structure is progressively washed out as the temperature increases. These results identify Krylov complexity as a spectroscopic probe of interaction-induced confinement and reproduce, in a microscopic lattice model, the hallmarks of Krylov complexity identified in confining field theories.

papers.title: Dependence of Merger-driven Star Formation and Gas-phase Metallicity Evolution on Merger Type and Stellar Mass
papers.abstract: Galaxy mergers play a fundamental role in driving gas inflows, altering star formation, and redistributing metals, yet how these processes depend on merger type, merger stage, and progenitor galaxy properties remains incompletely understood. In this work, we investigate the resolved impact of mergers on star formation rate (SFR) and gas-phase metallicity using MaNGA integral-field spectroscopy and the MaNGA Galaxy Merger Catalog of Comerford et al. (2024). By comparing merger galaxies to matched controls, we quantify local offsets in SFR and metallicity as functions of merger type, merger stage, stellar mass, and galactocentric radius. We find that major mergers generally exhibit stronger SFR enhancement and greater metallicity dilution than minor mergers. In major mergers, SFR enhancement is often spatially extended, whereas in minor mergers it is weaker and more centrally concentrated. The SFR response in major mergers varies non-monotonically with merger stage, with stronger enhancement in the early (first-passage) and post-coalescence stages and weaker enhancement in the late (between-passage) stage. Metallicity dilution is generally strongest in early-stage major mergers and weaker at later stages, although this stage dependence is not monotonic across all stellar-mass bins. We also find stellar-mass dependence that lower-mass systems show stronger metallicity dilution in both major and minor mergers, while the strongest SFR enhancement occurs in intermediate- and high-mass major mergers. These results show that the resolved star formation and metallicity responses depend jointly on merger type, merger stage, and stellar mass and exhibit different behaviors across the merger sequence.

papers.title: Prospects for Near-Far Constraints on Reionization from Simulated LSST Observations of Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies and Stellar Streams
papers.abstract: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) will detect resolved stellar populations of intact dwarf galaxies and disrupted stellar streams in the Milky Way (MW) halo and beyond, opening a new avenue for near-field cosmology, particularly for constraining the faint galaxies during reionization. To interpret these data, we present and publicly release mock LSST catalogs of satellites, stellar streams, phase-mixed galaxies, and field galaxies around 13 MW-mass hosts in the FIRE-2 zoom-in simulations, generated with \textsf{py-ananke}. Using a surface brightness limit of $μ_{g} \leq 34$ $\rm{mag}$ $\rm{arcsec^{-2}}$, we find that $\approx29\%$ of streams with $M_{\star} \gtrsim 5 \times 10^5$ $M_{\odot}$ are detectable with tidal tails, while another $\approx38\%$ are detectable only through their bound progenitors and would appear as satellites. We estimate that $\approx96\%$ of satellites and $\approx64\%$ of field galaxies (out to $\sim$3.5 Mpc) with $M_{\star} \gtrsim 10^{5}$ $M_{\odot}$ are detectable, decreasing to $\approx$59\% and $\approx$42\% for $M_{\star} \gtrsim 10^{4.5}$ $M_{\odot}$ owing to resolution limits. Including streams detectable as satellites reproduces the radial distribution of observed MW satellites, suggesting that some observed satellites may be bound remnants of disrupted systems. Our mock galaxies match the sizes of observed satellites with $M_{\rm{V}} \lesssim -6$. Star-formation histories computed from only the detectable stars broadly recover the simulated star-formation histories. As an application, we test the near-far technique for reconstructing the proto-MW ultraviolet luminosity function (UVLF) during reionization ($z \gtrsim 6$). Adding the detectable streams improves the recovered faint-end slope at $z = 7$ and reduces the halo-to-halo scatter by $\approx33\%$.

papers.title: The Fate of 1/4-BPS States in the D1-D5 CFT
papers.abstract: We consider the 1/4-BPS operators in the D1-D5 system on AdS$_3\times S^3\times T^4$. We evaluate the anomalous dimensions of low-lying sectors in conformal perturbation theory around Sym$^N(T^4)$ exactly in $N$. All anomalous dimensions are consistent with recombination of the short multiplets into long ones and take a particularly simple form. We show that at finite $N$ and at first nontrivial order in the deformation, for the sectors we consider, the BPS density of states agrees with that of the supergravity point. To the order in conformal perturbation theory we consider, this confirms that not all states that can get lifted do get lifted.

papers.title: Universal Scaling of Conditional Mutual Information in Classical Stochastic Dynamics
papers.abstract: Conditional mutual information (CMI) characterizes dependence between two regions conditioned on an intervening buffer. Its characteristic decay length, the Markov length, has recently been identified as a diverging length scale at mixed-state phase transitions. Here, we investigate CMI dynamics in one-dimensional classical stochastic models and propose a universal scaling form for systems whose Markov length diverges with time. We derive this form in the inactive phase of parity-conserving directed percolation, where domain-wall coarsening generates a growing length scale and a self-similar probability distribution. We introduce a Hankel-based truncation scheme that enables matrix-product-state simulations at long times and over large spatial regions. Using this method, we verify the proposed scaling both in the inactive phase and at the nonequilibrium critical point, where the dynamical critical exponent governs Markov-length growth. More broadly, the same scaling form captures cases in which collective inference sets the diverging Markov length. Despite these distinct mechanisms, the CMI between fixed microscopic regions exhibits a common scaling dimension of two. Finally, we extend this framework to temporal CMI, establishing an analogous relation between the strength of conditional dependence in time domain and its characteristic memory time.

papers.title: What sets the star-formation rate in the Milky Way?. II. Comparing the star-forming clumps from simulations and observations
papers.abstract: Context. Linking the star formation (SF) properties of dense clumps to their parent large-scale environment is a key step to interpret Galactic surveys. Achieving a consistent, multi-scale picture of SF requires a comparative analysis of observations and simulations. Aims. We exploit kiloparsec-scale magneto-hydrodynamic simulations designed to reproduce local Milky Way conditions. Leveraging the wide range of scales covered by the simulations (reaching a resolution of 0.03 pc), we aim to compare the properties of the simulated population of star-forming clumps with observational catalogues. Methods. After extracting the star-forming structures with the HOP clump-finding algorithm, we compare their physical (mass and size) and SF properties (SF rate and efficiency) with those of the Hi-GAL compact source catalogue. Results. Despite the different methodologies and the three-dimensional nature of our clump extraction, the simulated clumps show good agreement with the observed sample in their mass and size distributions. We discover a consistently linear relation between mass and SF rate (SFR) for the simulated clumps, which is remarkably independent of the initial conditions of the boxes. Using scaling relations to distinguish between turbulence- and gravity-regulated gas inflow onto the clump scales, we find tentative evidence in favour of a gravity-regulated regime of SF at the probed sub-parsec scales. Key words. methods: numerical - stars: formation - ISM: clouds

papers.title: Hybrid seesaw from $SU(2)_1 \times SU(2)_2 \times U(1)_Y$
papers.abstract: We study neutrino mass generation in a model based on the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_1 \times SU(2)_2 \times U(1)_Y$ gauge symmetry, in which the Standard Model $SU(2)_L$ arises at low energies as the diagonal subgroup of the two $SU(2)$ factors. The symmetry is enlarged with a global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry, spontaneously broken by the vacuum expectation value of a scalar bidoublet. Light neutrino masses are generated at tree level through a hybrid of the type-III, inverse and linear seesaw mechanisms. A distinctive feature of the construction is the existence of a Nambu-Goldstone boson, the majoron, which transforms non-trivially under the original gauge symmetry while being mostly singlet under the Standard Model gauge group. We explore the phenomenological consequences of this setup, including electroweak precision constraints, the production of the nearly degenerate $W'$ and $Z'$ bosons at colliders and lepton flavor violating decays with a majoron in the final state. The latter constitute the most promising signature of the model.

papers.title: Parity-doublet spin interactions in ultracold polyatomic molecules
papers.abstract: Precision measurements exploit internal molecular structure to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. Reaching the entanglement-enhanced regime requires preparing and preserving correlated molecular states within the same manifold used for sensing. Parity-doublet states are central to proposals for precision measurements with polyatomic molecules because they enable large molecular polarization for enhanced sensitivity, and provide internal state co-magnetometry to suppress systematic errors. Here we report the observation and control of resonant dipolar exchange interactions in a parity-doublet sensing manifold of ultracold polyatomic molecules. Using laser-cooled CaOH molecules in a crossed optical dipole trap, we encode a pseudospin in the $\ell$-type parity-doublet states and observe two complementary signatures of interactions: a density-dependent Ramsey contrast decay and a spin-projection-dependent mean-field precession whose sign reverses with the initialized population imbalance. Both observables are well described by a common discrete truncated Wigner model using independently calibrated experimental parameters. We further Floquet-engineer the interaction anisotropy and observe suppressed many-body dephasing near the SU(2)-symmetric Heisenberg point, identifying a protected regime relevant for spin squeezing and precision measurement with dense molecular ensembles. Our results establish parity doublets as a coherent, interacting, and programmable molecular degree of freedom, connecting the polyatomic precision-measurement platform to dipolar many-body physics and opening a route to entanglement-enhanced tests of fundamental physics.

papers.title: Late reheating in the era of precision cosmology
papers.abstract: We study the minimum cosmic reheating temperature allowed by recent measurements of primordial nuclear abundances and of the cosmic microwave background. We find that reheating by decays of a light particle into electrons and neutrinos is compatible with both at temperatures around 0.4 MeV, an order of magnitude below the bound for purely electromagnetic channels. This scenario has implications for cosmology and laboratory searches. For example, nearly standard neutrino radiation can coexist with a smaller active neutrino mass density at unchanged physical masses, by up to a factor of five for normal ordering. The weaker suppression of clustering changes matter power at the percent level, which forthcoming galaxy surveys and lensing measurements may probe. Late reheating also suppresses sterile neutrino production at mixings within the projected reach of laboratory experiments.

papers.title: Fresh Look at Shift Symmetric Modified Gravity
papers.abstract: Shift symmetric Horndeski gravity can be a simple, well posed theory with protection against quantum corrections. Overturning conventional thought that such a theory cannot cross the phantom divide ($w=-1$) we present both analytic and numerical proof that it can. We carry out a detailed dynamical systems analysis showing the evolution of ghost free and stable regions within the model family, identify the fixed point and dynamical attractor structure, and derive the interaction of the $w=-1$ curve with these phase space structures. This reveals two mechanisms for cosmologies crossing the phantom divide while preserving shift symmetry.

papers.title: Axionic Quintessence in Heterotic String Theory
papers.abstract: We investigate axionic quintessence in heterotic string compactifications. Starting from the ten-dimensional theory, we derive the four-dimensional axion effective action, including gauge couplings and non-perturbative potentials, and identify the curvature terms that can correct it. We examine the geometric requirements for ultralight axions generated by exponentially suppressed worldsheet instantons, finding significant restrictions through an exploratory scan of toric Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces. In an illustrative K3-fibred setup, the minimal benchmark also encounters a tension with the positivity of the one-loop corrected gauge kinetic functions. Aligned worldsheet-instanton contributions provide a way to alleviate this tension and yield an ultralight axion with a phenomenologically relevant decay constant. Our analysis also identifies lower-action instantons whose contributions must be controlled to preserve the ultralight axion. We then study the resulting class of quintessence potentials and qualitatively compare their late-time cosmological solutions with observationally preferred ranges.

papers.title: Absence of linear power corrections in heavy-quark pair production in a non-Abelian gauge theory
papers.abstract: We study the infrared sensitivity of heavy-quark pair production by a color-neutral vector current in perturbation theory. We work in a spontaneously broken SU(2) gauge theory where, by tuning parameters to make the gauge-boson mass $m_g$ small, we use it as a probe of infrared physics. We find that, through next-to-next-to-leading order, terms linear in $m_g$ cancel in the differential cross section, provided that it is expressed through a short-distance heavy-quark mass. Interestingly, we establish this cancellation without evaluating any integrals explicitly, by relating virtual integrals to real-emission ones through loop-energy residues, with a suitable redefinition of the real-emission momenta. Our result is the first strong indication that the cancellation of non-perturbative linear power corrections in the corresponding QCD process extends to the non-Abelian sector. It is also a concrete non-Abelian example of the extension of the Kinoshita-Lee-Nauenberg theorem to linear infrared terms for sufficiently inclusive observables.

papers.title: The evolutionary history of ultra-compact accreting binaries. II. HST spectroscopy of two eclipsing AM CVn stars
papers.abstract: AM CVn stars are ultra-compact binaries in which a white dwarf (WD) accretes helium-rich material from a hydrogen-deficient donor. They are promising mHz gravitational-wave sources and potential progenitors of Type Ia supernovae. However, their evolutionary pathways remain uncertain. Three formation channels have been proposed: the WD, helium star, and cataclysmic variable channels. We aim to determine the atmospheric chemical composition of the underlying accreting WDs in two eclipsing AM CVn systems, YZ LMi and ZTF J0407-00, in order to constrain their formation channels. Using ultraviolet spectra obtained with the Hubble Space Telescope, we modelled the atmospheres of the accreting WDs, whose surface compositions are enriched by material transferred from the donor and therefore trace the donor's composition. In particular, the nitrogen-to-carbon abundance ratio provides a diagnostic of the donor's nuclear burning history and hence of the system's formation channel. We measure effective temperatures Teff = 24400 $\pm$ 1500 K and surface gravities logg = 8.36 $\pm$ 0.05 for YZ LMi, and Teff = 29900 $\pm$ 2200 K and logg = 8.37 $\pm$ 0.05 for ZTF J0407-00. The inferred masses of the two WDs are 0.84 $\pm$ 0.10 and 0.86 $\pm$ 0.12 solar masses, respectively. Carbon is not detected in either system, yielding lower limits on the nitrogen-to-carbon mass ratio of N/C > 117 and N/C > 185. We increase from one to three the number of AM CVn systems whose accreting WDs and chemical abundances have been analysed using detailed UV atmosphere models. The high N/C ratios rule out the helium star formation channel for both systems. The WD channel is favoured by the absence of detectable hydrogen at all observed wavelengths, although the evolved cataclysmic variable channel cannot be conclusively excluded.

papers.title: Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling for efficient quantum trajectories in metastable open quantum systems
papers.abstract: Open quantum systems can display metastability, with multiple long-lived states coexisting. Examples include the bistability of bright and dim manifolds in nonlinear driven resonators, or the long-lived coherent states of opposite phases in parametrically-driven systems, the building block of cat-state-based quantum computers. Metastability often emerges at system sizes where density-matrix evolution is impractical. Quantum trajectories mitigate this issue by evolving wavefunctions rather than density matrices. Metastable states then emerge as attractors towards which the system rapidly relaxes until a rare switching event brings it to another attractor. Simulating them remains costly, as one must resolve fast intra-attractor dynamics over timescales long enough to gather switching statistics. To tackle this problem, we introduce the Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling (DiSLOU) method, which combines three optimization layers: (i) Switching among locally optimal unravelings that minimize the number of quantum jumps in each metastable region. (ii) Diagonal propagation: the no-jump evolution is accelerated by diagonalizing the non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian once per attractor. (iii) Local reduced eigenspaces: the no-jump state can be faithfully propagated in a truncated subspace of only slowly decaying eigenmodes. We benchmark DiSLOU on the driven-dissipative Kerr resonator, finding no measurable loss of accuracy and the largest speedup in the bistable regime, where standard trajectories are most expensive. We then apply the method to the more challenging problem of accurately simulating rare bit-flip events in the cat manifold emerging in a two-mode dissipatively stabilized parametric oscillator, obtaining a performance improvement of over one order of magnitude. An implementation of DiSLOU in Julia is available as an open-source package.

papers.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. We introduce Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions. This concentrates imagination where it matters most and distills counterfactual outcomes into fine-grained, action-level supervision without a separately learned value model. We build a scalable training system that unifies distributed world-model search with asynchronous real-robot execution, forming a self-reinforcing cycle: real-world experience continually sharpens the world model, and a sharper world model in turn drives further policy improvement. We term the world-model side of this cycle test-time physics grounding, a capability that hand-built physics simulators lack: while the world model serves as the training environment, real transitions from the policy it trains correct its dynamics through a lightweight LoRA pipeline. Experiments on three challenging real-world tasks show that Rollback improves success rates over the strongest baseline by an absolute 10.67%, 11.11%, and 11.85% on block extraction, ball tossing, and tabletop curling, respectively, while achieving more stable improvement throughout training. Although initialized from teleoperated demonstrations far below human level, Rollback surpasses the average success rate of human players on both ball tossing and tabletop curling within 8 hours of training.

papers.title: SpikePID: Real-Time Neuromorphic Cluster Counting in Future Drift Chambers
papers.abstract: Cluster counting ($dN/dx$) measures discrete ionization occurrences along a charged particle track traversing a gaseous medium and is currently being proposed to serve particle identification (PID) in next-generation drift chambers, as it is expected to offer higher separation power than the traditional approach based on the ionization energy loss measurement ($dE/dx$), which has intrinsically larger statistical fluctuations. However, measuring $dN/dx$ in drift chambers proposed for future colliders requires high-resolution waveforms, which result in very large data rates. Running the reconstruction at the edge would drastically reduce the bandwidth required to transmit data off the detector. In this paper, we introduce SpikePID, a neuromorphic computing approach applying spiking neural networks (SNNs) to this task due to their inherently sparse computing and processing nature. We show that an SNN with only 529 parameters improves the kaon-pion separation power by 17% over the traditional derivative-based method and by 4% over an MLP that has $8.6\times$ more parameters. When synthesized to an FPGA, it uses an order of magnitude fewer resources than the MLP, and has an inference latency compatible with the constraints of future collider experiments, making the SNN an excellent algorithmic candidate for real-time data readout in future drift chambers.

papers.title: Counting Markov triples and simple geodesics
papers.abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the number of Markov triples with largest entry below $x$. We show that the error term is $o(\log x)$, which improves upon the previous best known results due to McShane and Rivin. We give an explicit error based on classical zero-free regions of the Riemann zeta function, and a sharper estimate under the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The proof uses the correspondence between Markov triples and simple closed geodesics on the modular punctured torus and a careful analysis of the McShane-Rivin unit ball.

papers.title: Equilibrium Learning of Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Equilibrium learning trains a physical system using observables of its relaxed states. We extend this principle to gate-based quantum circuits by embedding a parametrized circuit in a Feynman-Kitaev (FK) Hamiltonian and imposing the compilation target either through an output clamping term or through a target-dependent cyclic condition on the clock register. The ground state energies and the overlaps of the corresponding ground states with the free history state define faithful cost functions for unitary and state compilation. We show that these costs are nonlinear functions of the compilation infidelity and therefore reshape the optimization landscape. We show that starting from the free history state, quantum phase estimation can prepare the relevant ground states and estimate the cost functions with polynomial resources. In two-qubit benchmarks, optimization with the equilibrium cost functions reaches a fixed fidelity threshold in fewer sweeps than standard compilation infidelity cost function for many instances. The results demonstrate the potential for encoding quantum learning problems as computation of equilibrium observables.

papers.title: The Glass Transition: From Competing Theories to Discriminating Tests
papers.abstract: The dramatic slowing down of liquids approaching the glass transition remains unresolved, partly because competing theoretical explanations are difficult to discriminate. Indeed, several mature, contrasting frameworks account for the main features of glassy phenomenology, making agreement with familiar observations a weak basis for identifying the microscopic mechanism responsible for the slowdown. Recent numerical advances are changing this situation in two complementary ways. Deep equilibration extends controlled equilibrium studies into regimes previously accessible only by extrapolation, allowing established predictions to be stress-tested over a broader dynamical range. At the same time, new numerical methods increasingly provide direct access to theory-specific quantities such as configurational entropy, static lengths, elastic properties, and local activation barriers. I discuss how these developments constrain thermodynamic, facilitation-based, elastic, and excitation-based descriptions. The emerging picture is not yet a unique theory, but a set of increasingly discriminating tests that can reveal where apparently successful laws cease to be universal and identify the microscopic ingredients that causally control the activation barrier.

papers.title: Some Coble surfaces admit only Bertini involutions
papers.abstract: In this article we show that a biregular involution $i : X \to X$ defined on an unnodal Coble surface $X$ with irreducible boundary curve $\{C\} = |- 2 K_X|$ is necessarily a lift of a Bertini involution. Then we show with counterexamples that the hypothesis of irreducibility of $C$ and unnodality of $X$ are both necessary.

papers.title: Regression on high-dimensional phase space
papers.abstract: Machine learning tasks in particle physics are typically expressed in terms of regression, or relaxation toward some optimal solution as defined by an objective or loss function. In this paper, we introduce a large multiplicity expansion for analyzing regression tasks, which enables significant analytic understanding. For concreteness, we study regression with energy flow polynomials (EFPs), a complete linear basis of infrared and collinear safe observables on Lorentz invariant phase space. While the expectation value of any EFP scales like a constant in the large multiplicity limit, we prove that the covariance on uniform phase space of any two EFPs is highly suppressed and scales like the inverse of the squared multiplicity. This very unintuitive result relies on detailed cancellation guaranteed by the interplay of permutation invariance, momentum conservation, and rotational invariance. This scaling of the covariance with multiplicity further implies that the coefficients in an expansion of EFPs must scale quadratically in multiplicity. We present an example of regression with EFPs as applied to $e^+e^-\to$ hadrons events, and show how the regression can be solved analytically through the complementary expansions of the large multiplicity limit and of familiar fixed-order perturbation theory of QCD.

papers.title: CROMA: a GPU-accelerated Fokker--Planck solver for modeling non-thermal emission in post-processing cosmological simulations
papers.abstract: Numerical modeling of cosmic-ray (CR) spectra and the resulting non-thermal emission is important for understanding the physical mechanisms of CR acceleration and transport in astrophysical environments. Galaxy clusters and cosmic filaments provide particularly important environments for studying these processes, where shocks, turbulence, magnetic fields, and CRs jointly shape diffuse synchrotron emission. Spectrally resolved modeling of CRs, including cooling, re-acceleration, and hadronic interactions, requires solving time-dependent Fokker--Planck (FP) equations. An increasing number of studies employ FP solvers coupled with magnetohydrodynamical (MHD) simulations to follow the evolution of CRs in dynamically evolving environments. We present a new C/C++-based FP solver with GPU acceleration for post-processing outputs from cosmological MHD simulations. The code evolves CR proton and electron spectra along Lagrangian tracer trajectories and consistently includes re-acceleration and secondary-particle production processes. With the Chang--Cooper finite-difference scheme, the FP equation for each tracer is reduced to an independent tridiagonal system, which is solved on NVIDIA GPUs using a CUDA implementation of the parallel cyclic reduction (PCR) algorithm. The code uses sub-stepping between tracer snapshots, with the timestep constrained by the relevant CR cooling or re-acceleration timescale, and a batching algorithm that groups tracers with similar sub-stepping patterns for efficient execution. We find that the GPU acceleration increases the per-node throughput by a factor of $\approx$10 on the Leonardo Booster system operated by CINECA. The fast FP solver is useful for high-resolution simulations dedicated to comparison with next-generation radio observations and future multi-messenger applications combining radio, gamma-ray, and high-energy neutrino observations.

papers.title: Jaxnasium: Embracing PyTrees For Any-Agent, Cross-Suite Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Hardware-accelerated reinforcement learning in JAX has gained rapid popularity in recent years and has proven to be a successful method of scaling online reinforcement learning. The resulting ecosystem, however, is fragmented: environment suites define their own interfaces, and algorithm implementations are typically written for a single suite, a single type of space, and either JAX-native or host-based environments. Here we present Jaxnasium, a library for JAX-based reinforcement learning, aiming to make the field more accessible. Jaxnasium represents observation and action spaces as PyTrees, and uses this structure to build networks and support multi-agent processing. Through this, its near-single-file implementations run on discrete, continuous, image, and composite spaces, as well as in multi-agent environments, without any changes to the algorithm code. The same files serve as readable, research-friendly algorithms, as well as importable algorithms for more applied workloads. Through a minimal Gymnasium-style interface and wrappers for 11 suites, over 300 environments are available on which a small PPO implementation with default hyperparameters is able to run. Additionally, through a simple wrapper, we can run Gymnasium and EnvPool environments with the same algorithm and training loop, with no performance loss compared to architectures specifically built for training JAX algorithms on host-based environments. Jaxnasium further provides tools for multi-seed evaluation, hyperparameter sweeps, and project scaffolding. Jaxnasium is open-sourced at https://github.com/ponseko/jaxnasium

papers.title: An algebraic characterisation of $n$-qubit pure-state invariants
papers.abstract: We study the set of $n$-qubit pure quantum states. Specifically, we consider their incarnation as density matrices in Bloch representation. Building on prior work, we define a family of quadratic functions in Pauli expectation values, and fully characterise all instances that result in state-independent purity constraints. The resulting family of pure-state invariants is surprisingly rich in structure, with strong ties to the geometry of symplectic polar spaces. After charting the general landscape, we define a sub-family of pure-state invariants that satisfies the dynamical constraint of being stable under state update. We prove that it corresponds with (different embeddings of) symplectic Lie algebras $\mathfrak{sp}(2^{n-1})\subset\mathfrak{su}(2^n)$, which admit a generating set of Pauli operators. We carefully distinguish the symplectic case from its orthogonal counterpart, using the Arf invariant of quadratic refinements of the symplectic form on the projective Pauli group, which we further identify with quaternionic structures on $\mathbb{C}^{2^n}$ that are both generated by and restricted to Pauli operators. As a consequence of this analysis, we reveal previously largely overlooked structure in the $n$-qubit Pauli group. We highlight this in a number of examples. We characterise all state-independent uncertainty relations in variance for Pauli observables, as well as all Pauli channels for which the output fidelity and output purity are state-independent. We further show that the orbits of the projective stabiliser groups of pure-state invariants, which for $n\geq2$ are proper subgroups of the Clifford group, form complex projective state $2$-designs, while their unitary lifts form symplectic $2$-designs.

papers.title: The Trinity: Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
papers.abstract: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. We introduce Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous tasks at the same node, Creator abstracts their common requirements into simplified, verifiable simulated worlds for capability learning, while evaluation on original tasks measures transfer. Along this capability tree, Explorer progressively evolves reusable capability modules through selective inheritance, forming a Harness tree whose validated updates accumulate across iterations within a fixed topology. The resulting Harnesses specialize in different capabilities, motivating a Capability-Aware Harness Router that uses public task information to select compatible module configurations from the tree. Our evolved Harnesses improve mean performance by 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two real-world embodied tasks.

papers.title: Learning on-the-fly quasi-stationarity diagnostics from low-dimensional surrogates
papers.abstract: Accelerated dynamics methods, such as parallel replica dynamics, require estimates of the decorrelation time, after which a process trapped in one of its metastable states is distributed according to the quasi-stationary distribution (QSD). In a method proposed by Binder, Lelièvre and Simpson, decorrelation times are defined by coupling a particle approximation of the non-linear conditioned probability flow of the process with MCMC-inspired diagnostics. We explore an alternative to MCMC diagnostics, based on coarse-graining of non-linear probability flows and simulation-based inference. We first develop a coarse-graining framework for killed Markov jump processes conditioned on survival, proving uniform-in-time, non-asymptotic estimates approximating the non-linear probability flow of the true process by the non-linear flow of a surrogate process, defined with a collective variable. The framework does not assume reversibility of the true process, and also gives bounds which scale explicitly in an adiabatic regime. Motivated by these results, we then construct a quasi-stationarity diagnostic using simulation-based inference: a recurrent neural network (RNN), trained on particle approximations of non-linear effective flows, estimates posterior probabilities of decorrelation. The learned diagnostic is then transferred to collective-variable traces of high-dimensional particle approximations. We investigate the behavior and robustness of this diagnostic on a set of numerical experiments, comparing it to the MCMC diagnostic of Binder et al.\ on both synthetic examples and a molecular system, in and out of its training prior distribution. When its prior assumptions hold, the RNN diagnostic outperforms the MCMC diagnostic in ROC analysis, is less conservative, fails less often, and has an interpretable decision threshold.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Aware Planning via Imitation-Free Speed Scoring for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has predominantly relied on open-loop imitation learning for training, which presents two limitations. First, expert demonstrations show only one behavior per scenario, so the model cannot learn alternative valid behaviors and, in turn, cannot adapt to user-specified preferences at test time. Second, noise or ambiguity in these demonstrations can produce inconsistent, unreliable supervision for the end-to-end models. Driving is inherently multi-modal: multiple different behaviors can be valid responses to the same scene, and this diversity arises largely from speed rather than path. We introduce a planning paradigm that learns the path through imitation while scoring a set of candidate speeds across multiple criteria with a learned function supervised by physically grounded safety constraints. We realize this paradigm as Closed-Loop Aware Planning for Autonomous Driving (CLAP-AD), a plug-in planning head that integrates with existing end-to-end driving models and, to our knowledge, is the first to enable explicit test-time control over their speed selection without speed-conditioned training. On Bench2Drive-Speed, CLAP-AD sets a new state of the art Speed-Adherence Score of 82.53, topping TFv6, the strongest baseline on this metric, by 12.9 points while retaining strong closed-loop driving performance. On Bench2Drive, it improves driving score by +28.5 and +32.7 over UniAD and VAD, and on NAVSIM v2, built on real-world driving data, EPDMS by +6.1 over its backbone. Project page: https://clap-ad.github.io

papers.title: Non-Hermitian Schwinger effect in an imaginary magnetic field
papers.abstract: We investigate a non-Hermitian Schwinger effect by analyzing a one-loop effective Lagrangian of scalar and Dirac quantum electrodynamics (QED) in the presence of a real electric field and a parallel imaginary magnetic field. We show that an imaginary magnetic field produces an additional pole family in the integrand of the proper-time representation. Unlike a real magnetic field, an imaginary magnetic field can generate a nonzero imaginary part of the effective Lagrangian even in the absence of an electric field. The interplay between the two fields leads to nontrivial phenomena, such as a cancellation mechanism between the contributions of two fields. We also point out that when the ratio of two field strengths is rational, some poles among the two families coincide, and a careful treatment of double poles is required. By further examining the complex Landau-level structure of the electric-pole contribution, we find that the field dependence of the vacuum decay rate from each Landau level exhibits a sinusoidal-like behavior, and their sum determines the overall field dependence. Our results clarify the analytic structure of the QED effective Lagrangian in imaginary magnetic backgrounds and provide a basis for investigating its relation to non-Hermitian phenomena in the QED vacuum.

papers.title: Custodial scalars and Higgs branch
papers.abstract: We show that, for most gauged scalar fields, the scalar potential can be systematically organised into an ordered tree of increasingly symmetric operators. The intermediary global symmetries represented in the tree allow at tree-level a subset of the scalar field components, the custodial scalars, to be technically lighter than the scalar mass scale, or even exactly massless (so-called accidents). We further demonstrate, using the notion of moment maps, that such structure can be related to the Higgs branch of supersymmetric theories, allowing the use of powerful symplectic geometry tools in studying the vacuum of non-supersymmetric scalar potentials. We present various applications, from an example of a non-abelian accident to a Standard Model-like Higgs sector generated from custodial scalars.

papers.title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning
papers.abstract: Financial institutions operating under data-residency constraints are restricted to open-weight models small enough to locally host, which trail frontier systems on multi-step quantitative reasoning. On-policy distillation narrows such gaps by supervising a student on its own rollouts, but traditional OPD requires a strong external teacher, and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) conditions on a full reference solution. We ask how much of that signal is necessary. We present Fin-SD, a localized hindsight self-distillation recipe for multi-step reasoning. Given a problem the student fails, the student itself identifies the first incorrect reasoning step and writes a short critique of that step. We truncate the student's trajectory immediately before the error (aiming to obtain a correct prefix), condition a frozen copy of the student on the same prefix plus the hint, and distill that hint-conditioned teacher into the student over a short rollout under reverse KL. No external model contributes a gradient. We apply Fin-SD to GPT-OSS-20B on a custom multi-step financial reasoning benchmark that requires deriving formula inputs from realistic scenarios via accounting conventions. We find: (i) replacing the critique with a generic-feedback control matches Fin-SD's entire 3.03 pp accuracy gain over the base model on the FinanceReasoning Hard subset, suggesting the gain comes from where supervision is applied, not hint content; (ii) the model writing the hint does not need to be stronger than the model receiving it: hints from same-family GPT-OSS-120B, at roughly 6x the parameters, yield no materially greater benefits than self-written hints; and (iii) Fin-SD matches on-policy self-distillation from full reference solutions on accuracy while generating 9.5% fewer tokens. With Fin-SD, general reasoning on MMLU-Pro and a fourteen-metric compliance audit on FinTrust show no material regression.

papers.title: FinLLM-KG: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced LLMs for Financial Sentiment Analysis in Algorithmic Trading
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Generative AI have substantially improved financial sentiment analysis through post-trained financial large language models (LLMs). However, existing approaches remain confined to predicting the sentiment of each article in isolation and operate as black boxes, which limits contextual understanding and hinders deployment in high-stakes financial decision-making. To this end, we introduce FinLLM-KG, a model-agnostic framework that combines causal LLMs with a financial knowledge graph, in order to inject temporally grounded, company-level knowledge from SEC 10-K filings at inference time, without updating model weights. Within FinLLM-KG, context is supplied either as a natural-language company profile or as a small set of relevance-ranked factual triples. This enables sentiment predictions to account for broader firm-level information rather than the article alone, at almost zero computational cost and for any causal LLM. In addition, attributing each article-level sentiment score to individual sentences and to the retrieved knowledge-graph facts makes the evidence behind the prediction inspectable, thereby enhancing explainability and supporting human-in-the-loop review. Simulations demonstrate that FinLLM-KG consistently improves portfolio performance over the state-of-the-art baseline.

papers.title: Not Just Why, but When and for Whom: Revisiting Common Estimands in Causal Inference
papers.abstract: Causal inference commonly defines an individual treatment effect as a quantity that varies across units. But we know such effects, even for a fixed unit, can also vary over time, across repeated studies, or over different methods of measurement, and they can even exhibit inherent stochasticity. In this work, we consider how such additional sources of variation create a need for more general notions of average treatment effects, including some estimands that have yet to be more formally explored by the causal inference community. This perspective also motivates a reconceptualization of our most common existing estimands, such as conditional average, sample average, and individual treatment effects (CATEs, SATEs, and ITEs), as subject to more axes of variation than are typically considered. We explore two main consequences of this reframing in the case where we have data from a single randomized controlled trial: (1) decision making in fixed samples and (2) uncertainty quantification during estimation. We find that different estimands, even for the same unit or the same sample, can qualitatively disagree on whether an effect is positive or negative. We demonstrate these issues empirically through a case study with real data and characterize through a simulation study how our assumptions about these sources of variation, even if we cannot observe the variation, can be consequential for estimation and proper coverage performance. Importantly, these phenomena arise even in the simplest of cases, where all structural and parametric assumptions are satisfied. More broadly, this paper aims to provide a preliminary investigation into an underexplored class of assumptions --- assumptions about unobserved non-confounders --- that should be considered when estimating treatment effects.

papers.title: Scalarized Einstein-Maxwell black holes in external scalar fields
papers.abstract: We construct static black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory under prescribed external scalar fields, mapping their existence domain and determining how their scalar charges vary with the external field. Focusing on solutions with positive scalar charge, we find that a positive external field induces scalar charge in Reissner-Nordström (RN) black holes below the zero-source scalarization threshold and extends the allowed charge-to-mass range. A negative external field instead introduces a finite lower existence boundary and permits distinct black holes under identical external conditions. Coupling these isolated responses through the leading companion-generated scalar fields, we find mutual scalar induction in binaries whose components are RN black holes in isolation. For binaries with scalar charges of the same sign, their scalar charges need not increase as the separation decreases, while some binaries with opposite scalar charges admit multiple equilibria and cannot continue along their original equilibrium branches to smaller separations.

papers.title: STEM-Bank-26: An Open Dataset of Analytical Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy Images and Spectra
papers.abstract: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) is a versatile, multi-modal method for studying materials at the nanoscale. It integrates multiple signal sources to provide atomic resolution imaging alongside spectroscopy for elemental composition and electronic structure. Despite its utility, few datasets spanning multiple years of data have been published. We introduce STEM-Bank-26, a 929 GB open dataset of 37,921 STEM images that spans 1,095 material samples across 1,499 sessions and includes energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) or electron-energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) data for 65.5% of sessions. We extract microscope control trajectories by comparing metadata between sequential images and provide tools for building similar datasets from archival data. To our knowledge, this is the largest openly available dataset that integrates experimental STEM, EDS and EELS data across a broad distribution of samples and sessions.

papers.title: A gaussian-process reconstruction of gravitational-wave friction from dark standard sirens
papers.abstract: Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. In many extensions of general relativity, GW propagation is modified by an anomalous friction term, which alters the amplitude evolution and leads to a GW luminosity distance that differs from its electromagnetic counterpart. In this work, we develop a non-parametric reconstruction of this anomalous friction from dark standard sirens. We reconstruct its redshift dependence, encoded in the friction function $α_M(z)$, with a Gaussian process (GP) and derive the corresponding GW-to-EM luminosity-distance ratio $Ξ(z)$ by integration, explicitly retaining the relation between the local friction modification and its accumulated effect on the observed distance, while enforcing a monotonic and invertible GW luminosity distance. We apply the method to the GWTC-5.0 catalog, jointly inferring the source population, modified propagation, and background cosmological parameters. We find no evidence for departures from GR, with $α_M=0$ and $Ξ=1$ consistent with the posterior over the redshift range probed by the catalog. The result is stable under variations of the GP kernel, smoothness and amplitude priors, resolution prescription, and likelihood treatment. We further introduce function-space diagnostics for comparing flexible and parametric reconstructions, including prior calibration, prior-to-posterior contraction, common summaries of propagation-population degeneracies, and principal-component analysis. These tools make explicit which features are informed by the data and which are imposed by the function-space prior, providing a framework for interpretable non-parametric tests of gravitational-wave propagation.

papers.title: The Cosmic Ultraviolet Baryon Survey X: Density and Pressure Profiles of Clumpy Circumgalactic Gas at $z=0.4-0.7$
papers.abstract: The thermodynamic state and turbulent properties of the cool circumgalactic medium (CGM) are investigated for 23 galaxies and galaxy groups at intermediate redshift ($z=0.4$--0.7) in the Cosmic Ultraviolet Baryon Survey (CUBS) midz sample using background QSOs within the virial radius. Kinematically resolved absorption-line measurements from Hubble Space Telescope/COS and STIS spectra, combined with photoionization modeling, yield gas densities of $n_\mathrm{H}\approx10^{-4}$--$10^{-2} \ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$, temperatures of $T\approx(1$--$5) \times 10^4\,\mathrm{K}$, and non-thermal line broadening of $b_\mathrm{NT}\approx2$--$30 \ \mathrm{km \ s^{-1}}$ for individual cool clumps. Combined with published samples at similar redshifts, the results indicate that photoionization equilibrium accurately describes the cool CGM and that turbulent motions are predominantly subsonic. At fixed projected distance, cool-gas density decreases systematically with halo mass, while inferred cool-gas pressures in $M_h\approx10^{12}$--$10^{13}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ halos are consistent with hot-gas pressures inferred from stacked X-ray observations. The analysis uncovers a near constant total cool gas mass across a broad halo mass range, which directly translates to a declining baryon mass fraction in the cool phase from $\approx 6$--$19\%$ in halos of $M_h \approx 10^{12}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$ to $\approx 0.6$--$1.5\%$ in halos of $M_h \approx 10^{13}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$. Finally, several CUBS galaxies exhibit kinematically aligned low- and high-ionization species spanning up to two orders of magnitude in density, reflecting local fluctuations in the halo gas pressure.

papers.title: Heavy Seeds and the Multi-scale Fueling of Early Supermassive Black Holes and Little Red Dots
papers.abstract: The formation of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in the early Universe has been a longstanding mystery due to the brief period available to assemble them. More recently, the unexpected discovery with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) of Little Red Dots (LRDs), compact sources exhibiting signatures of active galactic nuclei (AGN), has accentuated this challenge. Cosmological simulations investigating their formation and evolution confront the limitation that the compact scale of SMBH/LRD physics cannot be simultaneously resolved with the larger-scale cosmological environment. We address this limitation by utilizing a cutout technique, selecting a targeted region around an SMBH seed from a cosmological parent simulation and re-running the cutout at higher (sub-pc) resolution for shorter periods. We explore two SMBH formation scenarios: the standard, light seed stellar-remnant case, and the heavy-seed, direct collapse black hole (DCBH) channel. Within the high-resolution achieved by the cutouts, the DCBH, due to its larger mass, is able to induce a buildup of high density gas nearby and accrete gas in bursts of super-Eddington phases, growing in mass and producing an LRD-like spectrum. In contrast, the stellar remnant cannot do so and remains dormant, unable to affect the nearby gas or significantly evolve by gas accretion alone. Therefore, we find that observed high-redshift SMBHs and LRDs require the existence of heavy seeds to assemble dense gas around themselves, enabling efficient growth and producing red optical spectra with strong Balmer breaks resembling LRDs.

papers.title: Setting Things Straight: On the Straightness and Non-Straightness of Two-Step Rectified Flow
papers.abstract: Rectified flow (RF) is an ODE-based generative modeling framework that has achieved remarkable success in practice over the past few years. By design, RF seeks to produce flows that have a high degree of straightness, in the sense that the resulting ODE trajectories can be obtained with relatively few (ideally, one) sampling steps. However, a rigorous analysis of straightness or near-straightness of RF flows remains missing in the literature. In this paper, we study settings in which the coupling generated by two-step RF is provably straight at the population level. We provide a complete characterization in two popular classes of data distributions: (i) smooth, strongly log-concave densities and (ii) Gaussian mixture models. Our main results yield sharp conditions for the coupling generated by two-step RF to be straight. Non-straight couplings are constructed when these conditions fail, which demonstrate the sharpness of these conditions. Using the theory developed on the straightness of two-step RF, we propose a notion of approximate straightness that measures the straightness of the learned couplings and can be estimated from the data. We introduce a procedure for constructing asymptotic confidence intervals for our proposed notion of approximate straightness and propose a data-driven method for selecting the number of reflow rounds in multiple iterations of RF.

papers.title: Spectral $Γ_2$ inequalities for the $V$-Laplacian with evolving weighted measures
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish spectral Bakry-Émery $Γ_2$ criteria and their modified counterparts for the $V$-Laplacian on closed Riemannian manifolds equipped with evolving weighted measures. The estimates yield jointly optimized spectral bounds and sharp endpoint constants. When the measures evolve according to the Fokker-Planck equation, these estimates yield monotonicity formulas for the Fisher information associated with Shannon and Tsallis entropies, together with quantitative propagation of Poincaré, logarithmic Sobolev, and nonlinear interpolation inequalities. In the stationary reversible setting, our results specialize to the Witten Laplacian and recover the unweighted Cai-Wang estimates \cite{Cai}.

papers.title: Efficient regime boundary detection in discontinuous simulation models
papers.abstract: Many computational models exhibit multiple operating regimes separated by abrupt or non-smooth transitions as the input parameters vary. Such regime transitions complicate the construction of global parametric reduced-order models, often necessitating large training datasets to capture the distinct system behaviors. Accurate regime boundary detection instead enables localized modeling strategies by partitioning the parameter space into regions of qualitatively distinct behavior. In many cases, regime switching corresponds to the excursion set of a simulator output. When such a quantity is discontinuous or non-smooth, regression-based algorithms for level set estimation can struggle to correctly approximate the boundary. In this work, we show that solving a resulting binary classification problem can improve sample efficiency and we further propose a novel adaptive sampling strategy for support vector machines. Unlike uncertainty-based sampling schemes, the proposed approach uses a continuous search space and efficiently explores the currently estimated boundary in its tangential directions by gradient-based dynamic sampling. Because the decision function admits analytical gradients, this exploration incurs negligible computational overhead relative to the underlying model evaluations. Then, a space-filling subset of the generated samples is selected as the next batch to be queried. We demonstrate improved sample efficiency compared to existing active learning algorithms on analytical and numerical examples. The proposed method provides a sample-efficient framework for regime boundary detection in a broad class of discontinuous simulation-driven problems.

papers.title: Testing strong exogeneity in proxy SVARs with internal synthetic proxies
papers.abstract: Proxy SVARs often rely on a single credible proxy, leaving proxy exogeneity untestable. Narrative arguments used to justify proxy validity imply a stronger form of exogeneity. We formalize the strong exogeneity assumption and propose a corresponding test based on internal synthetic proxies. The approach uses the external proxy to locate the target-shock direction in the reduced-form innovations and synthesize the candidate shock into an additional internal synthetic proxies, which allows to test the joint exogeneity of the original and internal synthetic proxy. We derive the large-sample theory for the ISP test and show that the identification strength is governed by a direct measure of the target shock's non-Gaussianity. We study weak identification under asymptotic Gaussianity and develop an identification-robust version of the test. Monte Carlo experiments demonstrate the favorable power of the test when the proxy has a low signal-to-noise ratio. Applications to monetary policy and oil supply news shocks find no evidence against the exogeneity of the benchmark proxies.

papers.title: Hironaka decompositions in supersymmetric theories: an exploration
papers.abstract: We ask when tree-level supersymmetric cohomology admits a Hironaka decomposition: a unique expansion in finitely many secondary operators with polynomial coefficients in algebraically independent bosonic primaries. Such a decomposition organizes the cohomology into towers with a common set of unrestricted dressings. For diagonal models with $N$ labels, $d\geq1$ bosonic species and $f$ fermionic species, we construct this decomposition and obtain $(N!)^{d-1}2^{fN}$ secondaries. We also prove that the scalar-branch ring of ABJM theory admits a Hironaka decomposition at every rank and positive integer Chern--Simons level, and construct explicit bases for the $SU(2)\times SU(2)$ Klebanov--Witten scalar ring. We also do the same for the Higgs branches of two class-S theories. However, not all supersymmetric cohomologies admit a Hironaka decomposition. In the Wess--Zumino model with $W=x^2y^2$, every positive-degree scalar annihilates the nonzero class $xy$, while $x^n$ is in cohomology for every $n\geq 1$. These two properties rule out a Hironaka decomposition over scalar primaries.

papers.title: Instruction Capacity: Behavior and Degradation of Language Models under Controlled Load
papers.abstract: The quality with which language models follow instructions falls as the load grows, yet there is still no quantity that expresses the limit of a model in units of load with an uncertainty. We propose an instrument in which the load consists of rules that replace single-token words in a text without meaning: such an instruction is atomic, the rules are independent by the construction of the task, and the outcome of every application of a rule is determined by a computable reference answer. Every occurrence of a word to be replaced becomes a Bernoulli trial with a known position in the answer and a known rule number. The statistical model first measures the shape of the dependence of the probability of a right replacement on the text length, the word position, the replacement density, the number of rules and the rule number, then describes it by smooth laws and restores a reference level that does not depend on the choice of the coding. The model yields the instruction capacity - the number of rules held at a given share of right replacements - with an uncertainty. A measurement of GPT-4o mini (2958 requests, 642,430 trials) gave regular laws for every load factor and for the collapse of the answer; the instruction capacity was about 37-38 rules at a share of right replacements of 0.95, and about 18-19 rules at the full replacement density. The code of the instrument, the measurement data and the passport are open, and every number of the passport is recomputed from the published points. The passport of a model serves as the calibration of a future meter of the instruction load of prompts.

papers.title: Protostellar Outflows at the EarliesT Stages (POETS) X. Preliminary statistics of 6.7 GHz masers near POETS sources
papers.abstract: So far, the POETS survey has focused on studying at high angular resolution the properties of both 22.2 GHz H2O masers and the radio continuum emission near young stellar objects (YSOs). Now, we want to add the information coming from another star formation tracer, the Class II 6.7 GHz CH3OH (methanol) maser, towards the same POETS targets. We seek to probe the existence of 6.7 GHz maser emission near POETS sources with high sensitivity observations and study their kinematic properties with respect to local radio continuum and 22.2 GHz maser emission at high angular and spectral resolutions. Within the POETS survey, we used the Very Large Array (VLA) in the A configuration, operating at high spectral resolution (0.1 km/s) and achieving a sensitivity of a few mJy/beam per channel map, in order to (i) probe the emission from methanol gas in the 6.7 GHz maser transition and (ii) trace its absolute spatial distribution and local standard of rest velocity. We present a preliminary analysis of 6.7 GHz CH3OH maser emission toward a subsample of the POETS survey (22 fields observed so far), 60 % of which show detection above a brightness temperature threshold of 10^7 K. Five sources among this subsample are new detections. We draw a 6.7 GHz maser brightness function by studying the distribution of the intrinsic luminosity of the maser population and predict that more than 30 % of the whole population is undetected at typical interferometric sensitivities of a few 10 mJy/beam. We confirm that 6.7 GHz masers arise close to the young star they are associated with and quantify that, on average, 90 % of them are distributed within radii of 3000 au only. Furthermore, we find a tight correlation between the 6.7 GHz maser luminosity coming from a given source and the local free-free emission, suggesting that the radio continuum provides the dominant source of seed photons amplified by the methanol gas.

papers.title: Minimax-Optimal Small-Loss Bounds for Online Linear Optimisation on $\ell_p$ Balls
papers.abstract: We study full-information online linear optimisation on the unit $\ell_p$ ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$, for fixed $2\le p<\infty$ and losses of dual norm at most one. Let $Δ_T$ denote the cumulative loss of the best fixed action above each round's minimum. A follow-the-regularised-leader (FTRL) algorithm attains, on every loss sequence and without knowing $T$ or $Δ_T$, regret $O_p(1+\min\{Δ_T^{1-1/p},\, d^{1/2-1/p}\sqrt{Δ_T}\})$. Matching lower bounds show that this rate is minimax for each fixed $p$, and its constant $(2+o(1))p/\log p$ is optimal as $p\to\infty$ among guarantees uniform in $d$ and $T$. The algorithm uses a bounded radial regulariser and switches at most once to its quadratic augmentation. On some paths where follow-the-leader (FTL) has regret one, its regret grows with $T$. A switching extension keeps the sharp constant and also guarantees $\mathrm{Reg}_T\le 2\,\mathrm{Reg}_T^{\mathrm{FTL}}$. For i.i.d. losses whose mean has no zero coordinates, we compute the exact $\log T$ coefficient of the expected regret, which separates FTL's variance term from the bias of the regulariser.

papers.title: Texture Consolidation of Generated Multi-View Renderings
papers.abstract: We present a system for consolidating a sparse set of multi-view renderings into a single coherent texture image, providing a framework for integrating generative models for image generation within the geometry-processing pipeline. Given a texture-atlased triangle mesh and a set of renderings with associated camera parameters, we generate the texture image by: (1) back-projecting the renderings onto the mesh to obtain texture images with normalized colors and confidences; (2) solving for flow-fields on the mesh that align the colors to each other, taking into account the associated confidences; and (3) fusing the registered colors into a single texture image using gradient-domain stitching, again incorporating confidences. Our approach complements existing techniques for multi-view image generation, leveraging mesh-based optical flow and texture-space stitching. In doing so it addresses the challenge that while modern image generation pipelines generate highly convincing renderings, they struggle to produce renderings that are consistent across views. Code is available at https://github.com/hliuw/TextureConsolidation.

papers.title: Non-local to local limit for stochastic conservation laws
papers.abstract: This work proves the convergence of stochastic nonlocal conservation laws, with spatially inhomogeneous noise, to stochastic conservation laws when the range of particle interaction vanishes. This provides rigorous justification for a class of stochastic conservation laws that has received considerable attention in the last decade. To handle technical challenges such as gradient-dependent noise, modified versions of the equations with specific cutoff boundaries are utilized and new uniform estimates to ensure stability during the limiting process are established. In addition, the work demonstrates that this convergence depends on the presence of a viscous term, as a counterexample shows that without it, the limiting solution may fail to be an entropy solution.

papers.title: CohortFlow: A Steerable Clinical Cohort Curation Agent with Localized Semantic Correction
papers.abstract: Language model agents for clinical cohort curation should accommodate evolving eligibility criteria without repeatedly processing unchanged requirements. We introduce CohortFlow, a steerable agent that represents natural language corrections as localized updates to a structured cohort specification and reconciles them with a persistent execution graph. Explicitly recorded semantic dependencies enable affected computations to be selectively invalidated while preserving valid prior results. On 100 scenarios derived from clinical-trial eligibility criteria, comprising 126 correction turns, localized steering achieves 77.0% requirement micro-F1 versus 76.4% for full regeneration using the same 8B model, a small numerical advantage that is not statistically significant ($p=0.493$). It reduces mean correction latency by 64.8% after completion and 44.3% during execution, with 38.1% fewer model calls. In a separate proof-of-concept evaluation over MIMIC, all 13 cohort states execute successfully, while correction trajectories demonstrate selective preservation of unaffected computations and recomputation of changed or dependent nodes. Together, these results show that localized semantic steering can substantially reduce correction latency and model calls while maintaining strong requirement-level accuracy.

papers.title: Phase-Twist Instability in a Coprecessing Neutrino Plasma
papers.abstract: Dense neutrino plasmas support collective flavor motion. We derive the first explicit dispersion relation about a flavor-nondiagonal background, focusing on the coprecession solution underlying spectral-split formation during the prompt neutrino burst of an electron-capture supernova. We show that slow phase modulations are unstable Goldstone modes, causing the coprecession plane to wobble with increasing amplitude. The instability emerges in the hydrodynamic limit, governed by conservation laws and without resolving flavor-precession resonances. Coprecessing neutrino plasmas resemble magnetized plasmas: a coherent flavor field drives flavor isospins to precess, and the phase-twist instability is the flavor analog of the firehose instability.

papers.title: A Hybrid Brownian Dynamics-kinetic Monte Carlo Framework for Coupled Magnetic and Rotational Dynamics of Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Simulating the coupled magnetic and rotational dynamics of suspended magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) over experimentally relevant timescales remains computationally demanding, particularly under low-frequency alternating magnetic fields. Here, we develop a hybrid Brownian Dynamics--kinetic Monte Carlo (BD--kMC) framework that combines thermally activated magnetic switching with particle rotation while retaining local fluctuations of the magnetic moment. These fluctuations are incorporated through Metropolis Monte Carlo (MC) sampling, allowing the moment to depart from the energy minima and thereby capturing the thermally averaged anisotropy torque that governs particle rotation. To preserve the distinction between local fluctuations and magnetic reversals, a barrier-trapping criterion confines MC trial moves to the current energy well, leaving thermally activated switching to the kMC process. For non-interacting single-domain MNPs, comparison with stochastic Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert (LLG) simulations demonstrates agreement in the equilibrium torque and stationary easy-axis orientation, including the field-driven transition from predominantly perpendicular to parallel alignment. The resulting BD--kMC framework provides an efficient approach to coupled magnetic and Brownian Dynamics, reducing the computational cost of exploring the long timescales relevant to low-frequency magnetic applications.

papers.title: Dynamical constraints on the companion mass from pulsar timing and cyclotron line confirmation in the SFXT IGR J16418-4532
papers.abstract: Supergiant Fast X-ray Transients (SFXTs) exhibit extreme X-ray variability on short timescales of minutes to hours, driven by accretion processes that are still poorly understood. IGR J16418â4532 is an intermediate SFXT in which X-ray pulsations have been detected and which has been proposed as a candidate cyclotron line source, making it a key system for probing neutron-star accretion physics and magnetic field properties in this class of sources. We aim to constrain the projected semi-major axis of the SFXT IGR J16418--4532, through timing analysis, and confirm the presence of a Cyclotron Resonant Scattering Feature (CRSF), thereby characterising the nature of the compact object in this system. We analysed a 148 ks long $\mathit{NuSTAR}$ observation and several archival $\mathit{RXTE}$ observations using epoch-folding techniques to search for pulsations while correcting the photon arrival times for a range of $a_x \sin(i)$ values. We performed phase-averaged spectroscopy using several different continuum models and assessed the significance of the cyclotron line feature. We detect coherent pulsations with $P_{\mathrm{spin}}$ = 1208.67$\pm$ 0.04 s and $P_{\mathrm{spin}}$ = 1209$.$4178 $\pm$ 0.0084 s in $\mathit{NuSTAR}$ and $\mathit{RXTE/PCA}$ light curves, respectively. The pulsations exhibit clear dependence on the assumed projected semi-major axis, and are detected with the highest significance for $a_x\sin i$ = 55.1 $\pm$ 3.5 lt-s $(\mathit{NuSTAR})$ and 51.3 $\pm$ 2.6 lt-s $(\mathit{RXTE/PCA})$. The light curves show several flares, and the pulse profiles are found to evolve over the course of the observation.
