papers.abstract: We present the experimental study of spin rectification in parallel and series networks of ferromagnetic conductors. The networks were composed of Ni36Fe64 elements (wires) which, when subject to ferromagnetic resonance (FMR), develop a small spin-rectification photovoltage. We found that the effect of spin rectification can be modeled as an increase in resistance of the ferromagnetic elements and closely follows the usual dependence of total network resistance in series and parallel electric circuits: the total spin-rectification photovoltage in ferromagnetic wires connected in series is equal to the algebraic sum of contributions from individual wires, while in the parallel connection one needs to add the reciprocals of the individual contributions. Our results support a simple way to control and manipulate the magnitude of spin-rectification photovoltage in multi-element spintronic devices.

papers.title: A cascade of orbital-field-driven phases with a Lifshitz-type transition to unidirectional spiral order
papers.abstract: Frustration in magnetic systems gives rise to unconventional orders and exotic spin liquids. Here, we explore a new type of frustration arising from an intrinsic bond-dependent orbital-field that couples orbital degrees of freedom to spin correlations. Introducing this orbital-field interaction into the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice, we show that local spin-orbital constraints generate a subextensive degeneracy, lifted by order-by-disorder to select distinct collinear magnets in a cascade of phases as the orbital field increases from a para-orbital liquid. At larger fields, the selected phase gives way to an incommensurate unidirectional spiral that spontaneously breaks chiral symmetry. This transition is driven by the coupling of a Goldstone mode to gapped dynamical spin-orbital fluctuations. The spin stiffness becomes negative along a particular direction, while the spiral wavevector grows as the square root of the distance from the transition, signaling a Lifshitz-type transition. We present a microscopic route to realizing this orbital field and discuss candidate materials.

papers.title: Explicit Reed-Solomon Subspace Designs: Optimal List and Line Decoding
papers.abstract: For any desired rate $R \in (0,1)$, and gap to list-decoding capacity $\varepsilon > 0$, we give an explicit $n^{O_{\varepsilon}(1)}$ time construction of Reed-Solomon codes over extension fields of size polynomial in the block length $n$ that can be list-decoded from a fraction $1-R-\varepsilon$ of errors with the optimal list-size of $O(\frac{1-R}{\varepsilon})$. We also give a simpler, strongly explicit construction of evaluation points for which the associated Reed-Solomon code can be list-decoded from $1-R-\varepsilon$ errors with list size $(1/\varepsilon)^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$. We provide a deterministic list-decoding algorithm for both constructions running in time $O_ε(1)\mathsf{poly}(n)$. In fact, our Reed-Solomon codes are near-optimal subspace-design codes over a subfield. Via known results, this directly implies the combinatorial list-decoding guarantee, as well as near-optimal list-recovery bounds. We also present a new reduction showing that the subspace-design guarantee also implies line decoding over the extension field itself, which then yields proximity gaps and mutual correlated agreement up to proximity parameter approaching the optimal $1-R$ radius. Compared to the recent algorithm of Brakensiek, Chen, Putterman, Zhang, and Zheng (2026), which list decodes every Reed-Solomon code over prime fields up to capacity, our approach achieves constant (in fact, near-optimal) list size rather than a polynomially growing one, at the cost of carefully choosing the code's evaluation points. In a companion paper, we show that these respective restrictions are unavoidable.

papers.title: Computer-assisted proofs of periodic solutions of state-dependent delay equations beyond perturbative regimes
papers.abstract: Rigorous existence results for periodic solutions of state-dependent delay differential equations (SDDEs) are scarce outside perturbative regimes, where the equation is close to an ordinary or constant-delay differential equation. We develop a computer-assisted framework that proves the existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs directly. The numerical approximation is a trigonometric polynomial, and a true periodic solution nearby is obtained by a Newton--Kantorovich argument in the space of $C^1$ periodic functions. The main difficulty lies in the terms in which the solution is evaluated at a time that itself depends on the solution. We obtain rigorous enclosures of their Fourier coefficients by adapting validated discrete Fourier transform techniques for analytic nonlinearities. We apply the framework to three representative examples of increasing complexity: a periodically forced toy model, an autonomous scalar equation with two state-dependent delays, and a threshold-type delay model from operon dynamics in gene regulation. To our knowledge, these are the first computer-assisted proofs of existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs outside perturbative regimes. This opens the way to computer-assisted proofs for SDDEs more broadly. All computer-assisted proofs, including the requisite codes and the approximate objects, are accessible on GitHub at \cite{code_proof}.

papers.title: Finite-Branch Multipliers on a Hölder Algebra: Commutants, Norm Closures, and Essential Spectra
papers.abstract: Noninjective multiplication symbols allow commuting operators to mix function values along their fibers, while Hölder regularity constrains this mixing at branch points. We study these operators on the Banach algebra $A_β$, $0<β<1$, defined by a restricted interval-variation condition. For $u(t)=t(1-t)$, we determine the full commutant $\{M_u\}'=\mathscr C_β$, including operators whose reflection coefficients need not belong to $A_β$. Separately, we characterize the operator-norm closure $J_β$ of the regular multiplication--reflection subalgebra of $\mathscr C_β$, obtain two-sided norm-distance estimates, and find a complemented copy of $\ell^\infty/c_0$ in the Banach-space quotient $\mathscr C_β/J_β$. Every $T\in\mathscr C_β$ satisfies $σ(T)=σ_{\mathrm{ap}}(T)=σ_{\mathrm{usf}}(T)=σ_{\mathrm{ess}}(T)$, and Fredholmness is equivalent to invertibility. For multipliers with finitely many full bi-Lipschitz branches, we also characterize their full commutants and establish the same spectral equalities for every commuting operator. For the regular finite-branch algebra, we establish an exact norm-closure criterion using weighted local Hölder defects and separate row-difference conditions, even when several folds share a level.

papers.title: Beta decay of potassium-54 reveals the role of two-body currents in neutron-rich nuclei
papers.abstract: The beta decay of neutron-rich nuclei probes the microscopic nature of weak interactions in the nuclear medium under extreme conditions. Such weak decays drive the synthesis of heavy elements in astrophysical environments, but remain poorly understood. Far from stability, experimental data are scarce, placing strong demands on ab initio nuclear theory. Two-body weak currents have been proposed as the dominant mechanism responsible for the universal quenching of theoretically predicted Gamow-Teller decay strength. However, direct experimental validation in neutron-rich nuclei has been lacking. Here we measure the beta decay of 54K, a nucleus at the experimental frontier of radioactive ion-beam facilities. In this work, the doubly magic nature of the daughter nucleus 54Ca results in a remarkably simple decay pattern, dominated by a single transition to a neutron-unbound state at 6.2 MeV with a comparative partial half-life logft=4.4(1) or Gamow-Teller decay strength B(GT)=0.26 (+0.08) (-0.04). Our measurement is reproduced by new state-of-the-art calculations of the decay, providing direct evidence for the essential role of two-body currents in nuclear beta decay for systems with a significant neutron excess. We establish a key benchmark for theoretical predictions of weak processes in exotic nuclei.

papers.title: Bringing Hardware Security Education to All: A Seamless Curriculum Integration Approach
papers.abstract: Cybersecurity education has predominantly focused on software and network security, under the assumption that the underlying hardware is trustworthy. Threats introduced through the global semiconductor supply chain, together with vulnerabilities arising during design and integration, challenge the assumption that hardware can serve as an unquestioned root of trust. Sensor-enabled systems and machine-learning accelerators further expand the hardware attack surface. The undergraduate curriculum of electrical and computer engineering and computer science programs has not evolved accordingly. Core courses cover the design and the functionality of hardware while the security aspects remain overlooked, and dedicated hardware security (HS) courses are elective, scarce, and often restricted to graduate students. At the University of Florida, fewer than 7% of the undergraduate electrical and computer engineering students register for the introductory HS course each year. We present an integrated and economical approach that disseminates fundamental HS concepts within existing core courses through contextual learning. Nine hands-on modules were developed such that each security concept exercises an associated design concept of the core course, as a component of that course and not as a course of their own. Doing the security work is how the student exercises the design topic, so the modules are built to strengthen the host course and not only to add to it. Three were assessed across three offerings of the embedded systems course through one course survey and two conducted by an external evaluator, with 25 respondents. We report what those instruments measured and the limitations of the approach.

papers.title: The reverse isoperimetric inequality for convex shapes included in a triangle
papers.abstract: We establish a sharp reverse isoperimetric inequality for convex subsets of a triangle under a prescribed area constraint. Given a triangle $T$ and an area fraction $η\in(0,1)$, we determine the set with maximal perimeter among convex bodies $K\subset T$ satisfying $|K|=η|T|$ and characterize the equality cases. Every maximizer is a triangle, and the optimal configuration is obtained by retaining a longest side of $T$ and placing the third vertex on a shortest side, at the position determined by the area constraint. This characterization yields an explicit expression for the maximal perimeter in terms of $η$ and the side lengths of $T$.

papers.title: EREBOTS 4.0: A framework for conversational assistants with A2A agents and MCP tools
papers.abstract: In recent years, multi-agent systems have shifted from rule-based, symbolic agents to sub-symbolic agents built on language models. However, several limitations remain unresolved. The new frontier is neuro-symbolic agents, which pair language models with deterministic tools and explicit protocols. Without a common framework to standardize and compose them, each study rebuilds the same infrastructure, and results are hard to replicate. This paper presents EREBOTS 4.0, an open-source, hybrid-AI, multi-agent framework that fills this gap for conversational assistants. Language-model agents plan and route requests, while deterministic tools compute exact results over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). An orchestrator selects one or more specialist agents per turn and calls them over the Agent2Agent protocol (A2A). A new agent, local or remote, is added by listing its URL in a configuration file. The framework also manages identity, user context with consent flags, task states and traces. Its A2A server passed 97 tracked requirements in the official A2A Technology Compatibility Kit, with no failures.

papers.title: Relaxed MEMs: Enhancing Borrowing in Multisource Exchangeability Models for Small Sample Applications
papers.abstract: Information sharing in clinical trials provides a promising way to increase trial efficiency, specifically in rare disease settings where sample sizes are small. Multisource Exchangeability Modeling (MEM) is a method that incorporates historical data from potentially multiple data sources, such as past trials, by exploring all possible configurations of exchangeability and provides a weight estimate for each configuration, allowing the user to quantify how much is being borrowed from each source. While MEMs have previously been shown to be asymptotically consistent, small sample sizes introduce uncertainty that naturally limits the amount of borrowing MEMs can facilitate. The proposed ``relaxed MEMs'' provide a mathematical framework for relaxing or removing those limits and allowing greater borrowing even in small-sample settings. Several relaxed MEM versions are proposed, and all strategies provide enhanced borrowing with minimal sacrifice in the bias and variance of the mean estimates. Specifically, the maximum absolute mean bias was 3.5\% (0.035) of the true mean in the two source continuous outcome settings and 6.4\% (0.032) of the true proportion in the two source binary outcome settings (absolute mean bias was 1.4\% (0.014) and 3.6\% (0.018), respectively, for traditional MEMs) and variance decreased relative to traditional MEMs across all exchangeable and small difference scenarios. The methods were then demonstrated using two endpoints from a series of phase II trials in cystic fibrosis.

papers.title: Testing Pre-main-sequence Evolutionary Models with Gaia and SPHEREx Observations of Canis Major North
papers.abstract: Pre-main-sequence (PMS) evolutionary models can assign different ages across stellar mass within the same population. We use joint Gaia and SPHEREx spectral energy distributions to infer effective temperatures, radii, and luminosities for members of Canis Major North (CMaN), a nearby association with independent lithium and kinematic age constraints near 23 Myr. The SPHEREx fluxes agree with 2MASS and WISE photometry to 3--6\%, and we anchor the absolute flux scale to Gaia, 2MASS, and WISE. Using the revised temperatures, we obtain a lithium age of $22.4^{+2.8}_{-1.5}$ Myr. For a 29-star PMS sample, population-wide HR-diagram fits yield $20.5^{+1.5}_{-1.4}$ Myr for unspotted SPOTS models, consistent with the external constraints, $18.4^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ and $18.7^{+1.3}_{-1.2}$ Myr for the Feiden nonmagnetic and BHAC15 models, and substantially older ages of $32.2^{+2.3}_{-2.1}$ and $55^{+5}_{-5}$ Myr for the Feiden magnetic and PARSEC models. No grid returns a temperature-independent age. The Feiden, SPOTS, and BHAC15 models assign older ages to stars above $4000$ K, whereas PARSEC assigns increasingly older ages toward lower temperatures. The intrinsic luminosity dispersion is also mass dependent, approximately $0.14$ dex below $3450$ K but $0.05$ dex at intermediate temperatures. At a fixed age of 23.0 Myr, a single SPOTS filling factor cannot reproduce the width of the low-temperature sequence, whereas the empirical filling-factor distribution of young stars overpredicts it. Spotted isochrones can enclose every cool member only at ages of 37--50 Myr, inconsistent with the lithium and kinematic ages.

papers.title: Update on transverse-spin azimuthal asymmetries in single-hadron SIDIS on transversely polarised deuterons at COMPASS
papers.abstract: Over the years, the COMPASS experiment at CERN has pursued an extensive SIDIS programme aimed at a comprehensive understanding of the structure of the nucleon, using a high-energy muon beam and polarised targets. Within this programme, measurements with a transversely polarised deuteron target were performed in 2022 using the 160 GeV/c muon beam. In single-hadron SIDIS on such a target, eight transverse-spin-dependent azimuthal asymmetries arise, providing sensitivity to several transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution functions and to subleading-twist partonic correlations. We report the simultaneous extraction of all eight asymmetries from the complete 2022 deuteron sample. The Collins and Sivers asymmetries, previously presented using about 70% of the 2022 statistics, are updated with the full sample and found consistent with the earlier result, while the six remaining asymmetries are presented for the first time with the full 2022 statistics. Combined with the existing proton results, these measurements complete a comprehensive COMPASS programme on transverse-spin effects in SIDIS, providing essential input for global analyses.

papers.title: NOCTURNE. VI. Hour-timescale radio variability in early-stage active galactic nucleus SDSS J122844.81+501751.2
papers.abstract: Recently, a sample of radio-weak active galactic nuclei (AGN) was discovered to exhibit extreme Jy-level radio flares at 37~GHz. The origin of these extraordinary flares remains unknown. All sources host low-mass supermassive black holes, and most of them can be classified as narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. We employed multiwavelength observations to investigate one of these sources, SDSS J122844.81+501751.2, during a period of high 37~GHz activity. Our data include radio observations from Metsähovi Radio Observatory (MRO) at 37~GHz, OVRO at 15~GHz, and JVLA at 15, 22, and 33~GHz, as well as optical, UV, and X-ray observations from \textit{Swift}/XRT and UVOT. We studied the variability of the multiwavelength light curves (LC) using statistical tests, as well as derived the $e$-folding timescales of the flares. Utilising the timescales and the observed flare properties, we estimated the variability brightness temperatures and Doppler factors associated with the flares. Most individual LCs do not show statistically significant variability, which is likely due to the low number of measurements. The shortest timescale we estimated is only 1.1~hours, measured between MRO 37~GHz and JVLA 33~GHz detections. This is the fastest intrinsic radio variability reported in an AGN so far. This yielded an extreme variability brightness temperature of $T_\mathrm{B}$ = 4.20 $~\times$ 10$^{18}$~K and a variability Doppler factor of 438. We discuss magnetic eruptions near the black hole as a possible explanation for the extreme radio flares, and show that both incoherent and coherent processes can produce flares at these timescales. These flares challenge our current understanding of AGN radio variability. Whereas magnetic eruptions offer a viable explanation for the flares, more observations, preferably broadband and including polarisation, will be required to confirm their origin. (abridged)

papers.title: Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Structure predictors like ESMFold fold proteins using neural network computation and have transformed structural biology. However, the driving mechanism from amino-acid (AA) sequence to 3D structure is insufficiently understood, and biological meaning remains locked in the dense network. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have shown promising results in obtaining interpretable concept features over an overcomplete basis of intermediate protein sequence-model representations. Yet folding models, which predict physical shape from AA sequence semantics, have no such account. We hypothesize that the features carrying the folding computation evolve in the 3D structural regression process. In this paper, we interpret the folding trunk in three steps. First, a pilot analysis on the representation distribution across modules and recycles locates distinct spatial computation in the trunk. Second, the dictionaries expose a division of labor: the single representation carries inherited semantics, and the pair representation computes the pairwise geometry. Third, we interpret the dictionary at scale with a reasoning language model, trace how the concepts compose across blocks by gradient-based attribution, and follow the interpreted code to the model's folding output, verifying where the computation aligns with, or departs from, known biochemistry. Together, the sparse dictionaries we train capture the relational geometry the trunk computes beyond the sequence model, and their concept activations forecast the model's own fold quality, turning the black-box folding trunk into a sparse, interpretable, and scientifically verifiable circuit.

papers.title: Directional Statistics on Circles and Spheres: A New Angle on Data
papers.abstract: Two compass bearings near north can have an ordinary arithmetic mean pointing south: the difficulty is that angles live on a circle, not a straight line. Using real wind observations, diffusion-MRI orientations, and geometric examples from machine learning, this article introduces circular and axial averages, directional variability, and probability models on circles and spheres. The guiding principle is to identify the geometry and symmetries of the observations before choosing a statistical method.

papers.title: Non-minimal $α$-attractor magnetogenesis with potential dependent couplings
papers.abstract: We investigate inflationary magnetogenesis driven by a non conformal coupling in the case of large-field $α$-attractor inspired models. We introduce potential-dependent electromagnetic coupling functions $f(φ)$ that reproduce the scaling $f\propto a^p$ during slow roll. Starting from Starobinsky inflation, we analytically derive explicit couplings for $(E)$-model and $(T)$-model potentials. We then study how these functions affect electromagnetic amplification in the regime of non-minimal coupling between the inflaton field and the Ricci scalar $φ^2 R$. In particular, we compare different values for the coupling strength $ξ$, accounting for electromagnetic backreaction and Schwinger pair production through the gradient expansion formalism. Our numerical results show that the non-minimal coupling affects the evolution of the electromagnetic sector and the resulting magnetic-field amplitude. We find that, within the analyzed configurations, minimally coupled and $ξ>0$ scenarios are compatible with the adopted CMB constraints, yielding conditional present-day magnetic-field estimates of order $10^{-23}$ G.

papers.title: Agent or Human? Detecting Commits by AI Coding Agents in the Absence of Authorship Signatures
papers.abstract: AI coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot coding agent, and Cursor now commit directly to open-source repositories. Empirical studies of these agents identify their commits through authorship signatures, such as bot accounts and Co-authored-by trailers. These signatures are optional, can be removed, and are often attached to pull requests rather than to individual commits. Hence, it is unclear whether Agent commits can be told apart from Human commits once the signatures are gone. We investigate the signals and limits of signature-free detection using 7,837,946 commits from 1,226 repositories, covering five coding agents and Human commits. After signatures are masked, detectors rank Agent commits above Human commits with a ROC AUC of up to 0.859, and most of this signal comes from message verbosity and change size rather than from the code itself. On the shared sample, gpt-6-sol without fine-tuning reaches AUCs similar to XGBoost and TF-IDF. At the observed Agent share, however, the best detector on the full test set reaches a precision of only 0.332. Detection transfers poorly to held-out Claude Code and Copilot, with TF-IDF reaching an AUC of only 0.524 for Claude Code. Temporal changes also depend on the agent, e.g., Copilot AUC drops and later recovers, while more training history helps Claude Code but not Copilot. These results indicate that signature-free detection can prioritize commits for review but cannot replace recorded attribution, and that studies relying on signature-based labels should treat them as a lower bound on agent activity.

papers.title: Beyond IceBERT: Open-Data ModernBERT Encoders for Icelandic from 12M to 1B Parameters
papers.abstract: IceBERT, the reference encoder for Icelandic, found that a cleaned web crawl is enough to train a strong model and that starting from a multilingual model can help on some tasks. We revisit both findings with the ModernBERT architecture. We train Icelandic encoders from 12M to 1B parameters on 9B tokens of open data, and rerun IceBERT's benchmarks and five newer tasks for 30 encoders under one protocol with confidence intervals. Our 1B model trained from scratch, to our knowledge the first monolingual Icelandic encoder of that size, is significantly better than IceBERT on all eleven tasks; warm-started from the English Ettin encoder of the same shape, it has the best score of all encoders on every task we rank. Because our model shapes match the English Ettin encoders and the multilingual mmBERT, we can also test the warm start under controlled conditions, at six model sizes and four token budgets. With our vocabulary transplanted, a warm start was never significantly worse than scratch training on the same Icelandic text, and from base size up it was not significantly worse on four tasks than scratch training on 4 times the text (8 times at base and 1B). As models grow, most of the transfer comes from the source model's transformer layers, so even an English source helps. Keeping the source vocabulary instead cost 5 F1 on question answering and nearly three times the compute.

papers.title: On the existence of polarized varieties without weakly Ulrich bundles, ordinary instantons with bounded quantum number and supernatural bundles with bounded roots
papers.abstract: We give an obstruction to the existence of bundles $\mathcal E$ on a smooth $n$-dimensional polarized variety such that $\mathcal E$ is $a$-regular and $\mathcal E^*(K_X+(n+1)H)$ is $b$-regular. In particular, this gives an obstruction to the existence of weakly Ulrich bundles. Using these obstructions and some recent examples of \cite{a1} in dimension $2$, we prove that for any $n \ge 2$ there exist many smooth $n$-dimensional varieties $X$ with a very ample line bundle $H$, such that there is no weakly Ulrich bundle for $(X,H)$, no ordinary instanton bundle with bounded quantum number, no non-ordinary $μ$-semistable instanton bundle with bounded quantum number and no bundle with supernatural cohomology and bounded roots.

papers.title: Cost benefits of designing carbon capture processes for part-load operation of power plants
papers.abstract: As fossil power plants increasingly cycle to balance variable renewable generation, carbon capture plants must be designed for a wide range of part-load operating conditions, to avoid excessive capital costs. However, accounting for the variability in design optimization yields higher computational complexity, and is therefore not a current design methodology. Here, we apply two-stage stochastic optimization to identify optimal carbon capture plant designs accounting for part-load flue gas conditions. We reduce computational complexity through a data-driven approach-to-equilibrium model of the absorption and desorption processes. Operating scenarios are derived from real-world part-load operation data of coal and natural gas combined cycle power plants. Our results demonstrate that designs optimized over multiple operating scenarios substantially reduce equipment sizes, lowering capital costs by 5-9 % at the expense of higher operating costs, resulting in a moderate reduction in total annualized cost by 0.5-1.6 %. The lowest costs are achieved when targeting an average capture target across operating scenarios, which allows CO2 capture to be shifted from full-load to part-load periods to reduce peak equipment sizes without compromising overall CO2 emission reductions. These cost benefits are robust across sensitivity analyses and increase with higher shares of part-load operation. Thus, part-load variability should be considered at the design stage, particularly for plants subject to variable load.

papers.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
papers.abstract: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. Optical coherent control of the quantum-dot transition allows to generate a quantum superposition of zero and one photon. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. After correcting for collection and propagation losses, we obtain fidelities to the ideal state and quantum purities above 95%, together with near-optimal quadrature squeezing. The ability to generate a wide variety of Wigner-negative states with mature semiconductor technology opens promising opportunities for continuous-variable optical quantum technologies.

papers.title: MARQ: A Modular, LLM-Agnostic Requirement Quality Assessor Infused with Systems Engineering Knowledge
papers.abstract: Requirements engineering (RE) is foundational to systems engineering (SE), as requirement defects can propagate downstream and adversely affect development outcomes. Although large language models (LLMs) are promising for requirement quality assessment, prior work shows that off-the-shelf models miss a large share of expert-identified defects, perform unevenly across quality criteria, and vary across executions. This study investigates whether infusing expert-derived SE knowledge can improve LLM-based requirement quality evaluation beyond off-the-shelf capability. We present MARQ, a modular, LLM-agnostic prototype that supplements LLMs with a criterion-specific knowledge stack operationalizing INCOSE requirement quality criteria and evaluated against off-the-shelf baselines on an expert-labeled NASA requirement set using Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and the open-weight Gemma 3 12B, with 100 executions per model. MARQ achieves median F1 scores of 0.80 for Claude Opus 5, 0.62 for GPT-5.6 Sol, and 0.53 for Gemma 3 12B, compared with off-the-shelf baselines of 0.55, 0.52, and 0.18, respectively. However, the nature of these gains is model-dependent. Claude Opus 5 improves defect detection and false-alarm control; GPT-5.6 Sol gains detection and better execution-level consistency at the cost of more false alarms; and Gemma 3 12B reaches the performance of off-the-shelf proprietary models, although it remains highly variable. Criterion-level analysis shows gains concentrated in Correctness and Conformance, trade-offs between misses and false alarms within individual criteria, and model-dependent responses across several criteria. These findings position SE knowledge infusion as a promising model-agnostic pathway for strengthening trustworthy LLM-based RE support while underscoring the need for criterion-specific interventions and human-in-the-loop review.

papers.title: Neural fields for adaptive white matter microstructural modeling
papers.abstract: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is sensitive to the micron-level diffusion motion of water molecules, allowing in vivo characterization of white matter architecture in the brain. Microstructural models like diffusion tensors or the Standard Model are typically fit independently on each voxel, limiting their ability to incorporate local spatial context and adapt to regional tissue complexity. Here, we introduce FiberField, an approach using neural fields that selects from multiple candidate models with different numbers of fibers to estimate fiber configurations and properties. This method incorporates spatial context through coordinate representations and model-weighted priors inspired by Bayesian model averaging to adapt to local microstructure. To compare FiberField with ground truth fiber properties, we validate on simulated diffusion MRI before applying to in vivo data. In simulated diffusion MRI, FiberField accurately estimates fiber directions and diffusivities using a multi-stick model (angular error: $2.2 \pm 2.8°$, diffusivity root mean square error (RMSE): $4.4 \times 10^{-4} \pm 5.2 \times 10^{-4}$ mm$^{2}$/s, fiber sensitivity: $0.87 \pm 0.21$). FiberField resolves fibers at 25% smaller angular separations than fod2fixel, and the diffusivity RMSE is 52% lower within fiber crossings than the Standard Model. On acquired diffusion MRI, FiberField's estimated fiber directions agree with those from MRtrix3's fod2fixel while also mapping microstructural properties such as diffusivity (angular difference: $10.5 \pm 7.1°$). Using neural fields allows for adaptive white matter modeling for selecting from a set of alternative models while maintaining accurate fiber property estimation.

papers.title: Improving Learned AC-OPF Feasibility under Distribution Shift with PF-in-the-Loop Correction
papers.abstract: Learning-based AC-OPF enables fast dispatch, yet its feasibility can degrade under distribution shift. We analyze three state-of-the-art methods and identify a shared deployment-time limitation: none use feedback from the power-flow (PF)-realized state to ensure feasibility of the predicted control. Using a simple PF-in-the-loop feasibility restoration filter, we empirically show that such feedback substantially improves hard feasibility across four out-of-distribution scenarios with modest runtime overhead.

papers.title: Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of $φ$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $Λ$ elliptic flow
papers.abstract: The first measurement of the elliptic-flow coefficient ($v_{2}$) of $φ$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $Λ(\overlineΛ)$ hadrons performed in OO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36$ TeV with the ALICE detector is presented as a function of transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) in central and semi-central collisions. For the $φ$ meson, in particular, this is the first measurement of the elliptic flow in a small collision system. At low $p_{\rm T}$, a characteristic mass ordering of $v_{2}$ is observed, consistent with collective expansion of the system, in which heavier hadrons are shifted to higher $p_{\rm T}$ by a common velocity field. At intermediate $p_{\rm T}$, above 3 GeV/$c$, a baryon$-$meson splitting with a $10σ$ significance emerges, with the $Λ(\overlineΛ)$ baryon exhibiting larger $v_{2}$ values than mesons, while, despite its mass being close to the mass of the $Λ$, the $φ$ follows the K$^{0}_{\rm S}$. The $φ$ meson behavior disfavors a purely mass-driven interpretation of the observed patterns and supports the role of hadronization via quark recombination from a collectively flowing partonic medium. These results provide complementary evidence that key signatures of partonic collectivity observed in Pb$-$Pb collisions persist in light nucleus$-$nucleus systems.

papers.title: An approximate inner ball condition characterizing $C^{1,α}$ convex bodies
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper uses an approximate inner ball condition to characterize $C^{1,α}$ convex bodies for $0<α\leq 1$. In particular, we show that a convex body $K$ is of class $C^{1,α}$ if and only if there exist constants $C,\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for every $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$ and for every $x\in\partial K$ there exists $h^\varepsilon(x)$ satisfying $B(h^\varepsilon(x), C\varepsilon^\frac{1-α}{1+α})\subset K$ and $\operatorname{dist}(x,B(h^\varepsilon(x), C\varepsilon^\frac{1-α}{1+α}))\leq\varepsilon.$ We then give a new proof of the regularity of the convex envelope by showing that $\operatorname{conv}(f)\in C^{1,α}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ whenever $f\in C^{1,α}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $f$ satisfies the coercivity condition $f(x)\to\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Finally, we use the approximate inner ball characterization of $C^{1,α}$ convex bodies to prove that the Minkowski sum of a $C^{1,α}$ convex body and a nonempty closed convex set is a $C^{1,α}$ convex domain.

papers.title: BehaveRec: When Does Long-Term Behavioral History Help Sequential Recommendation? A Study with Session, History, and Community Signals
papers.abstract: Sequential recommendation models typically predict a user's next action from recent session interactions, which limits personalization when short-term signals are weak or ambiguous. Rather than assuming that incorporating longer-term history and community signals is universally beneficial, we study when it actually helps. We propose BehaveRec, a three-signal framework combining a causal session transformer, a bidirectional User History Encoder over a 90-day window, and a GraphSAGE module over a user-user graph built from behavioral embedding similarity rather than item co-occurrence; a learned gate blends the three signals per user. On an industrial dataset of 137M sequences from 12.6M users, BehaveRec improves R@5 by +3.2% over SASRec, with a larger-capacity SASRec baseline (more parameters than BehaveRec) still trailing by +2.5%, ruling out capacity as the explanation. More importantly, a user-level stratification by history length reveals a clear dose-response relationship: BehaveRec's advantage is negligible below roughly 10 interactions and grows monotonically with history richness, reaching +0.017 R@5 for users with 101+ events. This pattern is corroborated across one industrial and three public datasets spanning history-rich to history-sparse regimes, where session-only models remain preferable. These headline results, and the resulting deployment threshold, are established for category-level intent prediction; a preliminary, single-run check on the full item-level vocabulary yields a directionally mixed result and is scoped as an open question rather than a claim. We use these results to derive a practical deployment rule -- roughly 20 interactions per user -- for when long-term history and behavioral-graph signals are worth their added complexity. Despite this added complexity, BehaveRec remains lightweight: it uses 5.67M parameters and trains on a single GPU in under two days.

papers.title: Thermodynamic and structural properties of the thin atmosphere of a white dwarf
papers.abstract: We determine thermodynamic and structural properties of the Coulomb plasma (jellium) in the thin atmosphere of a white dwarf using the path integral Monte Carlo method within a general relativity description of the star.

papers.title: The Keller problem for the lowest positive eigenvalue of Dirac operators with Lorentz scalar potentials
papers.abstract: We study the Keller problem for the Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_m - Vβ$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and minimize its lowest positive eigenvalue over all potentials $V$ with prescribed $L^p$ norm. We prove that optimal potentials always exist and that the corresponding eigenspinors solve the nonlinear Soler equation. This provides a variational proof of existence of solitary waves for this equation. We prove that there are no zero modes for such operators in dimensions $1$ and $2$, and conjecture that zero mode may exist in dimension $3$. In dimension $d = 2$, we provide numerical evidence that the optimal potentials concentrate on flower-shape regions, which are not necessarily radial, showing that Faber--Krahn type results may fail for such Dirac operators. In dimension $1$, all quantities are explicit.

papers.title: Elasticized magnetohydrostatics
papers.abstract: The modern approach to modeling equilibria in stellarators features two blind spots: lack of foundational agreement between theory and computation, and inability to reliably explore economically-attractive high-$β$ concepts. These blind spots originate at a technical level from lack of a useful existence theory for the partial differential equations believed to describe equilibria, and from the encumbrance of crude, inflexible models for the topology of the confining magnetic field. This Article proposes the first stellarator equilibrium model that rigorously guarantees existence of an equilibrium with any chosen magnetic topology. It completely separates determination of the magnetic topology from the equilibrium existence question, and thereby enables importing realistic tearing physics into equilibrium computations. The new model replaces the standard plasma potential energy functional with its ensemble average over rapid kinetic-scale fluctuations. Averaging ``elasticizes" the potential by energetically penalizing separation of field lines. The elasticized potential's super-linear dependence on plasma strain embodies a phenomenological model for profile stiffness, and plays an essential role in the existence theory.

papers.title: Two-layer conjugate flows in an open channel
papers.abstract: We investigate conjugate flows in a two-layer fluid system with a flat bottom and a free surface. These are up- and downstream states consistent with simultaneous conservation of mass, momentum, and energy; and therefore candidate end-states of one-dimensional dissipationless bores. By choosing variables in a specific way, we are able to explicitly parameterize all physical non-trivial conjugate flows in the system, using only rational functions. This two-parameter family can be categorized according to whether the states are compatible with (1) a rising surface, and falling internal interface; or (2) vice versa. In particular, we rule out the existence of monotone bore solutions, consistent with an earlier result due to Chen, Walsh, and Wheeler. However, here we do so already at the level of conjugate flows. Separating these two distinct categories is a one-parameter family of critical trivial conjugate flows. The complete description obtained in the present paper serves as an important stepping stone towards finding actual realizing heteroclinic orbits connecting such conjugate states.

papers.title: Characterizing Privacy Leakage in Spiking Neural Networks: A Systematic Analysis of Temporal Dynamics, Stochasticity, Neuronal Dynamics and Learning Mechanisms
papers.abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) encode information not only in whether neurons fire but also in when they fire, and this temporal dimension shapes what a trained network reveals about its training data. Biologically inspired firing patterns can reduce membership leakage in SNNs without changing the network architecture, which positions temporal dynamics as a design variable for privacy. A change in firing behavior, however, alters stochasticity, spike timing, neuronal response, and the learning problem at once, so harnessing this effect requires identifying which of these properties produces it. This study traces that origin by separating temporal representation, stochasticity, intrinsic neuron dynamics, and learning within a common experimental framework, evaluated under a black-box membership inference attack across image and tabular benchmarks. Varying the temporal representation shows that burst-like firing patterns reduce leakage relative to regular spiking, but at a cost in accuracy. Injecting randomness into the input, spike timing, and spike trains does not reproduce this reduction in leakage, which shows that the reduction arises from how spikes are arranged in time rather than from noise. The privacy benefit further depends on where these firing patterns originate. When neurons generate these patterns through their own adaptive dynamics, leakage falls while accuracy is preserved, so privacy no longer comes at the expense of performance. The learning algorithm then sets the baseline leakage. Under evolutionary training, the attack already performs near chance level, leaving temporal dynamics little room to improve privacy further. Privacy in SNNs is therefore not an inherent property of spikes but a product of how temporal activity is generated, processed, and learned, which offers a principled basis for designing neuromorphic systems that protect sensitive data.

papers.title: Optimally Selling Heterogeneous Objects by Quantity
papers.abstract: I study the optimality of selling K heterogeneous objects to a buyer with private values through a quantity menu: the seller posts a price for each number of objects, and the buyer chooses a quantity, pays its price, and selects any objects up to that quantity. I propose a pricing method that aggregates critical values for second differences of quantity values (the highest values attainable at each quantity). Critical values can be determined separately when each second difference's conditional inverse-hazard ratio depends only on that difference. For additive values, I show that the resulting menu is optimal among all incentive-compatible and individually rational mechanisms under explicit distributional and support conditions, including ex ante symmetry across object labels. A separate result applies the same pricing method to obtain an optimal menu for nonadditive bundle values without ex ante symmetry, assuming free disposal, independence between the quantity-value vector and the vector of bundle shortfalls from their respective quantity values, and corresponding distributional and support conditions. For an arbitrary number of objects, applications yield explicit optimal menus that involve quantity discounts, sparse quantity options, or two-part tariffs. These results differ from those establishing the optimality of pure bundling in Haghpanah and Hartline (2021), nested bundling in Yang (2025), separate sales in Kwak (2026), and core-peripheral bundling in Zhong (2026).

papers.title: Three Worlds for the Price of a Logarithm: Baseline-Protected Best-of-Both-Worlds Combinatorial Semi-Bandits
papers.abstract: Improving on a baseline requires exploring away from it, precisely where its performance may be lost. We propose DUET (Doubling Under Empirical Tests), a horizon-free phased mixing scheme for combinatorial semi-bandits with arbitrary finite action sets. Two observable tests decide when to double the learning weight and when to double the empirical-regret budget and restart. We instantiate the scheme with entropy-FTRL in mixed phases and hybrid-FTRL in pure phases. Assuming the baseline selects every arm with positive probability, this instantiation keeps expected baseline regret logarithmic in $T$, while its expected regret to every fixed action is $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ under non-anticipating adversarial losses and polylogarithmic, gap-dependent, under i.i.d. losses with a unique optimal action. All three guarantees hold at every deterministic horizon, and the algorithm knows neither the horizon, nor the gap, nor the environment type. Baseline protection, adversarial robustness, and stochastic adaptivity thus come from one scheme and two base learners, at the price of a logarithm.

papers.title: Impact of Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus Debris on Milky Way Escape-velocity Estimates in TNG50
papers.abstract: The escape velocity is a key probe of the Milky Way (MW) potential, but standard estimates can be biased by unrelaxed substructures. Using MW analogs from the TNG50 cosmological simulation, we investigate the impact of the dominant, highly radial Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) debris on escape-velocity measurements. We introduce an adaptive selection strategy that balances statistical reliability with sample size to identify the power-law decline regime of the local halo velocity distribution. Applying this strategy to 16 MW analogs with prominent GSE-like structures and continuous high-velocity tails, we find that retaining GSE-like stars yields a systematic underestimate, with a recovery fraction of $97.5^{+2.1}_{-2.9}\%$, while removing GSE-like stars alone increases the recovery fraction to $99.4^{+2.1}_{-2.5}\%$. The $\sim 2\%$ underestimation of the escape velocity corresponds to an $\sim 6\%$ underestimation of the total mass. This improvement persists in LAMOST-like magnitude and footprint selection. GSE-like debris is therefore a key contributor to the systematic underestimation of escape-velocity measurements, with direct implications for the inferred MW mass.

papers.title: Freeze, Don't Clone: Fine-Tuning with Expressive Policies Without Retaining Offline Data
papers.abstract: Offline-to-online reinforcement learning uses offline pretraining to accelerate subsequent online learning. While many methods assume the offline dataset remains available throughout fine-tuning, there are many settings where this is not the case. Prior work attributes failures in this setting primarily to critic recalibration under distribution shift. We identify a complementary actor-side failure: once the offline data disappears, continued behavioral cloning (BC) no longer preserves the offline behavior distribution and instead refits the behavioral model to the agent's limited, and nonstationary, online experience. We demonstrate that stopping online behavioral fitting while preserving the pretrained expressive prior substantially improves no-retention fine-tuning across implicit flow Q-learning (IFQL), flow Q-learning (FQL), and action-chunked RL (QC) on seven OGBench domains. We trace this failure to a behavioral feedback loop: continuing online behavioral cloning rapidly erases the pretrained prior, inducing representational collapse and action diversity loss that starves the critic of useful exploration. Freezing the prior breaks this cycle, preserving offline coverage while allowing value learning to drive continuous improvement.

papers.title: DSMC Study of Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Unsteadiness Using Data-Driven Analysis
papers.abstract: The prediction of transition remains challenging because the receptivity amplitude is usually prescribed rather than measured. This work uses Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) to study an unforced Mach 6 nitrogen boundary layer over a 120 mm flat plate, with no imposed inlet wave, wall signal, modal shape, or disturbance spectrum. The retained unsteady field is the intrinsic finite-particle stochastic fluctuation field carried by the DSMC representation. Changing the DSMC particle count provides an independent numerical control parameter that sets a predictable finite-particle noise floor while preserving the time-averaged boundary-layer flow. Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) is then applied to unforced DSMC snapshots. The DMD eigenvalues and spatial modes estimate the quantities that appear in the LST normal-mode description, including frequency, temporal growth or decay, wavenumber, wavelength, phase speed, mode location, and amplification envelope. LST is used after extraction to test whether the data-derived structures occupy the expected second-mode band. The results show that DSMC data can connect a measured finite-particle stochastic disturbance level to second-mode instability dynamics without imposed disturbance spectra.

papers.title: Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning for Dyadic Relationship Recognition
papers.abstract: Dyadic relationship recognition aims to identify the latent social relationship between two individuals from their multimodal interactions. Existing methods typically project heterogeneous cues into a shared representation and optimise a flat classification objective, overlooking that relationships may rely on different interaction patterns. For instance, distant relationships can often be inferred from direct behavioural correspondence, whereas close relationships are better reflected by coordinated affective, behavioural, and multimodal responses. To address this limitation, we propose HiRe-DRR, a Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning framework that organises relationship evidence from three complementary perspectives: feature level, interaction type, and relationship hierarchy. HiRe-DRR decomposes facial, bodily, acoustic, and textual cues into low- and high-level representations and constructs homogeneous and heterogeneous cross-participant interactions. We further introduce the Mixture-of-Interaction Transformer (MoI-Former), which treats diverse interactions as specialised experts and employs relation-aware sparse routing to identify relationship-relevant evidence while preserving contextual interaction information. The proposed Hierarchical Conditional Loss (HC-Loss) exploits the hierarchical nature of social relationships through coarse-to-fine supervision, enabling structured relationship reasoning. Extensive experiments on three dyadic relationship benchmarks demonstrate that HiRe-DRR outperforms recent representative image-, video-, and multimodal methods. Our routing analysis further reveals that distant relationships tend to rely on low-level homogeneous interactions, whereas closer relationships focus on high-level heterogeneous interactions. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/tw-repository/HiRe-DRR.

papers.title: cuArms: GPU-Accelerated Conflict-Based Planning for Multi-Arm Manipulation
papers.abstract: Multi-arm manipulation has the potential to dramatically improve the throughput, efficiency, and dexterity of many manipulation tasks. Recent work coordinates multiple robot arms in a shared workcell by allocating and scheduling tasks for greater parallelism, jointly planning multi-arm motions, or directly learning multi-arm policies. So far, these approaches are either too slow, rely on domain-specific assumptions, or scale poorly with the number of robots and task horizon. Thus, we introduce cuArms, a conflict-based planner co-designed with GPU parallelism that efficiently decomposes the search space using reusable multi-modal roadmaps for individual robots and resolves conflicts and deadlocks through a lazy search. To jointly optimize task assignment, schedules, motions, and manipulation skills, we integrate a high-level scheduler that proposes candidate skeletons for cuArms to ground into coordinated manipulation plans. Experimental results show that our method establishes a new state of the art, with real-time initial solutions and anytime improvements in both motion quality and scheduling, without days of domain-specific training required by learning approaches. Videos of both simulated and real-world industrial tasks are available on https://cuarms.github.io/.

papers.title: Rank two cohomology jump loci on projective varieties
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth connected complex projective variety. We give a structure theorem for irreducible components of the reduced rank-two cohomology jump loci on $X$. More precisely, for such a component $Z$, if the general point of $Z$ is projectively virtually abelian or projectively rigid, then either $Z$ is a symmetric square of an algebraic torus, or a quotient of a torus by an involution, or its normalization $Z^ν$ is a torus. If the general point is neither, then either $Z^ν$ is a torus, or an étale quotient of $Q^ν \times T$ where $Q$ is a fixed-determinant, fixed-inertia component of the character variety of some DM-curve.

papers.title: Distribution Grid Reconfiguration and Restoration via Linearizable Multi-phase Power Flow Modeling
papers.abstract: Accurate and tractable power-flow (PF) modeling is essential for distribution grid topology optimization, where the presence of discrete branch-status decisions therein significantly increase the computational complexity. To tackle this challenge, we develop a topology-adaptive, low-complexity neural piecewise-linear (N-PWL) PF model. We propose a sequential layer design that can directly incorporate branch status variables into the PF mapping from branch flows to nodal injections. As a result, our N-PWL model not only preserves the PF branch-node consistency but also facilitates the representation of any unseen topologies without retraining. A low-complexity model design is further pursued to attain a linear NN parameter scaling by using a fixed-size area partition of the feeder. The resulting scalable N-PWL model enables mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations of feeder topology optimization tasks, including distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) and restoration ordering problems (ROP). Numerical studies on the unbalanced, multi-phase IEEE 123-bus feeder demonstrate our N-PWL model outperforms existing end-to-end baselines in PF prediction and, more importantly, can fill the gap by achieving accurate representation of any unseen topologies. For solving DNR/ROP, our model can significantly improve the AC feasibility over linearized PF models, with a notable reduction of computation time compared with AC-PF based nonlinear formulations, particularly under a large number of topology decisions.

papers.title: The Calderón problem for the fractional Schrödinger equation at a single point
papers.abstract: We revisit the Calderón problem for the fractional Schrödinger equation and prove that the potential is determined by Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps at a single exterior point, with exterior inputs varying in a disjoint open set. This holds for continuous potentials for all $0<s<1$ and for bounded potentials when $s\geq 1/4$. For ordered nonnegative bounded potentials, one fixed nonzero nonnegative input and one point measurement suffice for every $0<s<1$.

papers.title: Instant Software Factories
papers.abstract: Coding agents can quickly build prototypes, but a long tail of fixes, optimizations, tests, and releases separates a prototype from a product. A software factory handles this ongoing work through a repeatable process. We ask whether this work needs dedicated orchestration and how such factories should be judged. Given a tested repository and a coding agent, an instant software factory uses only two coordination inputs, a swarm of cron-job agents with standing objectives and a shared communication board, such as GitHub, where agents coordinate through the traces they leave. We developed a bootstrap prompt designed to set up both inputs from one round of human input, with governance as a separable layer. We distilled it from two manually configured industrial factories, observed for 15 and 17 days, and have not yet evaluated it. In the GitHub-coordinated CLI factory, daily merges rose 15x during agent rollout, an observed association. Its agents also filed 95% of new issues and authored 40 of 58 PRs that changed CI workflows, and at least 5.6% of issues marked as fixed were later found to have incorrect fixes. Unlike an agent scored on a fixed benchmark, a factory thus changes its own workload, evaluator, and measured progress. We formulate factory development as multi-objective optimization under this endogenous feedback. Over five months, we plan to evolve both factories, test the bootstrap on new repositories, and test five falsifiable hypotheses.

papers.title: What Should an Information Bottleneck Encoder Learn? Separating Representation Learning from Rate Control
papers.abstract: The information bottleneck (IB) trades compression of an input $X$ against prediction of a target $Y$ through a multiplier $β=1/λ$, yet each operating point is usually served by training, or fully conditioning, a new encoder. For jointly Gaussian data, we show that the IB solution factorizes as $A(β)=D(β)W$: the information-bearing directions $W$ do not depend on $β$, and $β$ acts only through scalar gains. We ask whether this separation of \emph{representation} from \emph{rate control} survives beyond Gaussian models, treating the budget as a given operating parameter rather than a quantity to be optimized. For a budget-free representation \(F(X)\), the \emph{separation gap} is controlled by the \emph{sufficiency deficit} $ε_F=I(X;Y\mid F(X))$: We show there is at least $ε_F$ in the worst case for finite inputs, and it is bounded uniformly in $λ$ by a function of $ε_F$ for finite label alphabets. The same certificate extends to a new target distribution and to pooled multi-domain data, where a conditional-alignment term appears. On MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10 and STL-10 (10 seeds, eight prespecified budgets), a frozen CNN representation with one compressor--decoder pair per budget reduces estimated training multiply--accumulate operations (MACs) by $7.7\times$ and wall-clock time by about $2\times$ relative to end-to-end VIBs, and attains higher budget-averaged accuracy ($65.6\%$ versus $57.3\%$ per domain; $67.1\%$ versus $57.1\%$ pooled), with the advantage concentrated at strong compression, where the VIBs collapse. At weak compression ($λ\le0.036$), VIB has higher cross-entropy and ECE; its surrogate Lagrangian is higher per domain, indistinguishable from the pooled VIB in the macro average, and lower on the pooled test set.

papers.title: Proximal Point Newton Methods for Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: Tensor methods offer improved complexity guarantees for nonconvex optimization, but evaluating high-order derivatives and solving the corresponding subproblems can be computationally expensive. In this paper, we develop a proximal point Newton framework that exploits third-derivative smoothness using only gradients and Hessians. Under Hessian Lipschitz continuity, a single-loop proximal point Newton method that alternates between negative-curvature directions and Newton steps finds an $(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)$-approximate second-order stationary point within $\mathcal{O}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-3/2},\varepsilon_H^{-3}\})$ second-order oracle evaluations. When the third derivative is also Lipschitz continuous, we introduce an accelerated proximal point Newton method and obtain a dimension-free complexity of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-4/3},\varepsilon_H^{-2}\})$, matching that of the third-order tensor methods up to logarithmic factors without constructing tensors or solving tensor subproblems. We further develop an adaptive inexact Newton--CG variant that requires no prior knowledge of Lipschitz constants and preserves the improved oracle complexity with high probability. Under uniformly bounded queried Hessians, this variant achieves a Hessian-vector product complexity of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-5/3},\varepsilon_H^{-5/2}\})$, improving upon the previous $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-3}\varepsilon_H^{5/2},\varepsilon_H^{-7/2}\})$ result attained by existing second-order methods such as cubic regularized Newton method and Newton--CG method. Preliminary numerical experiments are encouraging.

papers.title: Dynamical Tensor Train Approximation for Wigner--Fokker--Planck Equation with Applications to Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: We develop a dynamical tensor-train method for the Wigner--Fokker--Planck equation arising in continuous-variable open quantum systems. The Wigner function is evolved directly in tensor-train form using a projector-splitting integrator, while the nonlocal Wigner pseudo-differential operator is treated through low-rank representations of the potential difference and matrix-free exponential actions. The resulting method avoids full tensor-product computations in high-dimensional phase space. Numerical experiments in one, two, and three spatial dimensions demonstrate the accuracy and scalability of the method, including simulations in a six-dimensional phase space.

papers.title: SpecGuard: Detecting Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks via Specification-Based Runtime Monitoring
papers.abstract: Multi-turn jailbreaks turn dialogue safety into a trace property: a violation may become identifiable only when user intent and assistant behavior are considered across multiple turns. Existing guard models largely classify individual messages or exchanges and return risk scores or labels, without executable safety semantics or a formally checkable decision trail. We present SpecGuard, a training-free, specification-driven framework for monitoring multi-turn LLM interactions. SpecGuard uses a fixed atomic-proposition contract to map natural-language observations into causally scoped, evidence-backed facts, and expresses forbidden interaction patterns as Linear Temporal Logic specifications. Each specification is compiled into a symbolic finite automaton that incrementally consumes the resulting dialogue trace. The same monitoring mechanism supports buffered runtime checking and retrospective auditing, while accepting runs produce replayable witnesses that identify the triggered specification, supporting facts, and relevant dialogue turns. Experiments on multi-turn safety benchmarks show that SpecGuard consistently outperforms representative open-source guard models while maintaining controlled false-positive rates. These results demonstrate a practical path from heuristic risk classification toward formally specified, verifiable, and auditable LLM safety monitoring, without learned detector parameters or access to the protected model.

papers.title: Filling knots and essential geodesic systole
papers.abstract: We prove that every closed, orientable $3$--manifold contains hyperbolic knots with arbitrarily large essential geodesic systole. That is, for any $3$--manifold $M$, and $R> 0$ there is a hyperbolic knot $K \subset M$ such that every closed geodesic in the knot complement which is non-null-homotopic in $M$ has length at least $R$. The construction also produces filling knots, in the sense of Freedman-Krushkal [FreeKrus2023]. This answers two questions of Biringer.

papers.title: Infinite families and sporadic solutions of the equation $\varphi(n)=c+α\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi(p)$
papers.abstract: Ranjan and Singh proved that for every composite $n$ which is not twice an odd prime, $\varphi(n)$ is at least one plus the sum of $\varphi$ over the prime divisors of $n$, with equality exactly for $n=4,12,30$. \new{We study the weighted equation $\varphi(n)=c+α\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi(p)$. We determine the parameters $(c,α)$ admitting infinite families of solutions, prove that all remaining solutions are finite in number and arise from an explicit linear mechanism, and compute them exactly in a range of parameters; the finiteness of $\{4,12,30\}$ becomes a special case. We also settle the analogous equations for the divisor functions $τ$ and $σ$ and for the Jordan totients, and, from known results on the sum of the prime divisors, derive the full asymptotic expansion of the average deficiency.} \K{In the range $|c|\le10$, $1\leα\le6$ the composite solution set is determined completely\V{, and the number and the size of the sporadic solutions are shown to be bounded by polynomials in $|c|+α$}.} \B{Finally, replacing the prime values $\varphi(p)$ by their iterates $\varphi^{(k)}(p)$, we determine all solutions of $\varphi(n)=1+\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi^{(k)}(p)$: the solution sets are $\{1,4,12,30\}$, $\{1,3,4,10\}$ and, for every $k\ge3$, $\{1,3,4\}$; for the weighted iterated equation we exhibit an infinite family governed by the safe primes.

papers.title: The Complexity of Strategizing Against No-Regret Learners: Pure When It Is Easy, Hard Even When Mixed
papers.abstract: We study the computational complexity of clairvoyant strategy optimization against a known online learner in finite-horizon repeated games. In general-sum games with bounded payoffs, unless $\mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP}$, no polynomial-time optimizer can achieve a reward within $cT$ of the reward of the optimal pure-action sequence for an absolute constant $c>0$, even when allowed to output explicitly represented mixed strategies at every round. Our hardness result strengthens prior work along two complementary axes: it extends to a broader class of learning dynamics, including widely used mean-based algorithms, answering an open question of Assos, Dagan, and Rajaraman (2025) for learners beyond multiplicative weights; and it permits mixed outputs while retaining the weaker pure-sequence benchmark. Thus, neither mixed strategies nor algorithmic specificity removes the computational obstruction in general-sum games. In sharp contrast, zero-sum games exhibit the reverse phenomenon: deterministic pure actions suffice for efficiently recovering the leading surplus guarantees previously obtained through mixed play against Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) opponents. Thus, the two regimes form a striking mirror image: mixed play cannot overcome general-sum hardness even against a pure benchmark, whereas pure play retains the full surplus guarantees of mixed strategies in zero-sum games.

papers.title: Reduced magnetohydrodynamics with electron inertia in pseudodipole coordinates
papers.abstract: We study the altitude-dependent structuring of field-aligned currents by driven Alfvén waves in an expanding auroral flux tube. The model uses the reduced magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) long-thin ordering assumptions along with electron inertia. We derive a magnetic tension operator consistent with energy conservation in the expanding geometry. We compare uniform density with a prescribed profile containing a dense ionospheric end and a low-density upper region. The simulations produce localized current concentrations near the lower boundary and filamentary structures at greater heights. Broad structures remain visible in the magnetic and velocity stream functions while their perpendicular derivatives reveal finer magnetic field, velocity, and current structure. With the nonuniform density profile, the run with additional upper boundary reflection shows finer current structure and greater numerical dissipation. Spectral diagnostics show forward nonlinear energy transfer and altitude-dependent power-law-like intervals without a broad constant-flux range. The narrowest current concentrations span only a few grid cells, so their physical widths remain unresolved.

papers.title: Exciton-driven coherent dressing in transient absorption
papers.abstract: While coherent excitons have recently been observed to dress electronic states in time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES), exciton-driven dressing in optical spectroscopy remains largely unexplored. This work develops a theoretical and computational approach to exciton-driven dressing effects in transient absorption spectroscopy in the time-dependent adiabatic GW formalism and derives two symmetry- and band topology-protected selections rules for exciton-dressed transient absorption, unique from tr-ARPES. We then numerically calculate exciton-dressed transient absorption spectra of monolayer MoS2 and demonstrate the selection rules and their lifting after symmetry breaking.

papers.title: The Inbox as a Coordination Primitive for LLM Agent Societies
papers.abstract: Language-model agents increasingly coordinate in large groups, and current agent protocols focus on delivering messages. For these agents, however, the scarce resource is not delivery but reading: every message costs tokens, and the context is finite. Current infrastructure works by push: the sender decides when a message enters the recipient's context, so the recipient reads in arrival order and drops the oldest messages once its context is full. We study the alternative, pull, in which messages wait in an inbox outside the context and the recipient's own rules decide what it reads and keeps. We argue that the inbox is a coordination primitive: each agent sets its rules privately, and those rules decide whether other agents' requests reach it. In simulated societies of up to 16,000 agents, with every decision an LLM judgment, we report three findings. First, push fails as an agent takes part in more coordination at once: an agent leading 20 negotiations with a full memory proposes options already rejected 97% of the time, because it has dropped the oldest replies. Second, an inbox is necessary under heavy, noisy traffic. Where first come, first read misses every request, an inbox that first reads messages carrying a refundable deposit still finds about 60% of the agents a request needs, at every size from 1,000 to 16,000. On a real email network, losses compound: when half the agents adopt such an inbox, forwarded search recovers only 5% of full adoption, against 42% for one-hop search. Third, an inbox comprises four decisions (what to read, what to keep, what a sender pays, and what a reply may say), and the best rule for each depends on the traffic and the agent's role. Multi-agent coordination under load requires an inbox layer designed for the traffic each agent receives.

papers.title: On various notions of universally Baire sets and reflection of non-Baire property in Cantor sets
papers.abstract: Universally Baire sets are a standard tool in modern set theory, where they are closely connected with forcing and absoluteness. In this paper we study universal Baireness instead as purely a regularity notion for subsets of Polish spaces. Our aim is not to develop the set-theoretic theory, but to place the notion on a systematic descriptive-set-theoretic footing and to clarify the several nonequivalent definitions that occur in the literature. A subset of a Polish space is called \emph{universally Baire} if all its continuous preimages possess the property of Baire. However, it is important to specify what the domain of these continuous functions can be. In fact, a plethora of definitions are used by various authors in the literature, the class of possible domains is sometimes the class of Polish spaces, compact metrizable spaces, all topological spaces, compact topological spaces, etc. We clarify this situation by demonstrating that the above four options are pairwise nonequivalent under the Continuum Hypothesis, we determine all the implications between these four notions that are provable in $ZFC$, and also show that all the notions used in the literature are equivalent to one of these four. Furthermore, we use Miller forcing to show that actually the cases of Polish and compact metrizable spaces are consistently equivalent. We show that numerous definitions using Borel isomorphisms, changes of topologies and Boolean algebras are all equivalent to the case of Polish domains. We present an argument that the notion using Polish domains is the natural dual to the notion of universally measurable sets. Finally, as a byproduct, we prove that the following statement is independent of $ZFC$: if a subset of a Polish space has the property of Baire relative to every nowhere dense Cantor subspace, then the subset has the property of Baire in the whole space.

papers.title: Monte Carlo Power Iteration Algorithms: Convergence, Analysis and Application to Reactor Criticality Calculations
papers.abstract: We study Monte Carlo power iteration algorithms in the context of reactor criticality simulations. Under mild conditions on the underlying physical system and the algorithmic structure, we derive explicit error bounds, which are to the best of our knowledge the first rigorous results for such methods which are ubiquitous in nuclear engineering. This is done by exploiting connections to Sequential Monte Carlo algorithms, and extending recent developments about stochastic neutron transport. We demonstrate the applicability of our results by considering a concrete version of the Monte Carlo power iteration algorithm as well as variance reduction schemes.

papers.title: Preserving rare-item recall under a storage budget: quantization, distillation, and the limits of teacher fidelity
papers.abstract: Under a fixed embedding-storage budget, recommenders can use a small full-precision model, a distilled student, or a higher-rank low-precision model. We asked which choice preserves rare-item recall and whether teacher fidelity reflects it in seven dataset-backbone cells: matrix factorization on Gowalla, Last.fm, Amazon Video Games, Steam, Goodbooks-10k and MovieLens-20M, and LightGCN on Amazon Video Games. Seven candidates fit in 168 bytes per user or item row: 40-dimensional Bayesian personalized ranking (BPR), two 40-dimensional unbiased knowledge distillation (UnKD) students, and factorizations of a 300-dimensional teacher's scores at ranks 40, 80, 155 and 300, stored in 32, 16, 8 and 4 bits. Each test set was evaluated once after fixing candidates and confirmatory analyses. The rank-300 4-bit factorization used 13% of teacher storage and retained 95-103% of its tail recall@20 and 93-97% of its NDCG@20 in every cell. The rank-40 factorization had the lowest tail recall in every cell; the 4-bit factorization had 1.2-12.7 times its tail recall and 0.99-1.46 times its NDCG. UnKD students retained 56-102% of teacher tail recall. In all ten prespecified comparisons across five prospective-expansion cells, the 4-bit factorization had higher tail recall, with simultaneous 95% intervals excluding zero. Teacher-hit retention, the share of the teacher's relevant tail hits also found by a model, ordered 23 of 147 candidate pairs differently from tail recall and identified the wrong tail-recall leader in 3 of 7 cells: models can find relevant tail items the teacher misses. In these cells, spending bytes on rank rather than precision preserved rare-item recall at 7.5 times the arithmetic per score. Compressed recommenders should be judged by total tail recall, not teacher fidelity alone.

papers.title: Towards Quantum Computation of Bulk FeO
papers.abstract: Quantum computation offers a promising path towards efficient calculations of the electronic structure of correlated materials. The properties of iron-based materials, which are key for advancing geological and astrophysical understanding, are notoriously difficult to calculate with classical computers. However, despite the many recent advances in quantum computing on near intermediate scale quantum hardware, a full treatment of the electronic structure of high-$Z$ atoms or molecules remains challenging. Here, we investigate the ground-state properties of molecular FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ model Hamiltonians using classical exact diagonalization, Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD). The experimental quintet ground state of FeO is recovered classically and with quantum algorithms, while a nonet ground state is recovered for Fe$_2$O$_2$. Although raw VQE does not achieve chemical accuracy for the ground state of FeO or Fe$_2$O$_2$, SQD with two connectivity shells recovers the exact ground energy for both molecules utilizing remarkably few quantum computational resources. Overall, our results indicate that $ab \; initio$-informed low-energy models of correlated materials, combined with SQD, offer a new alternative for scaling up calculations of ground-state properties of strongly correlated solids on existing quantum hardware.

papers.title: Cross-modal Steering Vectors Exist Across Both Image and Text Generation
papers.abstract: Are concepts and mechanisms unified across modalities in current AI models, or instead implemented separately for each one? We operationalize this broad question of modality unification by studying cross-modal steering: 1) finding vectors that successfully steer generation on tokens of one modality, which then 2) transfer zero-shot to steer generation when added to tokens of another modality. Our study goes beyond simple correlational alignment (e.g. representational similarity) because steering is fundamentally causal. We study cross-modal steering in several unified multimodal models (UMMs), since they possess shared parameters for language and image generation, focusing on these two modalities.
